Ben and Sam were brothers. They liked to play in the cabin in the woods. The cabin was old and small, but it had many toys and books. Ben and Sam had fun with the toys and books.

One day, they heard a loud noise outside. They looked out the window and saw a big truck. The truck was red and shiny. It had a bald man driving it. The bald man got out of the truck and knocked on the door.

"Hello, boys," the bald man said. "I'm sorry to delay your play, but I need to talk to your dad. He asked me to fix the roof of the cabin. It has a hole and it leaks when it rains."

Ben and Sam were curious. They wanted to see the hole and the roof. They asked the bald man if they could help him.

"Sure, you can help me," the bald man said. "But you have to be careful. The roof is high and steep. You have to wear these helmets and gloves. And you have to listen to me and do what I say."

Ben and Sam nodded. They put on the helmets and gloves. They followed the bald man to the ladder. They climbed up the ladder and saw the hole. It was big and dark. The bald man had a hammer and some nails. He showed Ben and Sam how to fix the hole with some wood and tar.

Ben and Sam helped the bald man. They held the wood and the nails. They spread the tar. They hammered the nails. They worked hard and fast. They fixed the hole.

"Good job, boys," the bald man said. "You are very brave and smart. You helped me a lot. Now the roof is good and strong. It won't leak anymore."

Ben and Sam smiled. They were proud and happy. They thanked the bald man. They climbed down the ladder. They ran to the cabin. They told their dad what they did. Their dad hugged them and praised them. He gave them some cookies and milk. They ate the cookies and drank the milk. They went back to the cabin. They played with the toys and books. They had more fun.

Tom and Mia are friends. They like to play with toys. One day, Tom brings a new toy to Mia's house. It is a magnet. A magnet can stick to some things, like metal.

Tom and Mia have fun with the magnet. They stick it to Mia's fridge, her spoon, her car, and her bell. They make loud noises and laugh. Mia's mom smiles and says, "Welcome, Tom. I'm glad you came to play."

But after a while, Tom and Mia get tired. They yawn and rub their eyes. They want to take a nap. Mia's mom says, "You can sleep in Mia's room. She has a cozy bed and a soft pillow."

Tom and Mia go to Mia's room. They bring the magnet with them. They put it on Mia's nightstand, next to her lamp. They cuddle under the blanket and close their eyes. They dream of more things to stick with the magnet. They are happy.

Lila and Tom were playing with their toys in the garden. Lila had a big doll that she liked very much. Tom had a small car that he liked very much. They were happy and shared their toys.

But then, a big dog came and saw the toys. The dog ran and grabbed the doll with its mouth. Lila was scared and cried. "No, no, that is mine! Give it back!" she shouted. Tom tried to help her and threw a stick at the dog. But the dog did not care and ran away with the doll.

Lila and Tom ran after the dog. They saw the dog go into a house. They knocked on the door. A lady opened the door. She saw the dog with the doll. She saw Lila and Tom. She was angry and ashamed.

"I'm sorry, I'm sorry, this is my dog. He is naughty and likes to carry things. He did not mean to hurt you. Here, take your doll back. And here, have a cookie. I'm very sorry," she said.

Lila and Tom took their doll and their cookie. They thanked the lady and went back to the garden. They hugged their toys and each other. They were happy again. They learned to be careful with their toys and to forgive others.

Tom was a king. He had a big crown made of gold and jewels. He liked to wear his crown and sit on his throne. He felt very important and proud.

One day, he had to go to a party with other kings and queens. He wanted to show off his crown and make them jealous. He put on his best clothes and his crown and walked to his carriage.

But on the way, he did not see a stone on the ground. He stumbled and fell. His crown flew off his head and rolled away. He hurt his knee and his nose. He cried out loud.

"Help! Help! Where is my crown?" he shouted.

A girl who was passing by heard him. She saw his crown and picked it up. She ran to him and gave it back.

"Here is your crown, sir. Are you okay?" she asked.

Tom took his crown and looked at it. It was dirty and bent. Some of the jewels were missing. He felt miserable.

"Thank you, but my crown is ruined. It is not shiny and pretty anymore. The other kings and queens will laugh at me. I don't want to go to the party anymore," he said.

The girl felt sorry for him. She smiled and said, "Don't be sad, sir. Your crown is not the most important thing. You are still a king. You have a big heart and a kind voice. You can make people happy and help them. That is what makes you a good king. The other kings and queens will like you for who you are, not for what you wear."

Tom listened to her words. He wiped his tears and smiled back. He realized she was right. He thanked her and hugged her. He put on his crown and got on his carriage. He went to the party and had fun. He made new friends and learned new things. He was happy and proud. He never forgot the girl who helped him. He always remembered to be a good king.

Sara and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big tree with a swing. Sara and Tom run to the swing. They take turns to push each other.

"Look, I can hang from the swing!" Sara says. She lets go of the rope and holds on with her hands.

"Wow, you are brave!" Tom says. He claps his hands.

Sara swings back and forth. She feels happy. She sees a bird on a branch. The bird sings a song.

"Hello, bird!" Sara says. "Do you want to play with us?"

The bird flies down and lands on Sara's shoulder. It pecks her ear gently.

"Hi, Sara!" the bird says. "You are kind. I like you."

Sara smiles. She strokes the bird's feathers.

"What is your name?" she asks.

"My name is Spirit," the bird says. "I am a magic bird. I can talk to children who are kind and have fun."

Sara and Tom are surprised. They have never met a magic bird before.

"Can we be your friends?" Tom asks.

"Of course!" Spirit says. "You are both kind and have fun. You have a good spirit. Come, let's play some more!"

Sara, Tom, and Spirit play on the swing, on the slide, and on the seesaw. They laugh and sing. They have a wonderful time. They are happy.

Tom and Anna are having lunch with Mom and Dad. They have soup and bread and cheese. Tom likes soup, but Anna does not. She makes a face and pushes her bowl away.

"Anna, you have to eat your soup. It is good for you," Mom says.

"I don't like soup. It is hot and wet and yucky," Anna says.

"Look, Anna, you can use your fork to eat the cheese. Cheese is yummy and soft and yellow," Dad says. He shows Anna how to cut the cheese with his fork.

Anna looks at Dad's fork. It is big and shiny and has four teeth. She likes Dad's fork. She reaches for it, but Dad stops her.

"No, Anna, this is my fork. You have your own fork. It is smaller and easier for you to hold," Dad says. He gives Anna her fork. It is not as big or shiny as Dad's fork. It has three teeth and a pink handle.

Anna looks at her fork. She does not like her fork. It is small and dull and has a silly color. She throws her fork on the floor and cries.

"Anna, that is not nice. You have to pick up your fork and say sorry," Mom says.

Anna does not want to pick up her fork or say sorry. She is angry and sad. She wants a big fork like Dad's. She thinks it is not fair.

Tom looks at Anna. He feels sorry for her. He likes his sister, even when she is silly. He has an idea. He picks up his fork and gives it to Anna.

"Here, Anna, you can have my fork. It is big and shiny and has four teeth, like Dad's. I don't mind. I can use my spoon to eat my soup," Tom says.

Anna looks at Tom's fork. She is surprised and happy. She takes Tom's fork and smiles.

"Thank you, Tom. You are a good brother. I am sorry I was mean," Anna says.

Mom and Dad look at Tom and Anna. They are proud and happy. They hug their children and praise them.

"That was very kind of you, Tom. You are a good sharer. And that was very nice of you, Anna. You are a good apologizer. We love you both very much," Mom and Dad say.

Tom and Anna hug Mom and Dad back. They love them too. They eat their lunch with their forks and spoons. They are a happy family.

Lily and Ben were best friends. They liked to play with their toys in the garden. One day, Lily brought a new doll. It had long hair and a pretty dress. Ben wanted to play with it.

"Can I see your doll?" Ben asked.

"OK, but be careful," Lily said. She gave him the doll.

Ben looked at the doll. He liked it very much. He wanted to keep it. He had an idea.

"Let's trade," he said. "You can have my car. It is fast and shiny."

Lily liked the car, but she loved her doll more. She shook her head.

"No, thank you. I want my doll back," she said.

Ben did not listen. He ran away with the doll. He hid it behind a bush. He thought Lily would not find it.

Lily was very sad. She wept. She looked for her doll. She could not see it.

"Ben, give me my doll. That is not nice," she cried.

Ben did not answer. He was happy with the doll. He did not care about Lily.

Lily wept louder. She wanted her doll. She wanted her friend.

A grown-up heard Lily. She came to the garden. She saw Lily weeping. She saw Ben hiding.

"What is wrong, Lily?" the grown-up asked.

"Ben took my doll. He traded it for his car. He hid it. I want my doll," Lily sobbed.

The grown-up frowned. She went to Ben. She found the doll behind the bush.

"Ben, that is not nice. You should not take Lily's doll. You should not trade without asking. You should not hide things. You should say sorry," the grown-up said.

Ben felt bad. He knew he was wrong. He gave the doll back to Lily.

"I am sorry, Lily. I was mean. Can we be friends again?" he said.

Lily smiled. She hugged her doll. She hugged Ben.

"I forgive you, Ben. We can be friends again. But next time, ask before you trade," she said.

The grown-up smiled. She was glad they made up. She gave them a cookie each.

They ate the cookies. They played with their toys. They shared and took turns. They were happy.

Tom and Sue were friends who liked to play in the big house. The big house had many rooms and doors and stairs. One day, they found a new door that was locked. They wanted to see what was inside.

"Maybe there is a treasure or a toy or a cake," Tom said.

"Or maybe there is a monster or a trap or a ghost," Sue said.

They looked for a key, but they could not find one. Then they saw a hole in the wall. It was big enough for them to crawl through.

"Let's go in and see," Tom said.

"I don't know, it looks dark and scary," Sue said.

But Tom was curious and brave, so he went in first. Sue followed him, because she did not want to be alone. They crawled through the hole and came out in a big chamber. It was dark and cold and dusty. There were many things in the chamber, but they were old and broken and dirty.

"This is not fun, this is boring," Tom said.

"Let's go back," Sue said.

But when they turned around, they saw that the hole was gone. It was covered by a big stone that fell from the ceiling. They were trapped in the chamber. They were helpless.

"Help! Help!" they shouted, but no one heard them.

They cried and hugged each other. They wished they had not gone in the chamber. They wished they had listened to Sue. They were sorry for being naughty and curious.

Then they heard a sound. It was a voice. It was coming from a small window in the wall.

"Hello, hello, are you there?" the voice said.

It was their friend Ben. He had seen them go in the hole and followed them. He had seen the stone fall and blocked the hole. He had looked for another way to get to them. He had found the window.

"Ben, Ben, we are here, we are here!" Tom and Sue said.

"Don't worry, I will help you," Ben said.

He ran to get a rope and a flashlight. He came back and threw the rope through the window. He told Tom and Sue to tie it around their waists. He pulled them out one by one. He gave them the flashlight and hugged them.

"Are you okay? Are you hurt?" he asked.

"We are okay, we are okay, thanks to you," Tom and Sue said.

They were happy and grateful. They thanked Ben for saving them. They said they were sorry for being foolish and reckless. They said they learned their lesson. They said they would never go in the chamber again. They said they would always listen to their friend.

Ben smiled and said, "You are welcome. I am glad you are safe. You are my friends. Friends help each other. Friends solve problems together. Friends are good."

The end.

Lily and Sam were playing with their trucks in the backyard. They liked to make noises and pretend they were driving on the road. Lily had a red truck and Sam had a blue truck.

"Look at my truck, it is so fast and strong!" Sam said, zooming his truck on the grass.

"My truck is faster and stronger!" Lily said, chasing Sam's truck with her own.

They raced and bumped their trucks until they reached the fence. There, they saw a big sign that said "Lemonade for sale". It was made by their neighbor, Ben, who had a table with a pitcher and some cups.

"Let's go get some lemonade, I am thirsty!" Sam said, leaving his truck by the fence.

"Me too!" Lily said, following Sam with her truck.

They ran to the table and saw Ben smiling. He had a big yellow hat and a green apron.

"Hi, Lily and Sam! Do you want some lemonade? It is only one penny a cup!" Ben said, holding a cup.

"Yes, please!" Lily and Sam said, giving Ben a penny each.

Ben poured them some lemonade and handed them the cups. Lily and Sam took a sip and made a face. The lemonade was very sour!

"Yuck! This lemonade is sour!" Lily said, spitting it out.

"Me too! It is not good!" Sam said, putting down his cup.

Ben looked sad. He had worked hard to make the lemonade, but he had put too much lemon and not enough sugar.

"I'm sorry, Lily and Sam. I wanted to make good lemonade, but I guess I made a mistake. Do you want your pennies back?" Ben said, reaching for his jar.

Lily and Sam looked at each other. They felt sorry for Ben. He was their friend and he had tried his best.

"No, Ben, it's okay. You can keep the pennies. Maybe you can try again another day." Lily said, smiling.

"Yeah, Ben, don't be sad. We still like you and your sign. It is very nice. You can display it again when you make better lemonade." Sam said, pointing at the sign.

Ben smiled back. He was glad that Lily and Sam were nice and did not get mad at him.

"Thank you, Lily and Sam. You are good friends. Do you want to play with me and my truck? I have a yellow truck that matches my hat." Ben said, showing them his truck.

"Sure, Ben, we would love to play with you and your truck. Let's go to the backyard and have some fun!" Lily said, grabbing her truck.

"Come on, Ben, let's go!" Sam said, picking up his truck.

They ran to the backyard, leaving the sour lemonade behind. They played with their trucks and had a good time. They forgot about the lemonade and were happy.

"Let's go see the boat," Ben says. "Maybe they have something fun."

"OK," Mia says. "But we have to be careful. The boat might be bad."

They swim to the boat and look at the boxes. They see words on them. They do not know what they mean. They see a hole in one box. They peek inside. They see many shiny things.

"Wow," Ben says. "These are pretty. Can we take some?"

"I don't know," Mia says. "Maybe they belong to someone."

They hear a loud voice from the boat. It is a man. He is angry.

"Hey, you kids! Get away from there! That's my supply of jewels! I stole them from the reef! They are very valuable!"

Ben and Mia are scared. They drop the shiny things and swim away. The man tries to catch them, but he is too slow. He is crazy.

Ben and Mia reach the shore. They are safe. They hug each other.

"That was scary," Ben says. "We should not go near the boat again."

"Yes," Mia says. "The boat is bad. The man is bad. The shiny things are bad. They hurt the reef and the fish."

They decide to swim in another place. They find a nice reef with many colors and shapes. They see many friendly fish. They are happy. They forget about the boat and the crazy man. They have fun.

Lily and Tom were friends who liked to play with loops. Loops were round things that you could roll, spin, or wear. They had many loops of different colors and sizes. One day, they received a big box from their aunt. Inside the box, there were many new loops that they had never seen before.

"Wow, look at these loops!" Lily said. "They are so shiny and pretty. Can we play with them?"

"Of course we can!" Tom said. "Let's see what they can do."

They opened the box and took out the loops. Some of the loops had bells, some had beads, some had ribbons, and some had lights. They tried to roll, spin, and wear the loops, but they did not work well. The bells made too much noise, the beads fell off, the ribbons got tangled, and the lights hurt their eyes.

"These loops are not fun," Lily said. "They are too different from our old loops. I want to play with our old loops."

"Me too," Tom said. "Let's put these loops back in the box and play with our old loops."

They put the new loops back in the box and went to look for their old loops. But they could not find them. They looked everywhere, but they were gone.

"Where are our old loops?" Lily asked. "Did someone take them?"

"Maybe the aunt took them," Tom said. "Maybe she wanted to trade them for the new loops."

"That's not fair!" Lily said. "We did not want to trade our old loops. We liked our old loops. They were our favorite loops."

They started to cry. They wished they had not opened the box. They wished they had not played with the new loops. They wished they had kept their old loops.

The moral of the story is: Be careful what you wish for. Sometimes, the things that seem new and exciting are not as good as the things that you already have. You should appreciate what you have and not be greedy for what you don't.

Tom and Jen like to play with their toy cars. They have a big stadium where they can race and crash their cars. They pretend they are drivers and fans and make loud noises.

One day, Tom's car breaks. The wheel falls off and the car stops. Tom is sad and angry. He throws his car on the floor and cries.

"Tom, don't cry," Jen says. "We can fix your car. I have glue and tape. Come, let's go to the table and fix it."

Tom and Jen go to the table and find the glue and tape. Jen puts some glue on the wheel and sticks it back to the car. Then she wraps some tape around it to make it stronger.

"There, your car is fixed," Jen says. "Let's go back to the stadium and race again."

Tom smiles and hugs Jen. He is happy and thankful. He picks up his car and runs to the stadium. He and Jen race and crash their cars again. They have fun and forget about the scary broken car. They are good friends.

Ben and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to swing, slide and run. But they also liked to look for bugs. They had a jar with holes in the lid. They put some grass and leaves in the jar. Then they searched for bugs to put in the jar.

"Look, Lily, I found a green bug!" Ben said. He showed Lily a small beetle with shiny green wings. "It is so pretty! Can we keep it?"

Lily nodded. She liked the green bug too. She opened the jar and Ben put the bug inside. They closed the lid and shook the jar gently. The bug crawled on the grass and leaves.

"Let's find more bugs!" Lily said. She ran to a flower bed and looked for more bugs. Ben followed her.

They found a red bug, a yellow bug, a black bug and a blue bug. They put them all in the jar. They were happy. They had a lot of bugs.

But then they heard a loud buzz. A big bee flew near them. It saw the jar with the bugs. It wanted to see the bugs too. It flew to the jar and tried to get in. It pushed the lid with its head.

"Go away, bee!" Ben said. He waved his hand at the bee. "These are our bugs! You can't have them!"

But the bee did not go away. It was angry. It stung Ben on his lip. Ben cried out. His lip hurt. It was red and swollen.

Lily saw Ben's lip. She felt sorry for him. She hugged him. She said, "I'm sorry, Ben. The bee was mean. Let's go to mom. She will make your lip better."

Ben nodded. He held Lily's hand. They took the jar with the bugs. They ran to their mom. She was sitting on a bench. She saw Ben's lip. She said, "Oh, Ben, what happened? Did a bee sting you?"

Ben nodded. He said, "Yes, mom. The bee wanted our bugs. We found a lot of bugs. Look, mom, we have a green bug!"

Mom smiled. She said, "You have a lot of bugs. They are very pretty. But you have to be careful with bees. They can sting you. Let me see your lip."

Mom took a tissue and put some ice on Ben's lip. She said, "This will make your lip feel better. It will go down soon. Don't worry."

Ben felt better. He said, "Thank you, mom. You are the best."

Mom said, "You're welcome, Ben. You are very brave. Now, why don't you and Lily settle on the grass and watch your bugs? Maybe they will do something funny."

Ben and Lily settled on the grass. They watched their bugs. They saw the green bug fly, the red bug crawl, the yellow bug jump, the black bug hide and the blue bug shine. They laughed. They were happy. They forgot about the bee. They had fun with their bugs.

Anna liked to wake up early and watch the sunrise. She liked how the sky changed colors and how the birds sang. She liked to sit on the window and feel the warm sun on her face. But she was lonely. She wished she had someone to share the sunrise with.

One day, she saw a boy walking on the street. He had a big backpack and a funny hat. He looked up and saw Anna on the window. He smiled and waved at her. Anna smiled and waved back. She felt happy. She wanted to talk to him.

She ran to the door and opened it. She called out to the boy. "Hi! What is your name? Do you want to see the sunrise with me?"

The boy stopped and looked at her. He said, "Hi! My name is Ben. I am going to school. I like the sunrise, but I have to mind the time. I don't want to be late."

Anna felt sad. She said, "Oh. I don't go to school. I stay at home with my mom. She is sick and needs me. I don't have any friends. I am lonely."

Ben felt sorry for her. He said, "I am sorry. That is hard. I have an idea. Why don't you come with me to school? You can meet my friends and learn new things. Maybe you will like it. And you can still see the sunrise on the way."

Anna liked the idea. She said, "Yes, please. That sounds fun. Thank you, Ben. You are very kind. Can I bring my mom?"

Ben said, "Of course. She can come too. Maybe she will feel better. Come on, let's go. The sunrise is waiting for us."

Anna and Ben held hands and walked to school. They saw the sunrise together. They saw the sky change colors and heard the birds sing. They felt the warm sun on their faces. They were not lonely anymore. They were happy. They had found a friend.

Lily and Ben were excited to go to the lake with their dad. They liked to swim, splash and play with the fish. They also liked to find logs and sticks to make boats and rafts.

"Look, dad, I found a big log!" Ben shouted, dragging a long piece of wood to the shore. "Can we make a boat with it?"

"Sure, Ben, that's a great log for a boat. Let's see if we can find some rope and a sail," dad said, smiling.

Lily ran to help Ben with the log. She saw a blue towel and a stick nearby. "I have an idea, Ben. We can use this towel as a sail and this stick as a mast. Then we can tie them to the log with this rope," she said, holding up the items.

"Wow, Lily, you are very smart. That's a good idea. Let's do it," Ben said, nodding.

They worked together to make the boat. They tied the rope around the log and the stick. They attached the towel to the stick with some knots. They made sure the boat was strong and stable.

"Are you ready, Ben?" Lily asked, holding the boat.

"Yes, I'm ready, Lily. Let's send our boat to the water," Ben said, grabbing the other end of the boat.

They lifted the boat and carried it to the edge of the lake. They counted to three and pushed the boat into the water. The boat floated and the wind blew the sail.

"Look, dad, look! Our boat is sailing!" Lily and Ben shouted, jumping and clapping.

"Wow, you two, you made a wonderful boat. I'm very proud of you. Let's watch it go," dad said, hugging them.

Sara likes to read books. She has many books in her room. She reads them every day. She reads about animals, and cars, and stars.

One day, Sara finds a new book in her room. It is a big book with a shiny cover. She opens it and sees many pictures. She sees a picture of a chain. A chain is a long thing with many round parts. She reads the words under the picture. The words say: "A chain can be used to pull, to lock, or to make noise."

Sara wants to try the chain. She looks around her room. She sees her toy box. She sees a lock on her toy box. She thinks: "Maybe I can use the chain to open the lock." She takes the chain and puts it around the lock. She pulls the chain hard. The lock does not open. She pulls harder. The lock still does not open. She pulls harder and harder. The chain breaks. The lock falls to the floor. Sara is sad. She says: "Oh no, I broke the chain. Now I can't read the book anymore."

Sara hears a noise. She turns around. She sees her mom. Her mom is smiling. She says: "Sara, what are you doing? I brought you a new book. It is a book about chains. I thought you would like it." Sara is surprised. She says: "Mom, this is the book I was reading. I found it in my room. I tried to use the chain to open the lock, but I broke the chain. I'm sorry, mom." Her mom hugs her. Tim and Sam were shocked and angry. They felt cheated and lied to. They said, "No, thank you. We don't want your fish. You are not smart and rich. You are sneaky and bad. We will catch our own fish with our pole. Goodbye!"

They ran back to their pole and bucket. They hoped to catch a big fish and show the man. They learned a lesson that day. They learned that not everyone is honest and that fishing is hard work. The mule does not answer. He looks at Tom and Sue with big eyes. He is shy.

The mule does not like that. He kicks his legs and makes a loud noise. He runs away from Sue. He is scared.

"Ouch!" Sue says. She falls on the ground. She hurts her knee. She cries.

Tom runs to Sue. He helps her get up. He hugs her. He is sorry.

"Don't cry, Sue," Tom says. "The mule did not mean to hurt you. He is new here. He does not know us. He needs time to be our friend."

Sue stops crying. She nods. She understands.

Sue smiles. She agrees.

The mule sees the food. He smells it. He is hungry. He walks to the food. He eats it. He likes it.

Tom and Sue watch the mule. They are happy. They see the mule's ears move. They see his tail wag. They see his eyes glow. He is happy too.

"Look, Sue," Tom says. "The mule is glowing. He likes us. He is not shy anymore."

"Look, Mia, I can drive!" Ben says. He turns the key in the ignition. The car starts to move. It goes forward and backward. It bumps into the wall and the shelves. It makes noises like crash, bang, screech.

"Stop, Ben, stop!" Mia says. She is scared. She wants to get out. But the door is locked. She cries and screams. She pushes the horn. It makes a loud noise like honk, honk, honk.

Dad hears the noise. He runs to the garage. He sees the car moving and shaking. He sees Ben and Mia inside. He is angry and worried. He opens the door and takes them out. He hugs them and checks if they are hurt. He is glad they are okay. He scolds them and tells them to never play with his car again. He says it is dangerous and not a toy. He says they could have broken the car or hurt themselves or others.

Ben and Mia are sorry. They say they are sorry to dad and to the car. They promise to never do it again. They learn that they should not touch things that are not theirs. They learn that they should listen to dad and be careful. They learn that driving is not a game. They go back to their toy cars. They drive them safely and happily. They make noises like vroom, beep, honk.

Anna and Ben were at the park with their mom. They liked to play on the swings, the slide and the sandbox. They saw many other kids and some dogs too. They waved to their friends and said hello.

"Mom, can we have ice-cream?" Anna asked. She loved ice-cream, especially chocolate and vanilla. Ben nodded. He liked ice-cream too, but he preferred strawberry and banana.

"Sure, sweeties. Let's go to the ice-cream truck," mom said. She took their hands and walked with them to the truck. There were many flavors and colors of ice-cream. Anna and Ben chose their favorites and mom paid the man.

"Thank you, mom!" Anna and Ben said. They licked their ice-creams and smiled. They were very yummy and cold.

As they were eating their ice-creams, they saw a little girl with a big hat and a pink dress. She was holding a balloon and a teddy bear. She looked very adorable. She waved to Anna and Ben and came closer.

"Hi, I'm Lily. Do you want to play with me?" she asked. She had a friendly voice and a cute smile.

"Hi, I'm Anna and this is Ben. We would love to play with you," Anna said. She liked Lily's hat and balloon. Ben liked her teddy bear.

"Great! Let's go to the sandbox. I have some toys there," Lily said. She led them to the sandbox and they started to make sandcastles, bridges and tunnels. They had a lot of fun and shared their toys and ice-creams.

Anna, Ben and Lily became good friends. They played until it was time to go home. They hugged and waved goodbye. They promised to see each other again soon. They were very happy.

Lila and Tom were best friends. They liked to play in the park with their toys. One day, they saw some big kids coming. The big kids looked mean and angry. They wanted to take Lila and Tom's toys.

"Give us your toys, or we will hurt you!" one of the big kids shouted.

Lila and Tom were scared. They did not want to lose their toys. They did not want to get hurt. They hugged each other and held their toys tight.

"No, these are our toys! Go away!" Tom said.

The big kids laughed. They moved closer to Lila and Tom. They reached out their hands to grab the toys.

"Stop! Leave them alone!" a voice said.

Lila and Tom looked up. They saw Sam, their older brother. Sam was strong and brave. He came to the park to protect them. He stood in front of Lila and Tom and faced the big kids.

"These are my sister and brother. You cannot take their toys. You cannot hurt them. Go away, or I will make you go away!" Sam said.

The big kids did not laugh anymore. They saw that Sam was stronger than them. They did not want to fight him. They did not want to start a war. They turned around and ran away.

Lila and Tom were happy. They thanked Sam for saving them. They gave him a hug and a kiss.

"You are the best brother ever!" Lila said.

"You are our hero!" Tom said.

Sam smiled. He hugged them back. He was glad he could protect them.

"Let's go home and have some cookies," Sam said.

Lila and Tom nodded. They picked up their toys and followed Sam. They felt safe and loved. They were a happy family.

But then, the net starts to shake. It is not because of Tom and Mia. It is because of a big dog. The dog is chasing a ball. The ball rolls under the net. The dog follows the ball. The dog jumps on the net.

Tom and Mia are scared. The net is not strong enough for the dog. The net makes a loud noise. It breaks. Tom and Mia fall to the ground. They are not hurt. They are just dirty and sad. The dog runs away with the ball.

Tom and Mia look at the broken net. They are sorry. They did not mean to break the equipment. They go to find the park keeper. They want to tell him what happened. They hope he can fix the net. They want to test it again.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to slide, swing and run. But they did not like the big tree. The big tree had a hole in its trunk. It looked like a mouth. Tom and Lily thought the big tree was scary.

One day, Tom had an idea. He wanted to scare Lily. He said, "Lily, let's play hide and seek. You count to ten and I hide." Lily agreed. She closed her eyes and counted. Tom ran to the big tree. He climbed inside the hole. He thought, "This will be fun. Lily will be so scared when I jump out."

Lily finished counting. She opened her eyes and looked for Tom. She saw his shoes sticking out of the hole. She smiled. She knew where he was. She tiptoed to the big tree. She said, "I found you, Tom. You are in the big tree." She reached for his shoes. But then, something happened.

Tom heard a loud noise. He felt something move in the hole. He looked up. He saw a big, furry head. It had sharp teeth and yellow eyes. It was a raccoon. The raccoon was angry. It did not like Tom in its home. It growled and hissed. Tom was terrified. He screamed and ran out of the hole.

Lily saw Tom run out of the hole. She saw the raccoon chase him. She was shocked. She did not know there was a raccoon in the big tree. She said, "Tom, watch out! There is a raccoon!" She ran after him. They both ran to the other side of the park. They did not stop until they were safe.

Tom and Lily hugged each other. They were glad they were okay. They looked at the big tree. They did not like it anymore. They said, "Let's never play near the big tree again. It is too scary." They decided to play somewhere else. They found a sandbox. They thought it was fun. They forgot about the big tree and the raccoon. They did not try to scare each other again. They learned their lesson.

Once upon a time, there was a sleepy bunny named Ben. Ben lived in a big forest with many trees and vines. One day, Ben saw a tasty vine hanging from a tree. He wanted to eat it, but it was too high for him to reach.

Together, they went to the tree with the vine. Tim lifted Ben up, and Ben got the vine. After that, Ben helped Tim find the best leaves to eat. They both shared their food and were very happy.

The moral of the story is that when we help each other, we can solve our problems and make everyone happy.

Suddenly, an ant came to the giant and said, "I know a way to help. If you use your gentle hands, you can spread some dirt around the edges and the hole will be big enough to fit again."

The giant listened to the ant, and he carefully spread the dirt around the edges. Sure enough, the hole grew and the animals were able to get back inside.

The giant was so relieved, and he thanked the ant for the clever suggestion. From then on, he was extra careful with his toys and never made the hole shrink again.

Tom did not understand. He asked his mom where his dad was. He missed his dad. He had not seen him for many days. He wanted to hug him and hear his voice. But his mom said nothing. She just hugged him and cried.

They went to the big place. It was a church. There were many people. They were all dressed in black. They looked sad and quiet. Tom did not know them. He felt lonely and scared. He held his mom's hand.

They walked to the front of the church. There was a big box. It was covered with flowers. Tom saw a picture of his dad on the box. He remembered his dad. He loved his dad. He wanted to see his dad. He ran to the box. He tried to open it. He shouted, "Dad, dad, where are you?"

But the box did not open. The people gasped. The mom screamed. The priest stopped. Tom cried. He did not know. He did not know that his dad was gone. He did not know that it was his dad's funeral. He did not know that he would never see his dad again.

"That pipe is not for kids, Sam. It is bad for your teeth and your lungs. You don't want to be sick, do you?" his dad said.

"No, dad. I don't want to be sick. I want to be strong and healthy like you," Sam said.

"Good, Sam. Then let's jog some more and have a delicious breakfast when we get home. How about some eggs and toast and fruit?" his dad said.

"Yum, dad. That sounds delicious. I love eggs and toast and fruit," Sam said.

They jogged some more and left the park. They did not see the man with the pipe again. But they did not know that the man had dropped his pipe on the ground and that a dog had found it and chewed it. The dog did not like the pipe. It made him cough and sneeze and spit. The dog ran away and left the pipe on the grass. The next day, a bird saw the pipe and thought it was a worm. Tom was an adventurous boy who liked to explore new places. One day, he saw a big hill behind his house that he had never climbed before. He put on his jacket and his boots and told his mom he was going out to play.

"Be careful, Tom," his mom said. "Don't go too far and come back before it gets dark."

Tom nodded and ran outside. He followed a path that led to the hill. He saw many things on his way: flowers, birds, rocks, and bugs. He stopped to look at them and sometimes picked them up. He was having a lot of fun.

When he reached the top of the hill, he saw something that made him curious. It was a big hole in the ground, like a cave. He wondered what was inside. He decided to peek in and see.

He walked slowly to the hole and bent down. He could not see much, only darkness and shadows. He heard a strange noise, like a growl. He felt scared, but he wanted to know more. He moved closer and closer, until he was almost inside the hole.

Suddenly, a furry head popped out of the hole. It had big ears, sharp teeth, and angry eyes. It was a fox! The fox saw Tom and snarled. Tom screamed and jumped back. He turned around and ran as fast as he could. He did not stop until he reached his house.

He burst through the door and hugged his mom. He told her what he had seen and how he had escaped. His mom was glad he was safe, but also a little angry.

"Tom, you should not have gone near that hole. It was dangerous. You could have been hurt by the fox. You were very lucky."

Tom nodded and said he was sorry. He realized he had been too adventurous and had not listened to his mom. He learned his lesson and decided to be more careful next time. He still liked to explore, but he never peeked into holes again.

They reached the top of the tree and began to pick the nuts. They were so happy and busy that they did not notice a wild cat sneaking up on them. The cat saw the squirrels and licked its lips. It jumped on the tree and tried to catch them.

"Help! Help!" Tim and Tom shouted. "There is a wild cat!"

They dropped their nuts and ran down the tree. The cat followed them, but it was not good at climbing. It slipped and fell to the ground. It hurt its paw and ran away.

Tim and Tom were safe, but they had lost their nuts. They felt sad and hungry. They looked around and saw a group of children playing in the park. The children had a basket of nuts that they had brought for a picnic. They saw the squirrels and smiled.

"Hello, squirrels!" one of the children said. "Do you want some nuts?"

The children threw some nuts to Tim and Tom. The squirrels were surprised and happy. They ate the nuts and thanked the children.

"Thank you, children!" Tim and Tom said. "You are very kind and generous!"

The children were happy too. They liked to share and make friends. They clapped their hands and applauded the squirrels.

"Yay, squirrels!" the children said. "You are very brave and smart!"

Tim and Tom learned a lesson that day. They learned that nuts are good, but friends are better. They learned that sharing is caring, and that kindness is rewarded. They learned that wild cats are bad, but children are good. They learned to applaud the good and avoid the bad.

Chris and Eric had so much fun that they couldn't believe how quickly the day went by. They said, "Let's do this every day!"

"I fell and my knee hurts," Timmy said.

"Don't worry, I will put a bandage on it and it will heal soon," his mom said.

Timmy felt better and went back to playing. Later, his friend came over and said, "Let's play hide and seek."

Timmy said, "Okay, but let's wait until noon. It's too hot right now."

His friend agreed and they played until it was time to go home. Timmy was happy that his knee was healing and that he had a fun day with his friend. He went to bed with a smile on his face, knowing that tomorrow would be another great day.

Once upon a time, there was a little fish named Nemo. Nemo loved to swim in the deep blue sea with his friends. One day, Nemo and his friends were playing a game of tag when suddenly, Nemo saw a shiny pearl at the bottom of the sea. 

Excitedly, Nemo swam down to get the pearl, but as he got deeper and deeper, the silence around him grew stronger. Suddenly, Nemo heard a big voice say, "Who goes there?" It was a big, scary octopus! 

Nemo was scared, but he knew he had to be brave. He said, "It's just me, Nemo. I saw a pearl and wanted to dive down to get it." The octopus laughed and said, "Well, you're a brave little fish. Take the pearl and go play with your friends." Nemo quickly grabbed the pearl and swam away as fast as he could. He was happy to be back with his friends and told them all about his adventure.

"I know, but if you pick it, it won't look so pretty anymore," said Dad.

Mommy said, "I know you love your skirt, but we need to add soap and water to make it clean and fresh again."

Lily learned that sometimes we need to add something to make things better. And from that day on, she made sure to take care of her favorite skirt so it wouldn't get smelly again. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a frog named Freddy. Freddy lived in a pond with his friends. One day, Freddy saw a beautiful frog named Lily. He asked her, "Will you marry me?" Lily said, "Yes!"

Freddy was so happy, but his friends were miserable. They didn't like Lily because she was different from them. They said, "We don't want you to marry her, Freddy." But Freddy loved Lily and didn't listen to his friends.

Finally, Freddy and Lily got married by the pond. All of their friends came to the wedding and saw how happy Freddy was with Lily. They realized that being different was okay and they all became friends again. Freddy and Lily lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in the park. One day, he saw a pigeon flying in the sky. The pigeon looked so free and happy, and Timmy wanted to be just like the pigeon.

Suddenly, Timmy heard a loud noise. It was a group of big, mean bullies. They wanted to take Timmy's toy truck away. Timmy was scared and didn't know what to do. But then, he remembered the pigeon he saw earlier. The pigeon surrendered to the sky and flew away. Timmy decided to surrender his toy truck to the bullies and run away.

As Timmy was running away, he saw a kind old lady sitting on a bench. She noticed that Timmy looked sad and asked him what was wrong. Timmy told her about the bullies and how he surrendered his toy truck. The old lady smiled and said, "You did the right thing, Timmy. It's always better to be kind and surrender something small than to fight and get hurt."

From that day on, Timmy learned to be like the pigeon and surrender when things got tough. And he also made a new friend in the kind old lady at the park. Plus, he got a new toy truck from his mom, so he didn't even miss the one he surrendered. And it was a good thing too, because it was a hot summer day and Timmy wanted to play with his new truck in the cool shade.

When he reached the edge of the forest, the frog saw a big, scary bear. The frog jumped in surprise and tried to run away. But the bear was too fast and caught the frog in its claws.

The bear growled and said, "I'm gonna eat you for dinner!"

The frog was so scared he couldn't move. After a few seconds, it was all over. The pretty frog was never seen again.

The story of the brave little frog, who ventured into the unknown despite his worries, ended with a bad ending. But it only goes to show that no matter how curious you are, sometimes things don't turn out the way you expect.

Lily and her friends were very happy and thanked Mr. Smith. They continued playing hide and seek with the light from the flashlight.

Mr. Smith saw that Lily was upset and said, "Don't worry, I have another flashlight at home. I'll go get it for you." 

Lily and her friends were relieved and grateful that Mr. Smith could provide them with more light. They continued playing and had a great time. The end.

One day, a big fish named Bubbles saw Finny and said, "Finny, why do you always repeat swimming in circles?" Finny replied, "I like it. It's fun and makes me special." Bubbles thought for a moment then said, "Can I try too?" Finny smiled and said, "Of course, Bubbles!"

Bubbles tried to swim in circles like Finny, but he was not very good at it. He got dizzy and bumped into a big rock. Bubbles got hurt and started to cry. Finny felt bad and tried to help Bubbles. But it was too late. Bubbles had to go away and live in another harbor. All the other fish were sad and missed Bubbles. They learned that not everyone can be unique like Finny, and sometimes trying new things can have a bad ending.

The creature asked Lily to give the veil back. Lily didn't want to, but she was scared of the creature. So, she gave it back. The creature put the veil on and said, "Thank you. Now, you can't see me anymore." And just like that, the creature disappeared.

Ben and Lily were playing in the garden. They liked to dig in the dirt and look for bugs and worms. They had a big bucket to put their finds in.

"Look, Lily, I found a huge root!" Ben said, holding up a long, brown thing. "It's bigger than my arm!"

"Wow, Ben, that's amazing!" Lily said, admiring the root. "Can I see it?"

Ben nodded and handed the root to Lily. She felt how hard and rough it was. She wondered what kind of plant it came from.

Suddenly, they heard a loud yell from the house. It was their mom.

"Ben! Lily! Come here right now!" she shouted. "You made a big mess in the garden!"

Ben and Lily dropped the root and ran to the house. They saw their mom standing on the porch, looking angry. She pointed to the garden, where they had dug up many holes and piles of dirt.

"What were you doing?" she asked. "You ruined the flowers and the vegetables!"

Ben and Lily felt sorry. They didn't mean to hurt the plants. They just wanted to have fun.

"We were looking for bugs and worms, mom," Ben said. "We found a huge root. See?" He showed her the root.

"That's not a root, Ben," mom said. "That's a carrot. You pulled out one of our carrots. And you wasted it. Carrots are food, not toys."

Ben and Lily looked at the root. They realized it was a carrot. They felt silly. They didn't know carrots grew in the ground.

"We're sorry, mom," Lily said. "We didn't know. We won't do it again."

Mom sighed. She was still mad, but she also loved her children. She knew they were curious and didn't mean any harm.

"It's okay, Lily," she said. "But you have to be more careful in the garden. The plants are living things, too. They need water and sun and space to grow. And some of them are for us to eat. You can look for bugs and worms, but don't dig up the plants. Okay?"

"Okay, mom," Ben and Lily said. They hugged their mom and said they were sorry again. Mom hugged them back and smiled.

"Come on, let's go inside and wash up," she said. "Then we can have some carrot cake for snack. How does that sound?"

Ben and Lily smiled. They liked carrot cake. They followed their mom inside, leaving the huge root behind.

"Come back, bird! I want to be your friend!" Leo shouted.

But the bird did not come back. Leo felt sad and lonely. He wished he had a friend who liked his roar.

"Hello, lion. What are you doing?" the monkey asked.

The monkey nodded. "Yes, I like your roar. It sounds strong and brave. Can I hear it again?"

Leo smiled and roared as loud as he could. The monkey clapped his hands and cheered.

"Wow, that was a great roar! You are a hero, lion!" the monkey said.

Leo felt happy and proud. He had found a friend who liked his roar.

"Thank you, monkey. You are very patient and kind. Do you want to play with me?" Leo asked.

The monkey nodded again. "Yes, I want to play with you. You are fun and friendly. What do you want to play?"

Leo thought for a moment. Then he had an idea.

"Let's play hide and seek. I will count to ten and you hide. Then I will find you with my roar. OK?"

The monkey agreed. He ran to find a hiding spot. Leo closed his eyes and counted to ten. Then he opened his eyes and roared.

"Ready or not, here I come!" he said.

"Wow, Anna!" Tom whispered back. "We discovered a treasure! It's so pretty and sparkly!"

They wanted to touch the dragon and the treasure, but they were also afraid. They decided to leave a gift for the dragon, to show they were friendly. They picked some flowers and berries and put them near the cave. Then they ran back to the park, happy and proud.

They told their mom and dad what they discovered. Their mom and dad smiled and hugged them. They said they were very brave and clever. They said they had a wonderful imagination. They said they loved them very much.

Bunny was a famous hopper. He could hop very high and very far. He liked to hop all over the forest and show off his skills. He made many friends with the other animals, who cheered for him and gave him carrots.

One day, Bunny saw a hut in a clearing. He had never seen a hut before. He was curious and wanted to hop inside. He hopped closer and closer, until he reached the door. He knocked with his paw, but no one answered. He pushed the door and it opened.

Bunny hopped inside the hut. It was dark and dusty. He saw a big bed, a table, a chair, and a cupboard. He also saw a basket full of food. He smelled honey and bread and cheese. He was hungry and wanted to taste them.

He hopped to the basket and took a bite of the cheese. It was yummy. He took another bite, and another. He did not hear the footsteps outside. He did not see the shadow on the wall. He did not notice the big bad wolf who lived in the hut.

The wolf came in and saw Bunny eating his cheese. He was angry and hungry. He roared and showed his teeth. He wanted to eat Bunny for his lunch. Bunny was scared and sorry. He dropped the cheese and tried to hop away. But the wolf was faster and blocked the door.

Bunny was trapped. He wished he had not hopped inside the hut. He wished he had stayed with his friends in the forest. He wished he had listened to his mother, who told him not to go near the hut. He closed his eyes and waited for the end.

But then, he heard a loud noise. He opened his eyes and saw a big axe. It smashed the door and made a hole. He saw a man with a beard and a hat. He was a woodcutter, who worked in the forest. He saw the wolf and the bunny. He was brave and strong. He swung his axe and hit the wolf. The wolf howled and ran away.

Bunny was saved. He was happy and grateful. He thanked the woodcutter, who smiled and patted his head. He gave him some honey and bread and told him to go back to his friends. He warned him not to hop inside strange huts again. He said goodbye and left.

Bunny hopped out of the hut. He felt lucky and learned a lesson. He decided to be more careful and not to be too curious. He hopped back to the forest and found his friends. He told them what happened and they hugged him and gave him carrots. He was still a famous hopper, but he was also a wiser bunny.

"Help! Help!" Sam shouted. Ben heard him and climbed into the tunnel. He saw Sam's hand bleeding and the spike holding it. He was scared, but he wanted to help his brother.

"Sam, don't move!" Ben said. He grabbed Sam's hand and gave it a hard shake. The spike came loose and Sam's hand was free. Sam hugged Ben and thanked him.

"Let's go home, Sam," Ben said. "We need to put a bandage on your hand."

"OK, Ben," Sam said. "You're not weak, you're brave."

Mommy said, "Sure, but be careful. You can pet him, but don't lead him away from his owner."

Lily went up to the dog and petted him. But after a few minutes, she started to itch. She said, "Mommy, my arm itches. Maybe the dog has fleas." 

Mommy said, "Let's go wash your hands and put some cream on it. We don't want you to be uncomfortable." 

Lily and her mommy walked away from the dog, and Lily said, "That was fun! I like petting dogs, but I don't like the itch."

Lily was happy to help her mom, and together they watered the plants. "We make a great team," Lily said. "Yes, we do," her mom replied with a smile.

"Hey Johnny, do you want to play catch?" asked Timmy.

"Sure, but let's be careful not to split the ball," replied Johnny.

Timmy didn't know what "split" meant, so he asked Johnny. Johnny explained that it meant to break something into two pieces. 

"Oh, I understand now," said Timmy. 

They played catch for a while, but then Timmy accidentally threw the ball too hard and it split into two pieces. 

"Oh no, I'm sorry Johnny. I didn't mean to split the ball," said Timmy.

"That's okay, Timmy. We can still play with the pieces," replied Johnny with a smile. 

And so, they continued to play with the broken ball, and Timmy learned a new word that day.

The bear and the rabbit learned that it's important to be patient and wait for help instead of trying to remove obstacles on their own. They also learned that it's important to listen to each other's ideas and work together as a team. From that day on, they always remembered to be safe and patient on their adventures.

One day, the pirate saw a big storm coming. He knew he had to be careful, so he tied everything down and put on his raincoat. The wind started to rock the ship back and forth, but the pirate was brave. 

After the storm, the pirate saw that his ship was okay. He was happy and sang a song about the storm. The parrot rocked his head back and forth and squawked along. The pirate realized that even though things can be scary sometimes, it's important to be brave and stay safe.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved ice cream, especially the creamy one. One day, she asked her mom to buy her some ice cream. Her mom said, "Sure, but hurry back before dinner." 

Lily ran to the ice cream truck and got her favorite flavor. She ate it slowly, savoring every bite. But then she realized she was running late. She ran back home, but her mom was already angry. She said, "You're late! Now we have to hurry to eat dinner." 

Lily was frustrated because she didn't want to rush through dinner. She wanted to enjoy her food. But her mom made her eat quickly. After dinner, Lily felt sick. She had eaten too fast. Her mom scolded her and said, "Next time, don't take so long with your ice cream." 

Lily felt sad and regretful. She wished she had listened to her mom and hurried back home. From that day on, she learned to be more responsible and not take too long with her treats.

Lily realized that she needed to talk to Rose and Daisy and tell them how she felt. When she did, they apologized and invited her to play with them. Once upon a time, there was a little fish named Nemo. Nemo loved to swim in the big blue ocean. One day, Nemo saw a plastic bag in the water. "Oh no! That's waste!" Nemo said. "We must tell our friends to be careful of waste."

Nemo and his friends swam to the other side of the ocean to warn their friends. "Hey, friends! We saw waste in the water! We need to be careful!" Nemo said. 

One of Nemo's friends, Sammy, asked, "What is waste?" Nemo explained, "Waste is when we throw things away that we don't need anymore. It can hurt us and our home." 

Suddenly, they saw a spoiled apple floating in the water. "Ew, that looks gross!" Sammy said. "We should pick it up and put it in the trash." Nemo and his friends worked together to clean up the waste and keep their home safe.

One day, their parents had to go away for work, and they left Tom and Lily with their nanny, Mrs. Lee. Mrs. Lee was kind and patient, but she had rules. They threw their food on the floor, hid their toothbrushes, and fought over their toys.

Mrs. Lee was very sad and tired. She decided to rest on the couch for a while. She closed her eyes and fell asleep. Tom and Lily saw this and thought it was funny. They decided to play a prank on Mrs. Lee. They went to the kitchen and opened the freezer. They took out a big ice cream cake and carried it to the living room. They put the cake on Mrs. Lee's face and laughed.

But the cake was very cold and wet. It melted on Mrs. Lee's face and clothes and couch. It made a big mess. Mrs. Lee woke up and felt the cake. She was very angry and shocked. She screamed and cried. Tom and Lily were scared. They realized they had done a bad thing. They ran to their room and hid under their bed.

Mrs. Lee called their parents and told them what happened. Their parents were very disappointed and sorry. They came back home and scolded Tom and Lily. They made them clean up the mess and apologize to Mrs. Lee. They also took away their toys and books and clothes for a week. They told them to learn to be grateful and respectful and kind.

Tom and Lily felt very sorry and ashamed. They hugged Mrs. Lee and said they were sorry. They hugged their parents and said they loved them. They learned their lesson and promised to be better. They realized that being wealthy was not enough. They needed to be happy and good.

Sara and Ben were playing in the snow. They made a big snowman with a hat and a carrot nose. They were very happy.

But then, a big boy came. He was mean and rude. He said, "This is my snowman. Go away!" He pushed Sara and Ben and made them fall.

Sara and Ben were sad and scared. They did not want to fight. They said, "Please, don't be mean. We can share the snowman. It is big enough for all of us."

But the big boy did not listen. He said, "No, it is mine. I will make it bigger and better." He took some powder from his pocket and threw it on the snowman. He said, "This is magic powder. It will make the snowman grow and obey me."

But the powder was not magic. It was pepper. The snowman sneezed and sneezed. The hat and the carrot nose flew away. The snowman fell apart. The big boy was covered in snow and pepper. He cried and ran away.

Sara and Ben felt sorry for the big boy. They said, "He was not fit to play with us. He was selfish and rude. He did not know how to share and be kind."

They decided to make a new snowman. They used the hat and the carrot nose that they found. They also found a scarf and some buttons. They made the snowman smile. They said, "This is our snowman. He is happy and friendly. He likes to share and be kind."

They played with the snowman until it was time to go home. They said, "Goodbye, snowman. We will come back tomorrow. We hope you will not melt."

The moral of the story is: Sharing and kindness are better than selfishness and rudeness.

Tom watched Lily from the ground. He was worried. He said, "Lily, come down. It is not safe. You can hurt yourself." But Lily did not hear Tom. She was too busy climbing the tree. She was happy and proud. She said, "Look, Tom, I am on the top of the tree. I can see everything. I am the best climber."

But then, something bad happened. Lily saw a shiny thing on a branch. She reached for it. It was a needle. Someone had left it on the tree. Lily did not know what a needle was. She thought it was a toy. She touched the needle with her hand. It was sharp and it poked her. It made her bleed and it hurt a lot.

Lily screamed and let go of the branch. She fell from the tree. She hit the ground hard. She was hurt and she cried. Tom ran to her and hugged her. He said, "Lily, I am sorry. You are hurt. I will get help." He called for a grown-up. A grown-up came and took Lily to the doctor. The doctor gave her a band-aid and a hug. He said, "Lily, you are brave. But you should not climb the tree. It is dangerous. You should listen to your friend. He cares about you."

Lily was sad and sorry. She said, "I am sorry, Tom. You were right. I should not have climbed the tree. I was silly and mean. You are a good friend. Can you forgive me?" Tom said, "I forgive you, Lily. You are my friend. But please, do not climb the tree again. It is not worth it." Lily said, "I promise, Tom. I will not climb the tree again. I will play with you on the ground. It is safer and more fun." They hugged and smiled. But Lily's hand still hurt and she had a scar. She learned a hard lesson. Climbing the tree was a bad idea.

Lily and Ben were playing with their toys in the living room. They liked to make up stories with their dolls and cars. Lily had a big box of photos that her mom gave her. She liked to look at them and see the faces of her family and friends.

"Look, Ben, this is a photo of me and you when we were babies," Lily said, holding up a picture. "We were so small and cute. Do you remember?"

Ben shook his head. He did not remember being a baby. He only remembered being a big boy who could run and jump and talk.

"Mom says we were very lively babies. We liked to laugh and play and make noise. We still do, right?" Lily asked.

Ben nodded. He liked to laugh and play and make noise with Lily. They were best friends.

"Who is this?" Ben asked, pointing to another photo. It showed a man with a big smile and a hat. He was holding Lily in his arms.

"That's my dad. He lives far away now. He works on a big boat. He sends me letters and stickers sometimes. I miss him a lot," Lily said, feeling sad.

Ben hugged Lily. He knew how it felt to miss someone. His dad also lived far away. He worked on a big plane. He also sent him letters and stickers sometimes.

"Maybe our dads will come back soon. Maybe they will play with us and take us to the park. That would be fun, right?" Ben said, trying to cheer Lily up.

Lily smiled. She hoped Ben was right. She loved her dad and wanted to see him again.

"Maybe they will. And maybe they will take a photo of us together. Then we can put it in the box and look at it when we miss them. That would remind us of them, right?" Lily said.

Ben agreed. He liked that idea. He liked photos. They reminded him of happy times. He and Lily decided to make a card for their dads. They used crayons and stickers and wrote "We love you" on it. They put the card in an envelope and asked their mom to mail it. They hoped their dads would like it. They hoped their dads would come back soon. They hoped they would be a happy family again.

Lily liked to touch things. She liked to touch soft things, like her teddy bear and her blanket. She liked to touch hard things, like her blocks and her spoon. She liked to touch warm things, like her mom and her soup. She liked to touch cold things, like her ice cream and her snowman.

But Lily did not like to touch sour things. Sour things made her face scrunch up and her tongue sting. She did not like lemons, or vinegar, or pickles. She did not like sour things at all.

One Sunday, Lily went to the park with her dad. She saw a big tree with yellow fruits. She wondered what they were. She asked her dad, and he said they were grapefruits. He said they were good for you, but they were a little sour. Lily wanted to try one. She asked her dad to pick one for her. He did, and he peeled it for her. He gave her a slice and said, "Be careful, it might be sour."

Lily took a bite. She felt a burst of juice in her mouth. She felt a sour taste on her tongue. She felt her face scrunch up and her tongue sting. She did not like it. She spit it out and said, "Yuck! Sour! No like!"

Her dad laughed and hugged her. He said, "It's okay, Lily. You don't have to like everything. Here, have some water. It will make your tongue feel better."

Lily drank some water. She felt her tongue feel better. She smiled and said, "Thank you, dad. Water good. Grapefruit bad."

Her dad smiled and said, "You're welcome, Lily. I love you. Let's go play on the swings."

Lily nodded and said, "Yes, dad. I love you too. Swings fun."

They went to the swings and had a good time. Lily forgot about the sour grapefruit. She only remembered the sweet water and the warm hug. She was happy. It was a good Sunday.

Sam and Mia love to play at the beach. They like to make sand castles, find shells and splash in the water. One day, they see a big surf board near the shore. It is red and shiny and has a rope on it.

"Wow, look at that!" Sam says. "Can we try it?"

"I don't know," Mia says. "It looks hard to use. And maybe it belongs to someone."

"Let's ask Mom," Sam says. They run to their mom, who is sitting on a towel with a book. "Mom, can we use that surf board? Please?"

Mom looks at the surf board and smiles. "Sure, you can use it. But be careful, okay? And stay close to me. The surf board is for the water, not for the sand."

"Yay, thank you, Mom!" Sam and Mia say. They grab the rope and drag the surf board to the water. They take turns to sit on it and paddle with their hands. They feel the waves lift them up and down. They laugh and shout with joy.

"Look, Mom, I'm surfing!" Sam says.

"Me too, me too!" Mia says.

They have so much fun that they don't notice a hidden rock under the water. When a big wave comes, the surf board hits the rock and flips over. Sam and Mia fall into the water. They are scared and wet. They cry for help.

"Mom, Mom, help us!" they scream.

Mom hears them and runs to the water. She grabs the rope and pulls the surf board back. She helps Sam and Mia to get on it. She hugs them and calms them down.

"Are you okay, my sweeties?" she asks.

"Yes, Mom, we're okay," Sam and Mia say. "But we're sorry. We broke the surf board."

Mom looks at the surf board and sees a crack on it. She sighs and says, "Don't worry, we can fix it. Or we can buy a new one. The important thing is that you are safe and happy. But next time, be more careful, okay? And watch out for hidden rocks."

"Okay, Mom, we will," Sam and Mia say. They hug Mom and say, "We love you, Mom."

"I love you too, my darlings," Mom says. She smiles and says, "Now, let's go and have some ice cream. How does that sound?"

"Yummy, yummy, ice cream!" Sam and Mia say. They release the rope and leave the surf board on the shore. They follow Mom to the ice cream truck. They forget about the surf board and the hidden rock. They only think about the ice cream and the fun they had. They are happy.

Lily has a white coat and a stethoscope. Ben has a bandage and a hat. They find a teddy bear and put it on the couch. "This is our patient," Lily says. "He is sick. We have to make him better."

Ben nods. He looks at the teddy bear with his stethoscope. "He has a fever," he says. "And a sore throat. And a cough." He wraps the bandage around the teddy bear's neck. "There, that will help."

Lily smiles. She takes her finger and pretends it is a needle. "He also needs a shot," she says. "It will make him strong and healthy." She gently pokes the teddy bear with her finger. "Don't worry, it won't hurt."

The teddy bear does not say anything. He just looks at Lily and Ben with his big eyes. He thinks they are very kind. He feels better already. He gives them a hug and a kiss. "Thank you, doctors," he says. "You are the best."

Lily and Ben hug him back. They are happy. They like to play pretend. They like to help their friends. They are kind doctors.

Tom and Lily were at the beach with their mom and dad. They liked to play in the sand and look at the water. Sometimes they saw fish or birds or boats. But today they saw something big and gray and spouty. It was a whale!

"Wow, look at that whale!" Tom said. "It is so big and strong and loud!"

"I want to see it closer!" Lily said. "Maybe it will talk to us or play with us!"

Mom and dad shook their heads. "No, Lily, you can't go near the whale. It is too far and too deep and too dangerous. The whale might not like it if you bother it. It might get angry or scared or hurt you."

"But why?" Lily asked. "The whale looks nice and friendly. It is just swimming and splashing and having fun. Maybe it is lonely and wants some friends."

Tom decided to agree with Lily. He thought mom and dad were ignorant. They did not know anything about whales. He wanted to learn more about them and make them happy. He said to Lily, "Let's go find the whale. We can sneak away when mom and dad are not looking. We can swim to it and say hello and give it a hug."

Lily nodded. She thought Tom was brave and smart. She wanted to go with him and see the whale. She said to Tom, "OK, let's go. But we have to be quick and quiet. We don't want mom and dad to stop us."

They waited until mom and dad were busy with their books and towels. Then they ran to the water and jumped in. They swam as fast as they could, following the whale's spout. They did not see the big waves or the sharp rocks or the other animals. They only saw the whale.

They got closer and closer to the whale. They saw its eyes and mouth and fins and tail. They saw its skin and teeth and blowhole. They thought it was beautiful and amazing. They smiled and waved and shouted, "Hi, whale! We are Tom and Lily! We want to be your friends!"

The whale heard them and saw them. It did not smile or wave or shout back. It did not want to be their friends. It did not like them at all. It thought they were annoying and rude and stupid. It decided to teach them a lesson.

It opened its mouth and sucked them in. It swallowed them whole. It felt them squirm and scream in its belly. It felt satisfied and proud and happy.

It spouted a big jet of water and dived deeper into the sea. It left behind mom and dad, who were looking for Tom and Lily. They did not see the whale or hear their children. They only saw the water and felt the fear and the sadness.

"No, I don't. How do you play?" Mia asked.

"I think so. It sounds fun. Let's play," Mia said.

"Okay, you go first. What does your doll seem like?" Lila asked.

Mia looked at her doll and smiled. She said, "My doll seems like a princess. She has beautiful hair, a lovely dress and sparkly shoes. She is the most wonderful doll ever."

Mia was shocked and angry. She shouted and cried. She wanted her doll back. She did not like the game of 'seem'. She thought Lila and Max were very mean. She wished she had shared her doll with them.

The dog helped the cat find the key and they unlocked the ladder together. The cat was so happy that it climbed up the ladder and played on the roof all day long. From that day on, the cat was no longer grumpy and played with the dog every day.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved to run and play outside. One day, he found a green medal on the ground. He was so happy and proud of himself.

But then, his friend Billy came over and saw the medal. Billy said, "I want that medal. Can I have it?"

Timmy didn't want to give it away, but he didn't want to be mean either. So, he said, "Okay, you can have it. But can you replace it with something else?"

Billy thought for a moment and then said, "I have a red ball at home. I can give that to you instead."

Timmy thought that was a fair trade, so he gave Billy the medal and got the red ball. He was happy again.

The moral of the story is that it's important to share and be kind to others. Sometimes, you can even make a trade to make both people happy.

Lily took care of the bird every day. She gave it food and water. She was very kind to the bird. Soon, the bird's wing was all better. The bird wanted to fly again. Lily knew it was time to let the bird go.

She took the bird outside and opened her hands. The bird flew up into the sky. Lily was sad to see the bird go, but her heart was happy because she had been kind and helped the bird get better.

One day, a restless little dog named Spot was playing outside. The sun was hot, and the heat made Spot very warm. Spot wanted to find a friend to play with.

Spot saw a big tree and heard a bird singing. "Do you want to play with me?" asked Spot. The bird said, "Yes, let's play!" They decided to play a game called "Clap and Hop". Spot would clap his paws, and the bird would hop from branch to branch.

They played and played until they were tired. Spot and the bird sat under the tree to rest. "That was fun!" said Spot. The bird agreed, and they both took a nap in the shade.

They put the flower in Tim's pocket. They were both happy. Tim said, "Thank you, Sam!" And from that day on, Sam was not selfish anymore. They played together and shared their things.

Tom aimed the toy gun at the bad guy and shouted, "Bang! Bang!" The bad guy was scared of the toy gun and ran away. The ice cream man was so happy that Tom saved him. He gave Tom a big ice cream with lots of cream on top. Tom was no longer sleepy and enjoyed his yummy treat.

You have to put them together, like this." She showed him how to slide the hook into the hole. Then she said, "Now you can zip it up. Try it."

Tommy tried again. He pushed the zipper up and it worked. He was happy. He said, "Thank you, mom. I did it!" He put on his shoes and ran to the door.

Tommy was amazed. He said, "Wow. You are firemen. You are brave. You are nice."

The driver said, "Thank you. You are very sweet. You know what? You have something in common with us. Do you know what it is?"

Tommy thought for a moment. He looked at the driver. He looked at his jacket. He saw the zipper. He remembered what his mom taught him. He said, "I know. We both have zippers. We both can zip and unzip them."

The driver smiled. He said, "That's right. We both have zippers. You are very smart. You recognized the zipper. You learned something new today. I'm proud of you."

Tommy smiled too. He said, "Thank you. You are very kind. You taught me something new today. I'm happy."

But Tom did not want the spider to touch his car. He wanted the spider to go away. He shouted, "No, no, spider! Go away! Leave my car alone!"

"Of course, you can keep it, but you have to share it and take good care of it. It is a gift from nature, and we should respect and appreciate it," Mom said.

Tom and Ann take out the blocks. They try to build with them. But they are not easy. Some blocks are big and some are small. Some blocks have one number and some have two. Tom says, "How do we use these blocks?" Ann says, "Maybe we have to match the numbers."

They look at the blocks. They see a block with a one and a block with a zero. They put them together. They make a ten. They are happy. They say, "We made a ten!" They look for more blocks. They see a block with a two and a block with a zero. They put them together. They make a twenty. They are happy. They say, "We made a twenty!"

They keep making numbers with the blocks. They make a thirty, a forty, a fifty. They are very happy. They say, "We are good at this!" They want to make a big tower with the numbers. They start to stack the blocks. They put the ten on the bottom, then the twenty, then the thirty, and so on. They make a tall tower. They say, "Wow, look at our tower!"

But then, Tom steps on a block. He says, "Ouch!" He loses his balance. He bumps into the tower. The tower falls down. The blocks scatter everywhere. Tom and Ann are sad. They say, "Oh no, our tower!" They look at the mess. They see the blocks with the numbers. They see the block with the zero. They say, "This block is not useful. It does not make anything. It is just a zero." They throw the block away. They start to pick up the other blocks. They say, "Let's try again. Maybe we can make a bigger tower." They smile. They are friends. They like to play with blocks. They have fun.

Tim and Sam are curious about Luna. They want to pet her and play with her. But Luna is scared of them. She runs away and hides under the sofa. Tim and Sam try to reach her, but they cannot.

"Let me have her!" Tim says. He pulls Sam's arm.

"No, I want her!" Sam says. He pushes Tim's hand.

"Stop it, both of you!" Mom says. She comes into the living room and sees the mess. She sees Luna's eyes peeking from under the sofa. She says, "You are scaring Luna. She does not like loud noises and rough hands. You have to be gentle and quiet if you want to be her friends."

Tim and Sam feel sorry. They say, "Sorry, Mom. Sorry, Luna." They put away their toys and sit on the floor. They talk to Luna in soft voices. They say, "We are sorry, Luna. We want to be your friends. We have toys for you. You can come out and play with us."

Luna hears them. She sees that they are calm and kind. She feels a little braver. She comes out from under the sofa. She walks slowly to Tim and Sam. She sniffs their hands. She lets them pet her fur. She purrs.

Tim and Sam smile. They say, "Hello, Luna. We are happy to meet you. You are a nice cat. We love you."

Luna feels happy too. She settles on their lap. She naps. Mom watches them and smiles. She says, "You are good boys. You are good friends to Luna. I am proud of you."

One day, Ben and Lily went to the zoo with their mom. They saw many animals, like monkeys, elephants, and giraffes. But their favorite was the lion. The lion was big and strong, and had a long mane of hair. He was lying on a rock, looking bored.

"Can we raise a lion, mom?" Ben asked. He wanted to play with the lion and hear him roar.

"No, honey, we can't raise a lion," mom said. "Lions are wild animals, not pets. They need a lot of space and meat, and they can be dangerous."

"But he looks so gloomy," Lily said. She felt sorry for the lion. He had no friends and no toys.

"Maybe he is gloomy because he misses his home," mom said. "Lions live in Africa, where it is warm and sunny, and they have a family called a pride. They hunt and play together."

"Can we go to Africa and see the lions there?" Ben asked.

"Maybe someday, when you are older," mom said. "But for now, we can do something to cheer up the lion here. Do you have any ideas?"

Ben and Lily thought for a moment. Then they had an idea. They ran to the gift shop and bought a big yellow ball. They went back to the lion's cage and threw the ball over the fence. The ball bounced and rolled near the lion. The lion looked at the ball with curiosity. He got up from his rock and walked towards the ball. He sniffed it, then pawed it, then bit it. The ball squeaked and made a funny noise. The lion liked the noise. He started to play with the ball, tossing it and chasing it. He even roared a few times.

Ben and Lily clapped and laughed. They were happy to see the lion having fun. The lion looked at them and smiled. He was not so gloomy anymore.

"See, mom, we made the lion happy," Ben said.

"Yes, you did," mom said. "You were very kind and thoughtful. But remember, he is still a wild animal, not a pet. We can't raise a lion, but we can respect and admire him."

Ben and Lily nodded. They waved goodbye to the lion and thanked him for the show. They left the zoo feeling proud and happy. They had learned a lot about lions and how to care for them.

They finished their soup and put the cups and spoons back on the table. They thanked the sun and the picnic for their adventure. They held hands and walked down the hill, back to their home. They had a wonderful day.
