Lily and Max liked to play in the attic. They found many old things there, like hats and books and toys. One day, they saw a big box with a picture of a monkey on it. They opened the box and found a brown monkey with a long tail. It was soft and cute.

"Look, Max, a monkey!" Lily said. "Can we keep it?"

Max nodded. He liked the monkey too. He took it out of the box and hugged it. The monkey had a button on its chest. Max pressed the button and the monkey made a funny sound. It said, "Ooh-ooh-ah-ah!"

Lily and Max laughed. They played with the monkey and made it say, "Ooh-ooh-ah-ah!" They put a hat on its head and a scarf around its neck. They pretended it was their pet.

They found a hook on the wall and decided to hang the monkey there. They thought it would be fun to see it swing from its tail. They lifted the monkey and put its tail on the hook. The monkey looked happy.

"Bye-bye, monkey!" Lily said. "We will come back and play with you again!"

They closed the box and went down the stairs. They did not know that the monkey had a secret. When they were gone, the monkey pressed its own button and said, "Ooh-ooh-ah-ah! I'm free!" It jumped off the hook and ran around the attic. It was not a toy. It was a real monkey. And it was very naughty.

Tom and Mia are twins. They like to play outside in the sun. One day, they see a big hill with many trees. They want to climb the hill and see what is on the other side.

They hold hands and start to walk up the hill. They see many birds and flowers and bugs. They are happy and curious. They talk to each other and laugh.

"Look, Tom, a red bird!" Mia says, pointing to the sky.

"Wow, it is so pretty!" Tom says, looking up.

But as they look up, they do not see where they are going. They stumble on a rock and fall down. They hurt their knees and elbows. They cry and hug each other.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Mia says, rubbing her knee.

"Are you okay, Mia?" Tom says, wiping his tears.

"I think so, Tom. Are you okay?" Mia says, looking at his elbow.

"I think so, too. But look, what is that?" Tom says, pointing to something black and gray on the ground.

They see a pile of ash. It is from a fire that burned some of the trees. It is still warm and smoky. They are scared and curious.

"What is it, Tom?" Mia says, touching the ash.

"It is ash, Mia. It is what is left after something burns. It is not good to touch. It can hurt you." Tom says, pulling her hand away.

"Who burned the trees, Tom?" Mia says, looking around.

"I don't know, Mia. Maybe someone who is lazy and does not care about the trees. Or maybe it was an accident. But we should not stay here. It is not safe. Let's go back." Tom says, holding her hand.

"Okay, Tom. Let's go back. Maybe we can find another hill to climb. One that is green and happy." Mia says, nodding.

They get up and walk back down the hill. They are careful and watch where they are going. They see the red bird again and wave to it. They are happy and curious. They talk to each other and laugh.

Tim and Kim are twins who like to play in the park. They have a big red ball that they kick and throw to each other. One day, they see a new slide in the park. It is shiny and tall and has a spiral shape. Tim and Kim want to try the slide, but there is a long line of kids waiting for their turn.

"Can we go on the slide, please?" Tim asks their mom.

"Sure, but you have to wait your turn and be polite," their mom says.

Tim and Kim nod and join the line. But they are very impatient. They want to go on the slide now. They start to whine and fidget and push the other kids.

"Stop that, Tim and Kim," their mom says. "You have to be patient and wait your turn. If you don't, we will go home."

Tim and Kim stop whining and pushing, but they are still unhappy. They look at the slide and wish they could go on it.

Suddenly, they hear a loud noise. They see their big red ball rolling down the hill. It is going fast and heading towards the road. There are cars and trucks on the road. Tim and Kim are scared. They don't want their ball to get hit by a car or a truck.

"Mom, our ball!" they shout.

Their mom sees the ball and runs after it. She tries to catch it, but it is too fast. She sees a gap in the traffic and runs across the road. She grabs the ball and saves it. She is happy and relieved. She brings the ball back to Tim and Kim.

"Mom, you saved our ball!" they say. "Thank you, thank you!"

They hug their mom and kiss her. They are happy and grateful. They don't care about the slide anymore. They just want to play with their ball and their mom.

They go to a grassy spot and play with their ball. They kick and throw it to each other and to their mom. They laugh and have fun. They are not impatient anymore. They are glad that their mom saved their ball and their land.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play outside. Today they go to the park with their moms. They see a trail in the park. The trail has many leaves and rocks.

"Let's go on the trail!" Anna says.

"OK!" Ben says.

They run on the trail. They see a big puddle. The puddle is wet and shiny.

"Look, a puddle!" Ben says.

"Can we jump in it?" Anna asks.

"Yes, but be careful!" their moms say.

Anna and Ben jump in the puddle. They splash and laugh. The water is cold and fun. They get wet and muddy.

"That was fun!" Anna says.

"Yes, it was!" Ben says.

They hug and smile. Their moms give them towels and hugs. They go home happy.

Anna and Ben are twins. They share a room and a bed. They like to play and talk before they sleep. But sometimes they fight over toys and books.

One night, Anna wanted to read a book about a judge. A judge is a person who decides who is right and who is wrong. Ben wanted to play with a small car. A small car is a toy that can move and make noises.

"Give me the book, Anna. I want to read it too," Ben said.

"No, Ben. It is my book. You can play with your car," Anna said.

They pulled and pushed the book. They shouted and cried. They woke up their mom and dad.

Mom and dad came to their room. They were not happy. They looked at Anna and Ben.

"What is going on here? Why are you fighting? It is time to sleep," mom said.

"Anna took my book. She is not fair," Ben said.

"Ben took my car. He is not nice," Anna said.

Mom and dad sighed. They took the book and the car. They put them on a shelf.

"Listen, Anna and Ben. You are twins. You are family. You should share and care for each other. Fighting is not good. It makes you and others unhappy. Do you understand?" dad said.

Anna and Ben nodded. They felt sorry. They hugged each other.

"I am sorry, Anna. You can read the book tomorrow. I love you," Ben said.

"I am sorry, Ben. You can play with the car tomorrow. I love you," Anna said.

Mom and dad smiled. They kissed Anna and Ben. They tucked them in.

"Good night, Anna and Ben. Sleep well. We love you," mom and dad said.

Anna and Ben closed their eyes. They felt warm and cozy. They dreamed of judges and cars. They were happy.

Ben and Jen are twins. They like to play on the farm with their grandpa. Grandpa has many animals, but his favorite is Molly the mule. Molly is brown and big and strong. She helps grandpa carry things and plow the field.

One day, Ben and Jen want to ride Molly. They ask grandpa, and he says yes, but they have to be careful and gentle. He gives them a hat and a scarf to wear, because it is cold outside. He also gives them a carrot to give to Molly as a treat.

Ben and Jen go to the barn, where Molly is waiting. They say hello to Molly and pet her soft fur. They give her the carrot, and she eats it with a loud crunch. Then they climb on her back, one in front of the other. Grandpa helps them with a rope to hold on to.

Molly starts to walk slowly around the farm. Ben and Jen are happy and excited. They see the cows, the sheep, the chickens, and the ducks. They wave to them and say their names. Molly makes a funny noise with her mouth, like she is talking to them too.

But then, Molly sees something that makes her angry. It is a red cloth that someone has hung on a fence. Molly does not like red. She thinks it is scary and bad. She stops walking and starts to kick and buck. She tries to get Ben and Jen off her back. She runs towards the cloth and tries to rip it with her teeth.

Ben and Jen are scared and sad. They hold on to the rope and to each other. They cry for grandpa to help them. Grandpa hears them and runs to them. He grabs the rope and pulls Molly away from the cloth. He calms her down and talks to her softly. He takes Ben and Jen off her back and hugs them. He says they are brave and good. He says Molly is naughty and sorry.

Ben and Jen forgive Molly, but they do not want to ride her again. They say goodbye to her and give her a pat. They go back to the house with grandpa. He gives them some hot cocoa and cookies. He tells them a story about when he was a boy and rode a mule. He says mules are smart and loyal, but sometimes they are stubborn and silly. He says he loves Molly, even when she is naughty. Ben and Jen love grandpa, and they love Molly too. They smile and sip their cocoa. They are happy and warm.

Lily and Ben went to the shop with Mom. They wanted to buy a treat for being good. Mom said they could choose one thing each.

Lily saw a plastic doll with long hair and a pink dress. She liked the doll very much. She said, "Mom, can I buy this doll? She is so pretty and I can comb her hair."

Ben saw a plastic car with big wheels and a loud horn. He liked the car very much. He said, "Mom, can I buy this car? It is so fast and I can make it beep."

Mom smiled and said, "Yes, you can buy the doll and the car. They are not very expensive and you have been good. But first, let's buy some fruit for later. Fruit is delicious and healthy."

Lily and Ben agreed and helped Mom pick some apples, bananas and grapes. They put them in a bag and paid at the counter. Then they took their plastic toys and went home.

They were very happy with their new toys. They played with them all afternoon. They also ate some fruit and shared with Mom. They said, "Thank you, Mom, for buying us these toys and fruit. They are both delicious." Mom hugged them and said, "You're welcome, my sweeties. I love you very much."

Lily and Ben were friends who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big tree with red apples on it. They wanted to pick some apples to eat, but the tree was too high for them.

"Look, there is a ladder!" Ben said. He pointed to a wooden ladder that was hidden behind some bushes. "We can use it to climb the tree and get the apples."

Lily was not sure. She thought the ladder looked old and shaky. She was afraid it might break or fall. "I don't think we should use that ladder," she said. "It is not safe. Maybe the apples belong to someone else."

Ben did not listen to Lily. He ran to the ladder and started to climb. He reached the first branch and grabbed an apple. He smiled and said, "This apple is so juicy and sweet. Come on, Lily, don't be scared. There are more apples for us."

Lily shook her head. She stayed on the ground and watched Ben. She hoped he would be careful. But then, she heard a loud crack. The ladder broke and Ben fell down. He hit the ground hard and cried out in pain.

Lily ran to Ben and saw that he had hurt his arm and leg. She felt sorry for him and tried to help him. She said, "Ben, are you okay? I'm sorry you fell. We should go and find a grown-up to help you."

Ben nodded and said, "Lily, you were right. I was wrong. I should have listened to you. The ladder was not safe. The apples were not worth it. I'm sorry I was greedy and foolish."

Lily and Ben learned a lesson that day. They learned that they should be careful and respectful. They learned that they should listen to their friends and not take what is not theirs. They learned that sometimes, the best things are not hidden, but right in front of them.

Sam and Mia were playing in the garden. They liked to pretend they were lions and tigers. They would run and jump and roar at each other. They had a lot of fun.

One day, they found a big jug in the shed. It was empty and had a handle and a spout. Sam had an idea. He said to Mia, "Let's fill the jug with water and use it as a fountain. We can be lions and tigers who drink from the fountain."

Mia liked the idea. They took the jug to the tap and filled it with water. Then they carried it to the middle of the garden and put it on the ground. They took turns to tilt the jug and make the water come out of the spout. They pretended to lap up the water with their tongues and make happy noises.

They were having so much fun that they did not hear their mum calling them for lunch. She came out to the garden and saw them playing with the jug. She smiled and said, "You two look like very thirsty lions and tigers. Do you want to come inside and have some sandwiches and juice?"

Sam and Mia nodded and ran to their mum. They gave her a hug and said, "Thank you, mum. We love you." They left the jug in the garden. It was peaceful and quiet. The sun shone on the water and made it sparkle. The jug was happy too. It had made two new friends.

Jill liked to play with snow. She made snowballs and snowmen with her friends. She wore a pink hat and a pink coat and pink gloves. She was very popular and everyone wanted to be her friend.

One day, a new girl came to the park. Her name was Kate. She had a blue hat and a blue coat and no gloves. She looked cold and sad. Jill felt sorry for her and wanted to help her.

"Hi, I am Jill. Do you want to play with me?" Jill asked.

"Hi, I am Kate. I want to play, but I have no gloves. My hands are very cold," Kate said.

"That's okay. You can lend my gloves. They are very warm and pretty," Jill said. She took off her gloves and gave them to Kate.

"Thank you, Jill. You are very nice," Kate said. She put on the gloves and smiled.

Jill and Kate played with snow. They made snowballs and snowmen and had fun. Jill was happy to share her gloves with Kate.

But then, something bad happened. Kate saw some other kids playing with a sled. She wanted to try it too. She ran to the sled and jumped on it. She did not ask Jill or the other kids. She did not say goodbye. She just took the sled and the gloves and slid down the hill.

"Hey, that's not fair! That's our sled! And those are my gloves!" Jill shouted.

But Kate did not hear her. She did not care. She just kept sliding and laughing. She did not give back the sled or the gloves. She was very mean and selfish.

Jill was very sad and angry. She had no gloves and no sled and no friend. She felt cold and lonely. She cried and went home. She wished she never met Kate. She wished she never lent her gloves. She learned a hard lesson. Not everyone is nice and honest. Some people are bad and greedy. She had to be careful who she trusted.

Lily and Ben are twins. They share a room and a bed. They like to play and read and sing together. But sometimes they fight over toys and books and space.

One night, Lily and Ben are getting ready for bed. They brush their teeth and put on their pajamas. Then they climb into their bed and pick a book to read. Lily wants to read about princesses and dragons. Ben wants to read about cars and planes. They both pull the book they want and tug and tug.

"Let go of my book!" Lily says. "I want to read it first!"

"No, let go of my book!" Ben says. "I want to read it first!"

"Let's test our spears," Lila whispered to Rani. "You go left and I go right. We will throw our spears at the same time."

Rani nodded and they crept closer to the rabbit. They counted to three and threw their spears. But the rabbit was clever and saw them. It jumped away and ran into the bush.

"Oh no, we missed!" Lila said. "The rabbit is too fast and smart."

"Maybe we can trick it," Rani said. "Look, there is a carrot on the ground. We can use it as bait."

Rani picked up the carrot and placed it near the bush. She hid behind a tree and waited. Lila hid behind another tree and held her spear. They hoped the rabbit would come out and eat the carrot.

Soon, they heard a rustle in the bush. The rabbit poked its head out and sniffed the air. It saw the carrot and licked its lips. It hopped out of the bush and moved towards the carrot.

"Now!" Rani shouted. She and Lila threw their spears again. This time, they hit the rabbit and it fell to the ground.

"Yay, we got it!" Lila cheered. "We are good hunters!"

They ran to the rabbit and picked it up. They were proud of their spears and their clever plan. They took the rabbit home and cooked it for their dinner. The white dog does not like Lily. It barks and snaps at her. Lily is scared and sad. She runs back to Mom and Max. Mom hugs her and says, "Are you okay, Lily? That was a mean dog. It does not know how to be nice."

Max is angry at the white dog. He growls and shows his teeth. He wants to protect Lily. He does not like mean dogs. He thinks they are ignorant. He does not know what ignorant means, but he heard Mom say it once.

Mom sees Max growl. She says, "No, Max. Do not fight. We do not want trouble. Come, let's go to another part of the park. There are nicer dogs there." She pulls Max by his leash. Max nods and follows Mom. He trusts her. He looks at Lily and licks her face. He says, "I love you, Lily. You are a good girl." Lily smiles and says, "I love you too, Max. You are a good dog."

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play together, but sometimes they fight. One day, they want to play with the same toy car. Anna grabs the car first, but Ben pulls it hard. They both yell and tug at the car.

"Mine!" Anna says.

"No, mine!" Ben says.

Mom hears them and comes to see what is wrong. She sees them fighting over the toy car. She is not happy. She takes the car away and puts it on a high shelf.

"Stop fighting, Anna and Ben. You need to share and take turns. Now, go to the bathroom and wash your hands. It is time for lunch," Mom says.

Anna and Ben are sad and angry. They do not want to go to the bathroom. They want the toy car. They walk slowly to the bathroom, still frowning. They see a big mirror on the wall. They look at themselves and make funny faces. They start to giggle and forget about the car.

They wash their hands and dry them with a towel. They see a bottle of soap on the sink. They open it and squeeze some soap on their hands. They rub their hands together and make bubbles. They blow the bubbles and watch them fly. They laugh and clap their hands.

They have fun with the soap and the bubbles. They do not hear Mom calling them for lunch. They do not see the soap and the water making a mess on the floor. They think the bathroom is perfect. They do not know that Mom will scream when she sees the bathroom.

Lily and Tom are friends. They like to play outside. One day, they wake up very early. They want to see the sunrise.

They put on their coats and hats. They go to the hill near their house. They sit on the grass and wait. The sky is dark and quiet.

"Look, Lily, the sun is coming!" Tom says. He points to the horizon. He sees a bright orange ball. It is getting bigger and bigger.

"Wow, it is so pretty!" Lily says. She smiles and claps her hands. She sees the sky changing colors. It is pink and purple and yellow.

They watch the sunrise for a long time. They feel happy and warm. They talk and laugh and sing.

But then, Lily sees something. She sees a big rock behind Tom. It is rolling down the hill. It is coming fast.

"Tom, watch out!" Lily shouts. She tries to pull Tom away. But it is too late. The rock hits Tom. He falls down. He cries out loud.

Lily is scared. She runs to Tom. She hugs him and says sorry. She sees a cut on his knee. It is bleeding.

"Are you okay, Tom?" Lily asks. She feels sad and sorry.

Tom is hurt. He feels pain and angry. He pushes Lily away. He says, "Go away, Lily! You are not my friend! You made me fall!"

Lily is shocked. She does not understand. She did not make Tom fall. She tried to help him. She says, "No, Tom, I am your friend! I did not make you fall! The rock made you fall!"

But Tom does not listen. He gets up and limps away. He leaves Lily alone on the hill. He goes back to his house.

Lily is alone. She feels sad and lonely. She does not know what to do. She looks at the sunrise. It is not pretty anymore. It is just regular. She cries.

Lily and Tom were friends who liked to bake. They baked cakes, pies, cookies and bread. They shared their treats with their families and neighbors. Everyone in town loved their baking.

One day, it was very cold and icy outside. Lily and Tom could not go out to play. They decided to bake something warm and yummy. They asked their moms for some flour, sugar, eggs, butter and milk. They also found some chocolate chips and nuts in the pantry.

They mixed everything in a big bowl and poured it into a pan. They put the pan in the oven and waited for it to bake. They smelled the sweet and nutty aroma of their cake. They were very excited to taste it.

When the cake was done, they took it out of the oven and let it cool. They cut two big slices and put some whipped cream on top. They sat down at the table and ate their cake. It was soft, moist and delicious.

They said to each other, "This is the best cake ever! We are very good bakers!"

They smiled and hugged. They were happy and warm, even though it was icy outside.

One day, Tom and Lily went to play in the snow. They put on their warm coats, hats, gloves and boots. They ran outside and saw the white powder on the ground. It was cold and soft.

"Let's make a snowman!" said Tom. He rolled a big ball of snow and put it on the grass. Then he rolled a smaller ball and put it on top of the big one. He found two sticks for the arms, a carrot for the nose, and some stones for the eyes and mouth.

"Look, our snowman is done!" said Lily. She wrapped a scarf around his neck and gave him a hat. "He looks happy!"

They heard a loud noise. It was a snow plow. It was big and gray and had a metal blade. It was clearing the road of snow.

"Watch out!" shouted Tom. He grabbed Lily's hand and pulled her away from the snowman. The snow plow came closer and closer. It pushed the snow to the side of the road.

"Stop!" cried Lily. "You're going to hit our snowman!"

But the snow plow did not stop. It hit the snowman and broke him into pieces. The snow flew in the air and landed on Tom and Lily. They were covered in snow.

They were very sad. They looked at the snow plow. The driver saw them and waved. He said he was sorry. He did not see their snowman.

"It's okay," said Tom. He hugged Lily. "We can make another snowman. But we have to put him somewhere safe."

They brushed off the snow from their clothes and went to find a new spot for their snowman. They decided to put him in their backyard, where the snow plow could not reach him. They smiled and started to roll new balls of snow. They were happy again.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play in their room. They have many toys and books. But they do not like to share. They always fight over who gets what.

One day, they find a yellow box in their closet. They do not know what is inside. They both want to open it. They pull and tug and yell.

"Give me the box! It is mine!" Anna says.

"No, it is mine! I saw it first!" Ben says.

They do not listen to each other. They do not care about each other's feelings. They only want the box.

Suddenly, the box breaks. It falls to the floor. Out comes a big mess. There are papers and crayons and stickers and glue. They are all over the room. They are all over Anna and Ben.

Anna and Ben stop fighting. They look at the mess. They feel sad and sorry. They wish they had not been so greedy and mean.

They look at each other. They say sorry.

"I am sorry, Anna. I should have shared with you. You are my sister. I love you." Ben says.

"I am sorry, Ben. I should have listened to you. You are my brother. I love you." Anna says.

They hug and smile. They decide to clean up the mess together. They use the papers and crayons and stickers and glue to make cards and pictures. They have fun and laugh. They share and care.

They learn a lesson. They learn that sharing is better than fighting. They learn that listening is better than yelling. They learn that love is better than greed.

They are happy. They are twins. They are friends.

Sara was lonely. She had no friends to play with. She liked to read stories, but she had read all her books. She wished she had a new story to read.

One day, she found a big book in the attic. It had many pictures and words. Sara opened the book and saw a story about a princess and a dragon. She wanted to read it, but the words were too hard. She could not read them.

She looked at the pictures and tried to guess what the story was. She saw the princess in a castle, the dragon in a cave, and a knight on a horse. She made up her own story in her head. She said, "The princess was sad. She wanted to go out and see the world. But the dragon was scary. He breathed fire and roared. He did not let anyone near the castle. The knight was brave. He wanted to save the princess. He rode his horse to the cave. He fought the dragon with his sword."

Sara turned the page and saw a picture of the princess and the knight hugging. She smiled and said, "The knight won. He beat the dragon. He freed the princess. They were happy. They kissed and hugged. They went away together."

She turned the page again and saw a picture of the dragon. He was not dead. He was crying. He had a bandage on his nose. He looked sad and lonely. Sara felt sorry for him. She said, "The dragon was not bad. He was lonely. He had no friends. He only wanted to play. He did not know how to be nice. He did not know how to share. He did not know how to love."

Sara closed the book and thought for a while. She had an idea. She said, "I will be the dragon's friend. I will teach him how to be nice. I will teach him how to share. I will teach him how to love. I will read him stories. He will not be lonely anymore. He will be happy."

She took the book and ran down the stairs. She went outside and looked for the dragon. She did not see him, but she heard him. He was in the woods, behind the house. He was still crying. Sara called out, "Hello, dragon! I have a story for you. Do you want to hear it?"

The dragon heard her voice and stopped crying. He was curious. He peeked out from the trees and saw a little girl with a big book. He said, "Who are you? What do you want?"

Sara smiled and said, "I am Sara. I want to be your friend. I have a story for you. It is about a princess and a knight and a dragon. Do you want to hear it?"

The dragon nodded and said, "Yes, I do. I like stories. But I have no one to read them to me."

Sara said, "I will read it to you. Come closer. Don't be afraid. I will not hurt you."

The dragon came closer and sat down next to Sara. He looked at the book and said, "What is this?"

Sara said, "This is a book. It has pictures and words. The words tell the story. The pictures show the story. I will read the words to you. You can look at the pictures. You can ask me questions. You can tell me what you think. You can taste the story with me."

The dragon said, "Taste the story? What does that mean?"

Sara said, "It means to enjoy the story. To feel the story. To imagine the story. To learn from the story. To love the story. Stories are yummy. They make us happy. They make us smart. They make us kind. They make us friends."

The dragon said, "I want to taste the story. I want to be happy. I want to be smart. I want to be kind. I want to be your friend."

Sara said, "Then let's taste the story together. Let's start from the beginning. Once upon a time, there was a princess and a dragon..."

Lily and Tom were very sad. They liked the slide. They wanted to play on it. They were also scared of the truck. They ran away from the park and looked for their mom. They found her at home. She was making cookies for them.

She said they could have some cookies and play with their toys. She said maybe the fog would go away soon and they could go back to the park.

Lily and Tom felt better. They ate some cookies and played with their toys. They hoped the slide would be fixed soon. They still liked the fog, but they also liked the slide. They learned to be careful in the fog. They learned that sometimes things go wrong, but mom is always there to help.

Timmy's mom laughed and said, "No, Timmy. We can't read a book on the motorcycle. But we can enjoy the ride together!" Timmy smiled and held on tight as they rode down the road. He was having so much fun on the motorcycle with his mom.

Timmy's mommy quickly opened the windows to clear the air. They were all safe, but they knew they had to be careful with gas. The lion looked and looked, but he couldn't find them. He was starting to get frustrated. "Where did they go?" he roared. Suddenly, the rabbit popped out of the hole and said, "Don't be mad, we didn't mean to lose you!"

The lion was happy to have found them and they all laughed and played together. They were all happy that they were not dead and were still friends.

"Let me go!" Tweety said.

"No way, birdie. You're going to jail," the cat replied.

Tweety was scared and didn't know what to do. Suddenly, Tweety remembered that birds can move their wings really fast. So, Tweety flapped its wings and flew away from the cat's grasp. Tweety flew until it found a safe place to rest. From that day on, Tweety made sure to stay away from any unusual cages and any cats that might try to put it in jail.

Once upon a time, there was a big black dog. The dog loved to run and play in the park with his friends. One day, the dog saw a big tree and he wanted to climb it. So, he ran to the tree and started to climb. 

As he climbed, he saw a bird's nest on the tree. The bird was not there, but there were some eggs in the nest. The dog wanted to see the eggs, so he carefully reached out and touched them. Suddenly, the bird came back and saw the dog touching her eggs. She was angry and started to chirp loudly. 

The dog felt bad and wanted to make it up to the bird. He remembered that he had seen his owner stir some food in a pot before, so he went to his owner's house and got a wooden spoon. He brought the spoon back to the tree and started to stir the air around the bird's nest. The bird saw what the dog was doing and stopped chirping. She was happy that the dog wanted to help her. From that day on, the dog and the bird became friends and played together in the park.

"Maybe we can find another key," Tim says.

"Or maybe we can find another trunk," Mia says.

They keep playing in the park. They hope to find something fun and nice. They are not selfish. They like to share.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. They run and jump and laugh. One day, they see a big hill. They want to go up the hill.

"Let's go, Lily!" Ben says. "It will be fun!"

"OK, Ben!" Lily says. "But be careful!"

They start to climb the hill. It is steep and rocky. They hold hands and help each other. They are almost at the top when Lily slips. She falls and scrapes her knee. It is red and bleeding. It hurts a lot.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Lily cries. "My knee hurts!"

Ben runs to her. He sees her knee. He feels sorry for her.

"I'm sorry, Lily!" Ben says. "Are you OK?"

"No, Ben!" Lily says. "It hurts! I want to go home!"

Ben hugs her. He tries to make her feel better.

"Don't cry, Lily!" Ben says. "We can go home. But first, we need to get a patch. A patch will cover your knee and make it stop bleeding. It will also make it heal faster. Do you know what a patch is?"

Lily shakes her head. She does not know what a patch is.

"A patch is a small piece of cloth or plastic that sticks to your skin. It has a soft part in the middle that touches your wound. It is like a band-aid, but bigger. My mom has some patches at home. She can give you one. Come on, let's go!"

Ben helps Lily stand up. He holds her hand and leads her down the hill. They walk slowly and carefully. They go to Ben's house. Ben's mom sees them. She sees Lily's knee. She is worried.

"What happened, Ben?" Ben's mom asks. "Did Lily get hurt?"

"Yes, mom," Ben says. "She fell on the hill. She needs a patch. Do you have one?"

"Of course, Ben," Ben's mom says. "Come here, Lily. Let me see your knee. Don't worry, it's not too bad. I'll clean it and put a patch on it. It will feel better soon."

Ben's mom takes Lily to the bathroom. She washes her knee with water and soap. She dries it with a towel. She takes a patch from a box. She peels off the paper and sticks it on Lily's knee. The patch is pink and has a picture of a flower on it.

"There you go, Lily," Ben's mom says. "How do you feel?"

Lily looks at her knee. She sees the patch. She smiles.

"Thank you, Ben's mom," Lily says. "The patch is pretty. And it doesn't hurt anymore."

"You're welcome, Lily," Ben's mom says. "I'm glad you like it. You're a brave girl. Do you want some juice and cookies?"

"Yes, please," Lily says.

Ben's mom gives them some juice and cookies. They sit on the couch and eat them. They talk and laugh. They are happy.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. They run and jump and laugh. Today, they learned what a patch is. They learned that a patch can help a hurt knee. They learned that a patch can also make a friend feel better. They learned something new. And they had fun.

One day, a boy named Tom went to the park with his mom. He saw a big pond with many ducks and geese. He wanted to feed them some bread, but his mom said no. She said the bread was not good for the birds, and they had enough food in the pond.

But Tom did not listen. He took a piece of bread from his mom's bag when she was not looking. He ran to the pond and threw the bread to the geese. One goose was very greedy and tried to get all the bread for himself. He chased away the other geese and bit Tom's hand. Tom cried out in pain and dropped the bread.

"Ow, ow, ow! That goose is mean and hot!" Tom said.

"Tom, what did you do?" his mom asked. She saw the bread and the goose and understood what happened. She took Tom away from the pond and put some ice on his hand. She said, "Tom, you should not have fed the geese. They are wild animals and they can hurt you. You should respect them and their home. And you should listen to me when I tell you something. I know what is best for you and the birds."

Tom felt sorry for what he did. He said, "I'm sorry, mom. I was wrong. I will not feed the geese again. I will listen to you and be nice to the animals."

His mom hugged him and said, "That's good, Tom. I love you. And I'm sure the geese will forgive you too. But next time, if you want to see them, just watch them from a distance. And maybe you can learn something from them. Do you know what they do when they swim in the pond?"

Tom shook his head.

"They reverse. They turn around and stick their heads in the water to look for food. They are very clever and funny. Do you want to see them reverse?"

Tom nodded. He smiled and said, "Yes, mom. I want to see them reverse. Maybe they will make me laugh and forget my hot hand."

His mom smiled too. She said, "Let's go then. But remember, no more bread for the geese. OK?"

Tom said, "OK, mom. No more bread for the geese. Only reverse for me."

Lily was a little lamb who loved to eat hay. She always ate more hay than the other lambs, because she thought it was so yummy. She did not like to share her hay with anyone, not even her friends.

One day, she saw a big pile of hay in the barn. She ran to it and started to eat as much as she could. She did not notice that the pile was very high and unstable. She ate and ate, until she reached the top of the hay.

"Wow, this is the best hay ever!" she said to herself. "I am so lucky to have it all for me!"

But then, the hay started to move. It was too heavy for the pile to hold. The hay fell down, and Lily fell with it. She was buried under the hay, and she could not get out. She started to cry for help.

"Help! Help! I am stuck under the hay!" she shouted.

The other lambs heard her cry. They ran to the barn and saw what had happened. They felt sorry for Lily, but they also remembered how she never shared her hay with them.

"Why should we help you?" they asked. "You always ate all the hay by yourself. You did not care about us. You were greedy and selfish."

Lily realized that they were right. She had been greedy and selfish. She had not been a good friend. She felt very sorry and ashamed.

"Please, please, help me!" she begged. "I am sorry for what I did. I was wrong. I will share my hay with you from now on. I will be a good friend. Please, forgive me!"

The other lambs saw that Lily was sincere. They decided to forgive her and help her. They worked together to move the hay and free Lily. Lily was very grateful and happy. She hugged the other lambs and thanked them.

"Thank you, thank you, thank you!" she said. "You are very kind and generous. You are my true friends. I will never be greedy and selfish again. I will share my hay with you, and we can eat it together. It will be more yummy that way!"

The other lambs smiled and nodded. They were glad that Lily had learned her lesson. They took some hay and ate it with Lily. They enjoyed the hay and each other's company. They were happy and content.

The moral of the story is: Sharing is caring. Greediness and selfishness can lead to trouble and loneliness. Friendship and generosity can bring happiness and joy.

"Careful, the salsa is spicy," Mom warned.

Lila and Ben took a bite of the carrot with salsa. They felt a hot and tangy sensation in their mouths. They made funny faces and reached for their water.

"Spicy, spicy!" they shouted, laughing.

"Spicy is good, but not too much. You are brave to try new things. Just like explorers of the universe," she said.

Lily started to examine Hoppy. She looked at his ears, his eyes, and his nose. She listened to his heart with her stethoscope. She said, "Hoppy, you are very healthy. But I need to check one more thing. I need to see how high you can raise your arms."

Lily took Hoppy's arms and tried to raise them up. But Hoppy's arms did not move. They were sewn to his body. Lily was surprised. She tried again, but Hoppy's arms still did not move. Lily was confused. She said, "Hoppy, why can't you raise your arms? Don't you want to play with me?"

Lily did not know that Hoppy was not a normal toy. He was a special toy. He had a secret. He had a button on his belly. When Lily pressed the button, Hoppy's arms would raise up and he would say, "I love you, Lily!"

But Lily did not see the button. She did not hear Hoppy's voice. She only saw his arms that did not move. She felt sad. She thought Hoppy did not like her. She said, "Hoppy, I'm sorry. I don't want to hurt you. I just want to be your friend."

Lily put Hoppy down and hugged him. She said, "Hoppy, you are very soft and cute. I like you very much. Please, raise your arms and hug me back."

Lily did not know that when she hugged Hoppy, she pressed the button on his belly. She did not expect what happened next. Hoppy's arms raised up and wrapped around her. He said, "I love you, Lily!"

Lily was shocked. She looked at Hoppy's face. He smiled at her. She heard his voice. She said, "Hoppy, you can talk! You can raise your arms! You love me!"

Lily was very happy. She hugged Hoppy again. She said, "I love you too, Hoppy! You are the best toy ever! You are my new patient and my new friend!"

Lily and Hoppy played doctor for a long time. They had a lot of fun. They were very happy. They were the best friends ever.

Lily was a compassionate girl who loved animals. She had a pet rabbit named Fluffy who was white and soft. She liked to hug Fluffy and feed him carrots and lettuce. Fluffy liked Lily too and would hop around her room and lick her face.

One day, Lily's mom said they had to go to the store and buy some things. She told Lily to put Fluffy in his cage and lock the door. Lily did as she was told, but she felt sad to leave Fluffy alone. She gave him a kiss and said, "I'll be back soon, Fluffy. Don't be scared."

But Fluffy was curious and wanted to explore. He saw a small hole in the cage and pushed his nose through it. He realized he could squeeze his body out of the hole and escape. He was happy and jumped out of the cage. He saw a bag on the floor that smelled good. He went inside the bag and found some bread and cheese. He nibbled on them and felt full.

But then he heard a loud noise. It was Lily's mom who picked up the bag and put it in the car. She didn't see Fluffy inside the bag. She drove to the store and parked the car. She left the bag in the back seat and locked the doors. Fluffy was scared and wanted to go back to Lily. He tried to get out of the bag, but it was too dark and tight. Lily's mom sighed and said, "I'm not mad at Fluffy. I'm glad he's safe. But you have to watch him more closely and make sure he stays in his cage when we're not home. He's a smart rabbit, but he doesn't know the dangers of the outside world. He needs your protection and care."

Lily nodded and said, "I understand, mom. I'll be more careful and responsible. I'll make sure Fluffy stays in his cage and has enough food and water. I'll also play with him and keep him company. He's a compassionate rabbit, and I'm a compassionate girl. We love each other."

Lily's mom smiled and said, "That's good, Lily. You're a compassionate girl, and I'm proud of you. Now let's go home and give Fluffy a treat. He deserves it after his big adventure."

Lily and Fluffy were happy and went home with Lily's mom. They learned a lesson and became closer friends. They never escaped again.

"Uh-oh, what's that?" Tom asked.

"I don't know, but it smells bad!" Anna said.

"Who baked this cake?" the fireman asked.

Tom and Anna looked at each other and felt uncomfortable. They knew they had done something wrong.

"We did, sir," Tom said.

"We wanted to surprise our mom," Anna said.

The fireman smiled and said, "That's very sweet of you, but you should never bake without an adult. Baking can be dangerous if you don't watch the oven. Next time, ask your mom or dad to help you, okay?"

Tom and Anna nodded and said, "Okay, sir. We're sorry."

The fireman said, "It's okay, no one got hurt. But this cake is not edible. How about I help you make a new one? I know a good recipe."

Tom and Anna smiled and said, "Yes, please!"

The fireman took them to his fire truck and showed them his kitchen. He had some ingredients and tools in a box. He taught them how to measure, mix, and bake a cake. He also let them decorate it with frosting and sprinkles. The cake looked and smelled delicious.

"Wow, you're a great baker, sir!" Tom said.

"Thank you, you're great helpers!" the fireman said.

Rex barked louder and pulled them back. He knew the house was on fire and it was not safe to go near it. He wanted Lily and Tom to stay away from the smoke and the flames.

"Rex, let us go!" Tom said. "We just want to look!"

The moral of the story is: Listen to your reliable friends. They know what is best for you and they want to keep you safe.

"Come on, Lila, let's go up the hill!" Tom said.

"OK, Tom, but be careful. It looks high and steep." Lila said.

They started to climb the hill, holding on to the rocks and dirt. They were almost at the top when they heard a loud noise. It was a train, coming fast on the tracks below the hill. The hill was not a hill, it was a cliff!

"Tom, look! A train! We have to get down!" Lila shouted.

"Wow, a train! Let's watch it!" Tom said.

"No, Tom, it's not safe! The train might make the cliff fall!" Lila said.

But Tom did not listen. He wanted to see the train. He moved closer to the edge of the cliff. He leaned over to get a better view. He lost his balance and slipped. He screamed as he fell.

Lila was scared. She ran to the edge and looked down. She saw Tom lying on the ground, near the tracks. He was not moving. She saw blood on his head and clothes. She saw the train coming closer and closer.

"Tom! Tom! Wake up! The train is coming!" Lila cried.

But Tom did not wake up. He did not hear her. He did not see the train.

Lila did not know what to do. She wanted to help Tom, but she could not reach him. She wanted to call for help, but she did not see anyone. She wanted to run away, but she was frozen.

The train was very near. It was loud and fast. It had a horn and a light. It did not see Tom. It did not stop.

Lila closed her eyes. She heard a crash. She felt a shake. She opened her eyes. She saw dust and smoke. She saw rocks and dirt. She did not see Tom.

Lila was sad. She was scared. She was ashamed. She wished she had not climbed the cliff. She wished she had not delayed Tom. She wished she had saved Tom. She wished Tom was alive.

"I don't know, but it's so furry and soft. Let's play with it," Liz said.

They took the furry thing out of the box and put it on the floor. They hugged it and tickled it and gave it a name. They called it Fluffy.

"Fluffy is our new friend. We have to keep him a secret from mom and dad. They might take him away," Tim said.

"OK, Fluffy is our secret. We can seat him in the box when we are not playing with him," Liz said.

They played with Fluffy for a while, but then they heard mom calling them for lunch. They quickly put Fluffy back in the box and closed it. They ran to the kitchen and ate their sandwiches and juice.

"Can we go back to the garage and play with Fluffy?" Tim asked.

"Not now, sweeties. We have to go to the store and buy some things. You can play with Fluffy later," mom said.

Tim and Liz were sad, but they nodded. They put on their shoes and coats and followed mom to the car. They did not know that Fluffy was not a teddy bear, but a wild animal that mom and dad had found in the woods. They did not know that Fluffy was hungry and angry and wanted to get out of the box. They did not know that Fluffy had scratched the box and made a hole in it. They did not know that Fluffy had escaped from the box and was waiting for them in the garage. They did not know that Fluffy was not their friend, but their enemy. They did not know that Fluffy was going to hurt them when they came back. They did not know that their secret was going to be their end.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park. They found a shiny thing on the ground. It was a crown. Tom picked it up and put it on his head.

"Look, Lily, I am a king!" he said.

Lily laughed. "No, you are not a king, Tom. You are just a normal boy. A king has a big castle and many people who do what he says."

Tom did not like that. He wanted to be a king. He thought of a way to make Lily believe him.

"OK, Lily, if I am not a king, then what is my name?" he asked.

Lily thought for a moment. She knew Tom's name. It was Tom.

"Your name is Tom, silly," she said.

Tom smiled. He had a trick.

"No, Lily, that is not my name. My name is King Tom. And you have to call me that, or I will not be your friend," he said.

Lily was surprised. She did not like Tom's trick. She did not want to call him King Tom. She liked him better when he was just Tom.

"Tom, that is not nice. You are not King Tom. You are just Tom. And I like you as Tom. You are my friend. But if you want to be King Tom, then you can play by yourself. I will find another friend who is normal," she said.

She took off the crown from Tom's head and gave it back to him. Then she walked away.

Tom felt sad. He realized he had made a mistake. He did not want to be King Tom. He wanted to be Lily's friend. He ran after her.

"Lily, wait! I am sorry. I was just playing. You are right. I am not King Tom. I am just Tom. And I like you as Lily. You are my friend. Can we play together again?" he said.

Lily stopped and turned around. She saw Tom's face. He looked sorry. She forgave him.

"OK, Tom, I forgive you. You are just Tom. And I am just Lily. And we are friends. Let's play together again. But no more tricks, OK?" she said.

Tom nodded. He hugged Lily. They put the crown back on the ground. They did not need it. They were happy as normal. They played in the park until it was time to go home.

He paddled away with his hands. He saw some ducks and some fish. He had fun.

Lily saw Sam from far away. She saw his raft. She saw him smiling. She felt sorry. She said, "Sam, wait for me. I want to play with you. I want to see your raft. It looks nice."

She tried to catch up with him. But her raft was too big and heavy. She could not paddle fast. She said, "Sam, please, come back. I'm sorry. I want to be your friend."

But Sam did not hear her. He was too far away. He was happy. He said, "This is my raft. I made it by myself. It is better than Lily's raft."

They point to the dog. The dog is still running with a ball. It looks normal. It does not know it is bad.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny. The bunny loved to jump all around the forest. One day, the bunny saw a big rainbow in the sky. It was so pretty! The bunny wanted to touch the rainbow so badly. 

But the rainbow was too high up in the sky. The bunny tried to jump really hard, but he couldn't reach it. He felt sad because he wanted to touch the rainbow so much. 

Then, it started to rain. The bunny looked up and saw that the rainbow was gone. He felt even sadder now. But then, he realized that the rain was making the grass and flowers grow. And that made the bunny happy again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a shiny flute that she loved to play. One night, Lily was walking in the dark forest when she heard a strange noise. She stopped and stared into the dark. Suddenly, a big bear appeared in front of her!

"Hello, little girl," said the bear. "What do you have there?"

"I have my flute," replied Lily.

"Can you play it for me?" asked the bear.

Lily played a beautiful tune on her flute. The bear loved it and asked if he could keep it. Lily was scared, but she didn't want to be rude, so she said yes. The bear took the flute and walked away. Lily was sad, but she knew she would never forget the music she played on her flute that night.

The team searched and searched for the fox, but they couldn't find him. They were sad and worried. They asked all the other animals in the forest if they had seen the fox, but no one had.

Suddenly, there was a noise which sounded like a fire burning. Lucy looked around but could not see anything. Then she noticed smoke rising from the forest. She said to Mummy, "something's burning!" 

Mummy said, "Yes, sweetheart, the forest is burning". Lucy was so scared. Mummy held her close and said, "It's okay, the fire will die out soon". 

The fire burned and burned, until the sky turned dark. Then the rain started to fall. The rain put out the fire, and the sky was empty again. Everyone was relieved, and Lucy watched a rainbow appear in the sky. She smiled and said, "Look, Mummy! The rainbow is back. Everything is okay now."

The dragon watched over the witch, not making a sound. As he stared at her, he noticed something peculiar.

He looked closely and saw that the witch had shrunk in size! She was now only as tall as two inches! The dragon was amazed and decided to wait until the witch woke up.

After a few hours, the witch stirred and slowly opened her eyes. 

The dragon said excitedly, "Look how tiny you are! What happened?"

The witch smiled and said, "The ancient spell I did worked! I'm now two inches tall! Now I can explore and have more fun adventures!" 

The dragon cheered and the two of them went off to explore the world! 

The end.

One day, Timmy's mommy surprised him with a new toy truck. It wasn't as big as the one he admired, but it was clear and shiny just like it. Timmy was so happy and played with his new toy truck all day long. He admired it so much that he even slept with it at night. From then on, Timmy knew that sometimes the things we admire aren't always the things we need to be happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little birdie named Billy. Billy loved to fly high up in the sky and sing songs. One day, while flying, he saw a big, noisy bird named Max. Max was giving a lecture to all the animals in the forest. 

Billy flew down to listen to the lecture. But soon, he got bored and started to fly away. Max saw Billy leaving and said, "Hey, little birdie, where are you going? Don't you want to learn something new?"

Billy replied, "I don't like this lecture. It's too noisy and boring. I would rather fly and sing my own songs."

Now the otter was happy again and had plenty of fish to eat. The people who cleaned the river became the otter's friends. They came back to the river often to make sure it stayed clean. And the otter was happy to have new friends and a clean home. The end.

Tiki tried to fly but it couldn't. It didn't even flutter its wings. Tiki sadly looked up and saw a large bird gliding in the sky. "Hey," said Tiki, "Can you help me? I'm stuck here on the ground and can't fly anymore." 

The large bird scoffed. "Flying high is only for big birds, like me," it sneered. "You are too small to soar in the skies." Tiki sadly looked away and never tried to fly again. So its wings stayed broken and it stayed on the ground.

Then, Peter went outside to find something else to eat. He noticed a square cucumber in the garden! He thought it was funny and he asked his mum if she could lend it to him. His mum laughed and said she would gladly lend it to him.

So Peter took his two apples and the square cucumber and went away to find a place to eat them. After he was done he was no longer hungry! 

Peter was so happy that his mum had lent him all the fruits and veggies he wanted to eat. He thanked his mum for being so kind and for lending him her food. His mum smiled and said "You're welcome".

Once upon a time there lived a boy named Max. He was 3 years old and he loved to make things out of pieces of paper.

One day Max was trying to cut a paper bird with his scissors, but the scissors kept slipping. He was getting very frustrated.

"This is no fun," he said, feeling very miserable.

Just then, Max's mom walked in. She smiled at him and said, "Hey Max, why don't you take a break and come put your scissors away?"

Max sighed and nodded. He put his scissors away in the drawer and carefully went to find his mom.

When he found her, they hugged and she said, "I know it's hard to do things sometimes, but don't ever feel awful about it. You can always try again later."

Max knew she was right, and he smiled. He felt much better.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy called John. John was three years old and he really loved to skip. Every day, he would skip around the garden with his friends.

One day, John's dad asked him for help. He wanted John to go and talk to the mechanic about his car. John was a bit troubled, but he agreed to help his dad. The mechanic looked at the car and said he could fix it.

John listened carefully while the mechanic talked and later he skipped happily back home. He couldn't wait to tell his dad the news. When John got home, his dad was sad. He said the mechanic had fixed the car, but it cost too much money. He didn't have enough money to pay the mechanic's bill.

John was very sad and troubled. He sat in the garden and watched as his dad's car drove away. He never skipped again.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Paul. He wanted to go to the hospital. He asked his mom for permission but she said no, so he had a plan.

Paul put rags and hay into a box and then he buried it outside. Then he pretended to be very sick and he said he had a sour stomach. His mom didn't know what to do, so she took him to the hospital.

The hospital doctors checked him out, but they said he was fine. His mom was confused until they remembered the box outside. They dug it up and opened it, and inside they found a toy car. Paul laughed and laughed!

His mom couldn't be mad. She gave him a big hug and told him to never play that game again. So Paul promised and he never did. The end.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Jack and Hank. They loved to play together and explore the world.

One day they were on a big adventure. They were running and jumping and having lots of fun. 

Suddenly, they heard something. Jack said, "what do you think that noise is?"

Hank replied, "I don't know, let's go check it out!"

So, the two friends began walking towards the noise. It was getting louder and louder. 

When they finally reached the source of the noise, they looked around in amazement. It was a tough world with its own rules. There were big rock walls, a river, and a waterfall. It was beautiful.

Jack and Hank couldn't help but smile. It was an amazing place. But then they heard a voice.

"Stop," the voice said. "This world is tough, so be careful."

The two friends listened to the voice, and remembered to be careful. They enjoyed their time in the tough world, but when the sun began to set, Jack and Hank knew it was time to go home.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Katy. Katy lived in a big house with her grandma. One summer day, Katy wanted to explore the garden, but grandma said she had to stay inside. 

"No, I won't let you go out there!" Said grandma

Katy was very sad, but she decided to listen to her grandma. After a while, Katy heard something coming from outside. She got curious and went to the window to have a peak. She saw the wind was blowing gently and the leaves were falling from the trees. 

"Look Katy, the leaves are hidden in the garden! Can you collect them?" Asked grandma.

Katy was so happy about it. She grabbed a basket and went to the garden. Katy collected all the leaves she could find, and she arranged them in different shapes.

The moral of the story is that if we listen to our elders, we can discover ideas and find joy in something as simple as leaves falling from the trees.

Once there was a boy named Joe who was always curious. One night, when his parents were out, Joe decided to get a candle. He found the candle in a drawer and was so excited.

He lit the candle and was amazed to see the flickering light. He wanted to show his friend, so he quickly ran to their house. 

When he got there, his friend said, "wow, Joe, who gave you that candle?" Joe replied, "I got it! I found it in my house!" His friend was surprised, and asked, "Wasn't your mom mad when you got the candle?" Joe felt embarrassed and didn't know what to say. 

His friend came to the rescue and said, "Joe, I think it's ok for you to get a candle, but next time you should ask your mom first." Joe was relieved and was really happy that his friend had helped him. He thanked his friend and said, "I will make sure I ask my mom first next time!"

Lily and Tom were playing in the park. They liked to swing on the swings and slide on the slide. They also liked to hang from the monkey bars and pretend they were monkeys.

One day, they saw a new thing in the park. It was a big rope with a loop at the end. It was hanging from a tree. Lily and Tom wondered what it was for.

"Maybe it is for jumping," Lily said.

"Or for flying," Tom said.

They decided to try it. Lily went first. She put her foot in the loop and pulled the rope. She felt the rope lift her up. She felt happy and excited.

"Look at me, Tom! I am flying!" she shouted.

Tom clapped his hands and cheered. He wanted to try it too. He waited for Lily to come down. But Lily did not come down. She was stuck. The loop was too tight around her foot. She could not get it off. She started to cry.

"Help me, Tom! I am stuck!" she cried.

Tom ran to the tree. He tried to pull the rope. But the rope was too high and too strong. He could not reach it. He felt scared and worried.

"Help! Help!" he yelled.

A man heard them. He was walking his dog in the park. He saw Lily and Tom. He saw the rope. He knew what it was for. It was not for playing. It was for catching animals. It was a trap. He felt angry and sorry.

He ran to the tree. He had a knife. He cut the rope. He freed Lily. He lifted her down. He checked her foot. It was red and sore. But it was not broken. He felt relieved and glad.

"Are you okay, little girl?" he asked.

Lily nodded. She hugged him. She thanked him. She felt safe and grateful.

Tom hugged Lily. He hugged the man. He thanked him too. He felt happy and thankful.

The man smiled. He told them to be careful. He told them not to play with the rope. He told them it was dangerous. He told them it was a trap. He felt kind and helpful.

Lily and Tom felt guilty. They knew they did a bad thing. They knew they should not have played with the rope. They knew they could have been hurt. They felt sorry and ashamed.

They said sorry to the man. They said sorry to each other. They said sorry to the animals. They felt sorry and sorry.

They learned a lesson. They learned to be safe. They learned to be smart. They learned to be good. They felt better and better.

Lily loved to play with her toy boat. She liked to pretend she was a sailor and explore the sea. She had a lovely blue hat and a red scarf that her grandma gave her.

One day, she took her boat to the park and put it in the pond. She watched it sail with the wind and smiled. But then, a big duck came and bit the boat. The boat broke and sank. Lily was very sad and cried.

A boy saw Lily and came to help. He had a tool box and a big smile. He said, "Don't cry, I can fix your boat. I like to fix things. What is your name?"

Lily sniffed and said, "I'm Lily. Thank you for helping me. I love my boat. It was a gift from my grandpa. He was a sailor too."

The boy nodded and said, "I'm Tom. My dad is a sailor. He taught me how to fix boats. Come, let's get your boat out of the water and see what we can do."

Tom and Lily worked together to fix the boat. They used glue, tape, and paint. They made the boat look like new. Lily was very happy and hugged Tom. She said, "You are very kind and smart. You fixed my boat. Do you want to be my friend?"

Tom smiled and said, "Yes, I do. You are very sweet and brave. You love your boat. Do you want to play with me?"

Lily nodded and said, "Yes, I do. Let's play sailors and explore the sea."

They put the boat back in the pond and watched it sail. They had a lot of fun and became good friends. They both had lovely hats and scarves and toy boats. They both loved to be sailors.

Sara liked cream very much. She saw a big jar of cream on the shelf in the kitchen. She wanted to get some cream and eat it. She climbed on a chair and reached for the jar. But the jar was too heavy and slippery. It fell from her hand and broke on the floor. Cream and glass went everywhere.

Sara was scared and sad. She did not know what to do. She heard her mom coming. She knew her mom would be angry. She tried to hide under the table. But her mom saw her and the mess. Her mom was very angry. She shouted at Sara and said she was a bad girl. She said she had to clean up the mess and go to her room. She did not give Sara any hug or kiss.

Sara felt helpless and alone. She cried and cried. She wished she had not tried to get the cream. She wished her mom would love her. She wished she had a friend. But she had no one. She was very unhappy. The end.

Lila and Ben were playing with their new toy, a magic wand that could make things shrink. They had fun making their dolls, cars and books smaller and smaller, and putting them in a shoe box.

"Let's try it on something big!" Ben said. He pointed the wand at the window and said the magic word. "Shrink!"

The window became very small, like a stamp. Lila and Ben gasped. They could see the sky through the tiny hole, but it looked very far away.

"Oops! How do we make it big again?" Lila asked.

"I don't know. Maybe we can find the instructions in the box." Ben said. He ran to the closet where they had left the box. But when he opened the door, he saw that the box was gone.

"Where is it?" he cried.

Lila looked around and saw their cat, Fluffy, playing with something on the floor. It was the box, and it was very fragile. Fluffy had ripped it open with his claws and teeth, and had scattered the pieces all over the carpet.

"Fluffy, no!" Lila shouted. She ran to the cat and tried to grab the box, but it was too late. Fluffy had chewed up the instructions and swallowed them.

Lila and Ben looked at each other in horror. They had no way to fix the window, and no way to make their toys big again. They had ruined everything with their magic wand. They started to cry.

Ben and Lily went to the zoo with Mom and Dad. They saw many animals, like lions, monkeys, and giraffes. But Ben and Lily wanted to see the penguins most of all. They liked how the penguins looked, with their black and white feathers and their funny beaks.

"Can we go to the penguins now?" Ben asked Mom.

"Not yet, sweetie. We have to wait for the bell to ring. Then the penguins will come out and swim and play," Mom said.

Ben and Lily were impatient. They did not like to wait. They wanted to see the penguins right away. They looked at the big clock on the wall. It showed the time. It was almost time for the bell to ring.

"Come on, come on, hurry up, clock!" Lily said.

"Maybe we can make the bell ring faster if we clap our hands," Ben said.

They started to clap their hands loudly. They hoped the bell would hear them and ring sooner. But the bell did not ring. It was still quiet.

"Maybe the bell is broken," Ben said.

"Maybe the penguins are sleeping," Lily said.

They felt sad. They thought they would not see the penguins today.

But then, they heard a loud sound. It was the bell! It rang and rang and rang. Ben and Lily jumped up and down. They were happy. The bell was not broken. The penguins were not sleeping.

"Let's go, let's go, let's go!" they shouted.

They ran to the penguin pool with Mom and Dad. They saw the penguins come out of their house. They saw them slide on the ice, dive in the water, and chase each other. They saw them flap their wings, shake their tails, and make funny noises.

Ben and Lily laughed and clapped. They loved the penguins. They watched them for a long time. They forgot about the clock and the bell. They only cared about the penguins. They had a lot of fun at the zoo.

Lily and Ben were friends who liked to play outside. They had a big ball that was orange and black. It was a basketball. They liked to bounce it and throw it and catch it.

One day, they saw a big hoop on a pole near the park. It was very high. Lily and Ben wanted to try to put the ball in the hoop. They thought it would be fun.

They took turns to bounce the ball and jump. They tried to reach the hoop, but it was too high. They could not put the ball in the hoop. They felt sad.

Then, they saw a friendly dog running towards them. It was brown and white and had a long tail. It was harmless. It wanted to play with them. It barked and wagged its tail.

"Hi, doggy!" Lily said. "Do you want to play with us?"

The dog nodded and licked Lily's face. It made her giggle. Ben threw the ball and the dog ran after it. It caught the ball in its mouth and brought it back. It dropped the ball and waited for Ben to throw it again.

Lily and Ben smiled. They forgot about the hoop. They had fun playing with the dog and the ball. They made a new friend. They were happy.

Lily and Max were playing in the snow. They made a snowman and a snow fort. They threw snowballs at each other and laughed. They were having fun.

But then the sky became dark and the wind became cold. Lily and Max felt cold too. They needed to go inside. They looked for their cabin. Their cabin was huge and warm. It had a fireplace and a sofa and a big bed.

But they could not see their cabin. They only saw trees and snow. They were lost. They were scared. They hugged each other and cried.

"Where is our cabin?" Lily asked.

"I don't know," Max said. "Maybe we walked too far. Maybe we should shout for help."

They shouted as loud as they could. "Help! Help! We are lost! We need our cabin!"

But no one heard them. They shouted again and again. But no one came.

They were about to give up when they heard a bark. They looked up and saw a dog. The dog was big and furry. It had a collar and a tag. It said "Rex".

"Hello, Rex," Lily said. "Can you help us? Can you find our cabin?"

Rex wagged his tail and barked. He sniffed the air and ran. Lily and Max followed him. They hoped he knew the way.

Rex ran fast and smart. He followed the tracks and the signs. He led them to their cabin. He barked and scratched the door.

Lily and Max saw their cabin. They were so happy. They ran to the door and opened it. They saw their mom and dad. They were so worried.

"Lily! Max! Where were you?" their mom and dad said. "We were looking for you. We were so scared."

"We were playing in the snow. But then we got lost. We could not find our cabin. We needed help. But then Rex came. He helped us. He found our cabin. He is a good dog," Lily and Max said.

They hugged their mom and dad. They thanked Rex. They gave him a treat and a pat. They went inside their cabin. They warmed up by the fireplace. They cuddled on the sofa. They felt safe and cozy.

They learned a lesson. They should not go too far from their cabin. They should always stay together. They should always listen to their mom and dad. And they should always be nice to Rex. He was their hero. He was their friend.

Ella and Ben were twins who liked to play outside. They had a big yard with a swing, a slide and a sandbox. They also had a dog named Spot who was very friendly and liked to chase balls.

One morning, Ella and Ben woke up very early. They looked out the window and saw the sky was pink and orange. They knew it was sunrise, when the sun comes up and makes the day bright. They wanted to see the sunrise better, so they put on their shoes and ran outside.

They saw the sun peeking over the hills and shining on the flowers and the grass. They felt the warm air and heard the birds singing. They smiled and said, "Wow, the sunrise is so pretty!"

They decided to play on the swing and the slide, and they called Spot to join them. They had a lot of fun, until they heard a loud scream from the house. They stopped and looked at each other, scared. They wondered who was screaming and why.

They ran back to the house and saw their grandma standing on the porch. She was elderly, with white hair and glasses. She looked angry and scared. She pointed at the kitchen and said, "There's a mouse in the kitchen! It ran under the table and scared me! Help me get rid of it!"

Ella and Ben looked at each other and giggled. They thought a mouse was not so scary, but they knew their grandma did not like them. They said, "Don't worry, grandma, we'll help you. Come on, Spot, let's catch the mouse!"

They ran into the kitchen, followed by Spot, who barked and wagged his tail. They looked under the table and saw a small brown mouse with a long tail. It squeaked and ran away, but Spot was faster. He chased the mouse and caught it in his mouth. He brought it back to Ella and Ben, who praised him and petted him.

They showed the mouse to their grandma, who said, "Thank you, Ella and Ben, and thank you, Spot. You are very brave and smart. Now, please take the mouse outside and let it go. I don't want it in my house!"

They nodded and said, "Okay, grandma, we will. But can we have some breakfast first? We are hungry from playing and helping."

Their grandma smiled and said, "Of course, you can. You deserve some pancakes and juice. Come on, let's go to the dining room. And don't forget to wash your hands!"

They washed their hands and went to the dining room, where they ate their pancakes and juice. They told their grandma about the sunrise and how beautiful it was. They asked her if she wanted to see it with them next time. She said, "Maybe, if you wake me up gently and not with a scream!"

They laughed and hugged their grandma. They said, "We love you, grandma, and we love the sunrise. And we love Spot, too. He's a good dog."

They finished their breakfast and went outside again, with Spot. They let the mouse go in the grass, where it ran away. They waved goodbye to the mouse and said, "Have a nice day, mouse. And don't come back to our house!"

They played some more on the swing and the slide, and watched the sun go higher in the sky. They felt happy and proud. They had a good morning.

Tom and Mia are twins. They like to play in the park with their mom and dad. They have a big blanket to sit on and eat snacks. They also have a ball, a kite and some books.

One day, they see a big dog in the park. The dog is brown and furry. It looks tough and strong. It runs fast and barks loud. Tom and Mia are scared of the dog. They rush to their mom and dad and hide behind the blanket.

"Mom, dad, help! There is a big dog!" Tom cries.

"Shh, it's okay. The dog won't hurt you. He is just playing," mom says.

"But he is so big and tough. He might bite us," Mia says.

"No, he won't. He is a friendly dog. He just wants to say hello. Look, he has a collar and a leash. His owner is over there. He is calling him," dad says.

Tom and Mia peek from behind the blanket. They see a man waving and whistling. The dog hears him and runs to him. The man pets the dog and puts the leash on him. He smiles and walks away.

"See? The dog is gone. He was not mean. He was just curious. Do you want to play some more?" mom asks.

Tom and Mia nod. They feel better. They come out from behind the blanket. They pick up their ball, their kite and their books. They play in the park with their mom and dad. They have fun. They are not scared of the dog anymore.

Lily and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys in their room. Sometimes they share, sometimes they fight. One day, they find a big blanket in the closet. It is soft and warm and has many colors.

"Wow, look at this blanket!" Lily says. "It is so pretty! I want to use it for my dolls."

"No, I want to use it for my cars!" Ben says. "It is so big! I can make a road with it."

They both pull the blanket and try to take it. The blanket makes a loud rip sound. Lily and Ben stop and look at the blanket. It has a big hole in the middle. They feel sad and sorry.

"Mommy, mommy!" they cry. "We broke the blanket!"

Mommy comes to their room and sees the blanket. She is not happy. She asks them what they did.

"We wanted to play with the blanket, but we fought over it and ripped it," Lily says.

"We are sorry, mommy," Ben says.

Mommy sighs and hugs them. She says, "I know you are sorry, but you have to learn to be generous. Generous means you share and care for others. The blanket was a gift from grandma. She made it with love for you. She was generous to give you the blanket. How do you think she would feel if she saw the blanket now?"

Lily and Ben think about grandma. They love grandma. They don't want to make her sad.

"We feel bad, mommy," Lily says. "We want to make grandma happy."

"Can we fix the blanket, mommy?" Ben asks.

Mommy smiles and says, "Yes, we can try to fix the blanket. But first, you have to say sorry to each other and promise to be generous from now on."

Lily and Ben hug each other and say sorry. They promise to be generous and share the blanket. Mommy gets some needles and threads and helps them sew the hole. The blanket is not as good as before, but it is still soft and warm and has many colors. Lily and Ben thank mommy and say they love her. They also make a card for grandma and say they love her and are sorry for the blanket. They hope she will forgive them and be proud of them. They are happy to be generous.

Sara was a dancer who loved to shine. She wore a pink dress and pink shoes and danced with joy. She liked to show off her moves and make everyone look at her.

One day, she went to a big dance show with other dancers. She wanted to be the best and the brightest. She did not care about the other dancers. She pushed and bumped them to get to the front. She did not say sorry or smile.

The other dancers were sad and angry. They did not want to dance with Sara. They moved away from her and left her alone. Sara felt lonely and confused. She did not understand why they did not like her.

Then, she saw a little girl in the audience. The girl was wearing a pink dress and pink shoes, just like Sara. But the girl was not happy. She was crying. Sara asked her why she was crying. The girl said that she wanted to be a dancer, but she had hurt her leg and could not dance. She said that she loved to watch the other dancers, but Sara had blocked her view and made them unhappy.

Sara felt sorry for the girl. She realized that she had been selfish and rude. She wanted to make the girl happy. She gave her a hug and a smile. She asked the other dancers to join her. She said that she was sorry and that she wanted to share the dance with them. The other dancers forgave her and welcomed her. They danced together in a circle, with Sara and the girl in the middle. They all shone with joy and friendship.

The moral of the story is that being a good dancer is not only about being bright and beautiful, but also about being kind and respectful. Sharing and caring make everyone happy.
