Ben had a parrot named Polly. Polly was a good parrot. She could talk and sing and make funny noises. Ben loved Polly very much.

One day, Ben and Polly were playing in the backyard. Ben threw a ball and Polly flew after it. But Polly flew too fast and hit a tree. Polly fell to the ground and cried. Ben ran to Polly and picked her up.

"Polly, are you okay?" Ben asked. He saw that Polly had a cut on her wing. It was red and hurt. Ben felt sad and scared.

"Polly hurt, Polly hurt!" Polly said. She was in pain and scared too.

Ben hugged Polly and said, "Don't worry, Polly. I will help you. We will go to the vet. The vet will make you better. You are my best friend, Polly. I love you."

Ben took Polly inside and told his mom what happened. His mom said, "Oh, poor Polly. Let's go to the vet right away. He will fix Polly's wing. You are a good boy, Ben. You care for Polly."

Ben and his mom got in the car and drove to the vet. The vet was a nice man. He looked at Polly's wing and said, "Polly has a small cut. It is not bad. I will clean it and put a bandage on it. Polly will be fine. She just needs some rest and love."

The vet cleaned Polly's wing and put a bandage on it. He gave Polly a treat and said, "You are a brave parrot, Polly. You will heal soon. You have a good friend, Ben. He loves you."

Polly smiled and said, "Thank you, vet. Thank you, Ben. I love you too."

Ben and his mom took Polly home. Ben put Polly in her cage and gave her some water and food. He said, "Polly, you are my best friend. I am sorry you got hurt. I will never quit playing with you. I will always be with you."

Polly said, "Ben, you are my best friend too. I am happy you helped me. I will never quit talking to you. I will always love you."

Tom and Lily were at the beach with their mom and dad. They liked to play in the sand and splash in the water. They saw a big boat with a funny name: Ancient Shark. They asked their dad what it meant.

"It's a boat that looks for old things under the sea. Things that were there a long time ago, before we were born. Like pots and coins and bones. They are called ancient things," dad explained.

"Can we go on the boat, dad? Please?" Tom and Lily begged.

"Sorry, kids. The boat is not for visitors. It's only for people who work there. They have special tools and machines to find the ancient things. Like this one," dad pointed to a hose that was attached to the boat. "It can spray water very hard and make the sand move away."

Tom and Lily were curious. They wanted to see how the hose worked. They waited until dad was busy talking to mom and sneaked to the boat. They climbed on the deck and found the hose. Tom turned the knob and the hose started to spray water everywhere.

"Wow, this is fun!" Tom shouted.

"Be careful, Tom! You might break something!" Lily warned.

But Tom did not listen. He sprayed the water at the boat, at the sand, at the sky. He sprayed the water at a big metal box that was on the boat. The box had a lock on it, but the water was so strong that it broke the lock and opened the box.

Inside the box, there was something that made Tom and Lily scream. It was a big, gray, scary shark. It had sharp teeth and a fin. It was not alive, but it looked very real. It was an ancient shark that the boat people had found under the sea.

"Help! Help!" Tom and Lily cried.

The boat people heard them and ran to the deck. They saw the hose, the box, and the shark. They were very angry.

"What are you doing here? How did you get on the boat? Do you know how much this shark is worth? It's a rare fossil! You could have damaged it!" one of them yelled.

Tom and Lily were very sorry. They did not mean to cause trouble. They just wanted to see the hose. They apologized to the boat people and ran back to their dad and mom. They told them what happened and promised to never go on the boat again.

Dad and mom were not happy. They scolded Tom and Lily for being naughty and dangerous. They said they had to respect other people's work and property. They said they had to be more careful and listen to them.

Tom and Lily felt bad. They learned their lesson. They said they were sorry and hugged their dad and mom. They decided to play in the sand and splash in the water instead. They did not want to see the ancient shark ever again.

Lily and Tom were playing in the park with their ball. They liked to kick the ball to each other and run after it. They were having fun and laughing.

But then a big dog came. The dog was barking and running towards them. Lily and Tom were scared. They thought the dog was a threat. They dropped the ball and ran away.

"Help! Help!" they shouted. "The dog is coming!"

A man heard them and came to see. He was the dog's owner. He saw the ball and picked it up. He called the dog and gave it the ball.

"Don't be afraid," he said to Lily and Tom. "The dog is not a threat. He just wanted to play with the ball. He is friendly and gentle. See, he is wagging his tail."

Lily and Tom stopped running and looked at the dog. The dog was licking the ball and wagging his tail. He did not look angry or mean. He looked happy and playful.

"Can we play with him?" Lily asked.

"Sure, you can," the man said. "His name is Rex. He likes to share his ball. You can throw it and he will fetch it. He is a good dog."

Lily and Tom smiled. They went closer to the dog and petted him. He licked their hands and nuzzled their faces. He was soft and warm.

"Hello, Rex," they said. "We are sorry we were scared of you. You are a nice dog."

They played with Rex and the ball for a while. They threw the ball and he brought it back. They praised him and gave him hugs. They were having fun and laughing again.

After a while, they got tired and thirsty. They said goodbye to Rex and the man. They thanked them for the ball and the play.

They went to the bench where their mom was waiting. She had a bottle of juice and some cookies for them.

"Did you have fun?" she asked.

"Yes, we did," they said. "We played with a dog. His name is Rex. He was not a threat. He was friendly and gentle. He shared his ball with us. He was a good dog."

"That's wonderful," mom said. "I'm glad you made a new friend. Here, have some juice and cookies. They are sweet and yummy."

They took the juice and cookies and ate them. They were sweet and yummy. They felt happy and relaxed.

They drank the juice and ate the cookies. But one cookie was sour. Lily made a face and spit it out.

"Yuck!" she said. "This cookie is sour. It tastes bad."

Mom looked at the cookie and saw it was green and fuzzy. It was moldy.

"Oh, no," she said. "This cookie is bad. It is a threat. It can make you sick. Don't eat it. Throw it away."

She took the cookie and threw it in the trash. She checked the other cookies and saw they were good. She gave Lily and Tom another cookie each.

"Here, have these cookies. They are good. They are not sour. They taste good."

They took the cookies and ate them. They were good. They were not sour. They tasted good.

They finished the juice and cookies and smiled. They felt happy and relaxed.

They hugged mom and said, "Thank you, mom. You are the best."

Mom hugged them back and said, "You are welcome, my loves. You are the best, too."

Lily was anxious. She did not like the deep end of the pool. It was dark and scary. She could not see the bottom. She did not know what was there. She was afraid of diving.

Lila and Ben were twins who liked to play in the forest. They were not afraid of anything, not even the big wolf who lived there. They thought the wolf was funny and friendly, and they often gave him some of their food.

One day, they found a big basket of cookies and pies in the forest. They were very hungry and wanted to eat them all. But the wolf came and said, "Hello, little ones. Can I have some of your food? I am very hungry too."

Lila and Ben did not want to share. They said, "No, wolf. These are our food. You can find your own food. Go away!"

The wolf was sad and angry. He said, "That is not nice. You should share with others who need help. If you do not share, I will order you to give me your food. And if you do not obey, I will eat you!"

Lila and Ben laughed. They said, "You cannot order us. You are not our boss. And you cannot eat us. You are too old and slow. We are faster and smarter. You are a disgusting wolf. Go away!"

The wolf was very sad and angry. He said, "You are very rude and mean. You will see what happens when you do not share and respect others. I will teach you a lesson."

The wolf waited until Lila and Ben were busy eating the cookies and pies. Then he sneaked behind them and grabbed them by their clothes. He dragged them to his cave and locked them inside. He said, "Now you will stay here until you learn to share and respect others. And maybe I will eat you later."

Lila and Ben were very scared and sorry. They said, "Please, wolf, let us go. We are sorry for being rude and mean. We will share with you and respect you. Please, wolf, forgive us."

The wolf said, "I will think about it. But first, you have to promise me something. You have to promise me that you will never be rude and mean to anyone again. And you have to promise me that you will always share and respect others. Do you promise?"

Lila and Ben said, "Yes, wolf, we promise. We promise with all our heart. Please, wolf, let us go."

The wolf said, "OK, I will let you go. But you have to keep your promise. And you have to give me some of your food. And you have to be my friends. Do you agree?"

Lila and Ben said, "Yes, wolf, we agree. We will give you some of our food. And we will be your friends. Thank you, wolf, for being kind and forgiving."

The wolf said, "You are welcome, little ones. Come, let us eat together and be friends."

The wolf opened the cave and let Lila and Ben out. They gave him some of their cookies and pies, and they ate together and talked. They became friends and learned to share and respect each other. They never forgot the lesson that the wolf taught them.

The moral of the story is: You should share and respect others who need help. You should not be rude and mean to anyone. You should not judge others by their appearance. You should be kind and forgiving. You should make friends with different kinds of people.

"Look, mom, look!" Tom said. "That swan is stretching its neck so high!"

"Yes, it is," mom said. "Do you know why?"

Tom shook his head. He wanted to know.

"Swans stretch their necks to show their mates how much they love them," mom said. "They also stretch their necks to scare away other birds that might bother them."

Tom thought that was cool. He wanted to stretch his neck too. He tried to imitate the swan, but he could not reach as high. He felt silly.

Lily laughed at Tom. She pointed at him and said, "You look funny, Tom. You are not a swan. You are a boy."

Tom felt sad. He did not like Lily laughing at him. He stopped stretching his neck.

Mom saw Tom's face. She hugged him and said, "Don't mind Lily, Tom. She is just teasing you. You can stretch your neck if you want to. It is good to be curious and try new things. You can learn a lot from the swans and other animals. But you should also be proud of who you are. You are a wonderful boy, and I love you very much."

Mom nodded. She said, "That's right, Tom. You are a boy, and you are beautiful and smart too. And so is Lily. She is a girl, and she is beautiful and smart too. We are all different, but we are all special. And we can all stretch our necks in our own way."

Tom and Lily looked at each other. They said sorry for being mean. They hugged and said, "We love you, mom. And we love each other. And we love the swans."

Mom smiled. She said, "I love you too, Tom and Lily. And I love the swans. They are old and wise. They can teach us a lot about love and respect. Let's watch them for a while, and then we can go home and stretch our necks some more."

Lily was a little girl who liked to chew on everything. She chewed on her toys, her books, her clothes, and even her hair. Her mom and dad always told her to stop chewing, but she did not listen. She thought chewing was fun and tasty.

One day, Lily saw her mom's cup of coffee on the table. She was curious and wanted to try it. She climbed on a chair and reached for the cup. She took a big sip and then spit it out. It was hot and bitter and made her tongue hurt. She started to cry and ran to her mom.

"Mommy, mommy, what is this?" she sobbed, pointing at the cup.

"That's coffee, Lily. It's a drink for grown-ups, not for kids. You should not touch it or drink it. It can make you sick and burn your mouth. Why did you drink it?" her mom asked, hugging her.

"I wanted to chew it, mommy. I chew everything. It looked ordinary, like water or juice. But it was not. It was yucky and ouchy. I'm sorry, mommy. I won't chew on things anymore. I learned my lesson." Lily said, wiping her tears.

Her mom smiled and kissed her. "I'm glad you learned your lesson, Lily. Chewing on things can be dangerous and bad for your teeth. You should only chew on food or gum. And you should always ask before you try something new. There are many things in the world that are not ordinary, and you need to be careful and respectful. Do you understand?" she said.

"Yes, mommy. I understand. I love you, mommy. Can I have some water, please?" Lily said.

"Of course, sweetie. I love you too. Here's some water. And maybe later we can have some cookies. But only if you promise not to chew on them too hard." her mom said, laughing.

Lily nodded and smiled. She drank some water and felt better. She decided to chew on things less and to listen to her mom more. She realized that chewing was not always fun and tasty, and that coffee was not ordinary at all. She learned a valuable lesson that day.

At the hospital, a nurse came to take her to a room. She wore a white dress and a funny hat. She smiled at Lily and said, "Hello, Lily. I'm Nurse Anna. I'm here to help you. You are a very brave and beautiful girl. Do you want to speak to me?"

Lily shook her head. She hid her face in her teddy bear. She did not want to speak to Nurse Anna. She did not want to speak to anyone.

Nurse Anna did not give up. She said, "Lily, I know you are scared. But the operation is not so bad. It will be over soon. And then you will feel much better. You will be able to play and run and laugh again. And you will have a special bandage on your arm. Do you want to see it?"

Lily peeked at Nurse Anna. She saw a bandage with colorful stickers on it. She liked stickers. She liked colors. She wondered what the bandage was for.

She said, "What is that?"

Nurse Anna said, "This is your bandage. You will wear it after the operation. It will protect your arm and make it heal faster. And it will look very pretty. Do you want to choose a sticker for it?"

Lily nodded. She liked to choose things. She looked at the stickers. There were stars and hearts and flowers and animals. She saw a pink bunny. She liked bunnies. She said, "I want that one."

Nurse Anna said, "That's a good choice. The pink bunny is very cute. Do you want to put it on the bandage?"

Lily said, "Yes, please."

Nurse Anna helped Lily put the sticker on the bandage. She said, "There. Now you have a beautiful bandage. And you know what? You can have more stickers after the operation. You can decorate your bandage as much as you want. How does that sound?"

Lily smiled. She liked the idea of having more stickers. She liked the idea of having a beautiful bandage. She felt a little less scared. She said, "Thank you, Nurse Anna. You are very nice."

Nurse Anna said, "You're welcome, Lily. You are very nice too. And very brave. And very beautiful. Are you ready to go to the operation?"

Lily said, "Yes, I think so."

She held her teddy bear and her bandage. She looked at her mom and dad. They hugged her and kissed her and said they loved her. They said they would be waiting for her. They said everything would be okay.

Lily said, "I love you too. I'll see you soon."

She went with Nurse Anna to the operation. She was still scared, but she was also curious. She wondered what the operation would be like. She wondered what the doctor would say. She wondered what stickers she would get.

She hoped it would not hurt too much. She hoped it would make her well. She hoped she would be able to play and run and laugh again.

She hoped she would have a beautiful bandage.

Tom was a big rat who liked to live in the dark. He did not like the sun, because it made his eyes hurt. He only came out at night, when he could find food and play with his friends.

One night, Tom saw something shiny in a trash can. He was curious, so he climbed up and looked inside. He saw a shiny ball that looked like a small sun. He wanted to touch it, but it was too high. He jumped and jumped, but he could not reach it.

"Hey, Tom, what are you doing?" asked Sam, another rat who came by.

"I want to touch the shiny ball," said Tom.

"That's not a ball, that's a trap!" said Sam. "It's a trick to catch rats like us. If you touch it, it will snap and hurt you. Come on, let's go away."

But Tom did not listen. He was too stubborn and greedy. He jumped one more time, and this time he reached the shiny ball. But as soon as he touched it, he heard a loud snap and felt a sharp pain. The shiny ball was a trap, and it closed around his paw. He was stuck and helpless.

"Help! Help!" he cried. "It hurts! It hurts!"

Sam heard his cries and ran back. He saw Tom in the trap and felt sorry for him. He tried to open the trap, but it was too strong. He could not help him.

"I'm sorry, Tom," he said. "I tried to warn you, but you did not listen. Now you are in trouble. Maybe someone will come and free you, but I have to go. It's almost dawn, and the sun will shine soon. I don't want to be seen by the big people. Goodbye, Tom."

Sam left, and Tom was alone. He wished he had listened to Sam. He wished he had not been so curious and greedy. He wished he had not touched the shiny ball. He was scared and sad. He did not know what would happen to him. He hoped someone would come and help him, but he did not see anyone. He only saw the sky getting brighter and brighter, and the sun starting to shine.

But when she got home, her mom was not there. She had gone to the store to buy some food. There was a note on the table that said: "Back soon. Love, Mom." Lila felt sad. She wanted to share her gem with her mom. She took it out of her pocket and looked at it. It was still shiny and pretty, but it did not make her happy anymore.

She decided to wait for her mom on the porch. She sat on the steps and held her gem in her hand. She saw a boy walking by. He had a big smile and a ball. He looked at her and said: "Hi, I'm Sam. Do you want to play with me?"

Lila looked at him and then at her gem. She thought for a moment. She liked her gem, but she also liked to play. She remembered that her mom always said: "Sharing is caring." She smiled and said: "Hi, I'm Lila. Sure, I want to play with you. Do you want to see my gem?"

Sam nodded and came closer. He looked at her gem and said: "Wow, that's a beautiful gem. Where did you find it?"

Lila told him about her skipping and finding the gem in the grass. She said: "It's my lucky gem. But I don't need it right now. You can have it if you want. I have something else that's lucky."

Sam looked surprised and said: "Really? What is it?"

Lila pointed to her mom, who had just arrived from the store. She said: "My mom. She's the best. She's always there for me. She's always available."

Sam smiled and said: "You're right. Your mom is lucky. And so are you. And so am I. Thank you for the gem. It's very nice of you. Can I give you something in return?"

Lila nodded and said: "Sure. What do you have?"

Sam said: "I have this ball. It's my favorite. It bounces high and far. Do you want to try it?"

Lila said: "Yes, please. That sounds fun."

Sam gave her the ball and they started to play. They bounced the ball, threw the ball, and caught the ball. They laughed and had a good time. They became friends.

Lila's mom watched them from the porch. She smiled and felt proud of her daughter. She knew that Lila had learned a valuable lesson. She had learned that skipping was fun, but sharing was even better.

Lily and Ben were playing with their toy bow and arrow in the garden. They liked to pretend they were brave hunters, chasing rabbits and birds. Lily had a red bow and Ben had a blue one. They took turns to shoot the arrow at a big tree.

"Look, I hit the tree!" Lily said, pointing at the arrow stuck in the bark.

"That's easy, I can do that too!" Ben said, pulling back his bow.

But Ben did not aim well. His arrow flew past the tree and hit the window of the house. CRASH! The window broke into many pieces.

"Oh no!" Lily and Ben said together. They ran to the house to see what happened.

They saw their mom standing in the kitchen, looking very angry. She had a broom in her hand and was sweeping the glass.

"What did you do?" she asked them, frowning.

"We're sorry, mom, it was an accident!" Lily said.

"Ben shot the arrow and it broke the window!" Ben said.

Mom shook her head. "You should not play with the arrow near the house. It is dangerous and messy. You could hurt yourself or someone else. Now you have to help me clean up this mess. And no more bow and arrow for today. Go and shut your toys in the box."

Lily and Ben felt bad. They knew they had done something wrong. They helped mom pick up the glass and put it in the bin. Then they shut their bow and arrow in the box and said sorry to mom again.

Mom hugged them and said, "I know you didn't mean to break the window, but you have to be careful and listen to me. Next time, play with the arrow far away from the house, OK?"

Lily and Ben nodded. They learned their lesson. They decided to play with something else, like their ball or their bike. They hoped mom would let them use the bow and arrow again soon.

One day, he found a very unusual bug. It was big and shiny and had many colors. It looked like a rainbow. Tom was very happy and put the bug in his jar. He wanted to show it to his friends and family.

But the bug was not happy. It did not like being in the jar. It wanted to be free and go back to the garden. It tried to escape, but the jar was too tight. It felt sad and scared.

The next day, Tom saw that the bug had changed. It was not shiny and colorful anymore. It was dull and gray. It did not move or make noises. It looked sick and weak. Tom felt sorry for the bug. He realized he had been selfish and cruel. He decided to let the bug go.

He opened the jar and gently took the bug out. He carried it to the garden and placed it on a flower. The bug felt the sun and the breeze and the smell of the flower. It felt happy and grateful. It started to glow and sparkle again. It thanked Tom and flew away.

Tom learned a lesson. He learned that bugs are not toys. They are living things that have feelings and needs. He learned to respect and care for them. He decided to not keep bugs in jars anymore. He decided to watch them in the garden and learn from them. He felt good and wise.

Lily wanted to play with the cane too. She was jealous of Ben. She said, "No, I want to be the pirate. You can be the parrot. Give me the cane, or I'll tickle you!"

They started to tug on the cane, pulling it back and forth. They did not see their grandma coming into the room. She was using a cane to walk, because her legs were old and sore. She saw the twins fighting over her cane. She said, "Hey, hey, hey, what are you doing with my cane? That's not a toy, that's my helper. Give it back to me, please."

Ben and Lily stopped fighting. They felt sorry for taking their grandma's cane. They said, "Sorry, grandma. We didn't know it was yours. We thought it was a toy. Here, you can have it back."

But next time, ask me before you take something that belongs to me. And remember to share your toys with each other. How about we play a game together? I can be the pirate, and you can be my crew. How does that sound?"

Mia is not happy. She says, "I lose. I have less scores."

Tom sees that Mia is not happy. He wants to be a good friend. He says, "You played well. You said many numbers right. You can have one of my scores."

But, Whiskers stretched too far and knocked the bowl off the table. The milk spilled all over the floor and made a big mess. Whiskers was sad that she couldn't drink the milk and that she made a mess. 

The family was angry and they decided to give Whiskers away to another home where she could learn how to behave. Whiskers was very sad that she couldn't stay with her family anymore. The end.

As Timmy splashed in the puddle, he saw a rat running by. "Look, Mommy! A rat!" he shouted. His mom quickly picked him up and said, "Rats are not our friends. They can be dangerous."

After a while, Timmy got tired and they sat on a bench. His mom showed him a fragile flower and said, "This flower is delicate and needs to be taken care of." Timmy looked at the flower and said, "It's pretty, but it could break easily." 

As they walked home, Timmy thought about the rat and the flower. He realized that some things are not meant to be played with, and some things need to be treated gently.

Lily and Ben run from bush to bush, looking for the biggest and ripest blueberries. They pop some in their mouths and some in their baskets. They laugh and sing as they pick.

But then, Lily sees something that makes her pause. She sees a fat, furry animal hiding under a bush. It has a black nose, a long tail, and sharp teeth. It is a raccoon!

Lily is scared of the raccoon. She drops her basket and runs to Mom and Dad. She cries, "Mom, Dad, there is a raccoon! It wants to eat our blueberries!"

Mom and Dad come to see what is wrong. They see the raccoon, too. They are not scared. They say, "Don't worry, Lily. The raccoon is not going to hurt you. He is just hungry, like you. He likes blueberries, too. Let's share some with him."

They take some blueberries from their baskets and toss them to the raccoon. The raccoon sniffs them and then eats them happily. He wags his tail and makes a soft noise. He says thank you in his own way.

Lily and Ben smile. They are not scared anymore. They think the raccoon is cute and funny. They say, "You're welcome, raccoon. Enjoy the blueberries. We have enough for everyone."

They pick up their baskets and go back to picking blueberries. They have a fun and friendly day in the field.

Lily and Ben were friends who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big red pepper on a bench. Lily wanted to eat it, but Ben said no.

"That pepper is not for us. It is for someone else. Maybe it is spicy and will hurt our mouths. Let's play with the ball instead," Ben said.

But Lily did not listen. She was curious and hungry. She took the pepper and bit it. It was very spicy and hot. Lily felt a fire in her mouth and tears in her eyes. She spit out the pepper and shouted.

"Ow, ow, ow! This pepper is bad! It hurts me! Help, help!" Lily cried.

Ben ran to her and tried to help. He gave her some water and hugged her. He was sorry for his friend. He wanted to make her feel better.

But then, a man came to the bench. He was angry and scary. He had a big beard and a loud voice. He saw the pepper on the ground and Lily and Ben.

"Hey, you little thieves! That was my pepper! You stole it from me! How dare you! I will teach you a lesson!" the man shouted.

He grabbed the pepper and threw it at Lily and Ben. It hit Lily on the head and Ben on the chest. They both fell down and cried. The man laughed and walked away.

Lily and Ben were hurt and sad. They wished they had never seen the pepper. They learned that some things are different and not good for them. They also learned to listen to each other and not take what is not theirs. They hoped someone would come and help them. But no one did. They were alone and scared in the park. The end.

But Tom and Spot didn't listen. They chased the rabbit across the field, towards the pond. Anna ran after them, hoping to stop them. She was scared and worried.

Tommy loved his mother very much. She was kind and humble and always helped him. She taught him how to pray every night before bed. She said that praying was talking to God and asking him for good things.

One day, Tommy's mother got very sick. She had to go to the hospital and stay there for a long time. Tommy was sad and scared. He missed his mother and wanted her to come home. He prayed every night for her to get better.

One night, Tommy heard a knock on the door. He ran to open it and saw his father. His father had a big smile on his face and a surprise behind his back. He said, "Tommy, I have some good news for you. Your mother is coming home tomorrow. She is feeling much better. And I have a gift for you from her."

Tommy was so happy that he hugged his father and jumped up and down. He wondered what the gift was. His father showed him a small box wrapped in shiny paper. He said, "Your mother made this for you while she was in the hospital. She said it was a special way to say thank you for your prayers."

Tommy opened the box and saw a beautiful necklace with a cross pendant. He recognized it as the one his mother always wore. He felt a warm feeling in his heart. He said, "Thank you, father. Thank you, mother. Thank you, God. I love you all."

He put the necklace around his neck and felt his mother's love. He prayed again and thanked God for his mother's recovery and his father's support. He felt happy and peaceful. Lily liked to look at the stars at night. She wondered what they were and how far they were. One night, she saw a bright light in the sky. It was a comet, her dad told her. A comet was a big rock that flew very fast and had a long tail.

"Wow, it's so pretty!" Lily said. "Can we send it a message?"

Her dad smiled and hugged her. "How do you want to send it a message?" he asked.

Lily thought for a moment. She ran to her room and came back with a flashlight. She turned it on and off, making dots and dashes. She was trying to use Morse code, a way of talking with lights that her dad had taught her.

"I'm saying hello, comet. I'm Lily. I hope you are not troubled," she said.

Her dad was impressed by her effort. He helped her with the code and said, "That's very kind of you, Lily. Maybe the comet will hear you and be happy."

They watched the comet for a while, until it disappeared behind the clouds. Lily felt a warm feeling in her heart. She hoped the comet was not troubled, and that it would come back someday. She said good night to the stars and the comet, and went to bed with a smile.

Lily and Ben were best friends. They liked to play in the park with their toys. One day, they saw a big red balloon tied to a bench. It looked very high and shiny.

"Wow, look at that balloon!" Lily said. "I want to touch it!"

"Me too!" Ben said. "Let's go and get it!"

They ran to the bench and tried to reach the balloon. But it was too high for them. They jumped and stretched, but they could not touch it.

"Maybe we can use this stick," Lily said. She picked up a long stick from the ground and tried to poke the balloon. But the stick was too short.

"Maybe we can use this rock," Ben said. He picked up a big rock and tried to throw it at the balloon. But the rock was too heavy.

They were about to give up, when they saw a man walking towards them. He was holding a big bag of candy.

"Hello, kids," the man said. "Do you like candy?"

"Yes, we do!" Lily and Ben said.

"I have a reward for you," the man said. "If you can squeeze this balloon and make it pop, I will give you some candy."

Lily and Ben were very excited. They wanted the candy and the balloon. They took the balloon from the man and tried to squeeze it. But it was very hard and did not pop.

"Try harder," the man said. "You can do it!"

Lily and Ben squeezed harder and harder. They did not notice that the man was smiling in a bad way. He had a pin in his hand. He was waiting for the right moment to pop the balloon himself and scare them.

But before he could do that, a dog came running to the bench. It saw the candy and wanted some. It barked and jumped on the man. The man dropped the pin and the candy. The dog grabbed the candy and ran away.

Lily and Ben saw what happened. They realized that the man was not nice. He wanted to trick them and make them sad. They felt angry and scared.

They let go of the balloon and ran away from the man. They found their toys and hugged them. They were glad that they still had each other.

The moral of the story is: Don't trust strangers who offer you rewards. They might have bad intentions. Stick with your friends and be careful.

But then, the gum gets stuck in her hair. She tries to pull it out, but it hurts. She cries. Her mom hears her and comes to help. She sees the gum in Anna's hair. She is not happy. She says, "Anna, you should not chew gum. It is not good for your teeth and your hair. Where did you get it?"

Anna feels sorry. She says, "I found it in your bag. I thought it was candy. I'm sorry, mom."

Her mom hugs her and says, "It's okay, Anna. I forgive you. But next time, ask me before you take something from my bag. And don't chew gum. It is not for kids. Now let's go to the bathroom and try to get the gum out of your hair."

Sam and Lily were playing hide and seek in the park. Sam was the seeker and Lily was the hider. Lily ran to a big tree and hid behind a branch. She thought Sam would not find her there.

Sam looked around and saw the branch moving. He smiled and walked to the tree. He said, "I see you, Lily! You are hiding behind the branch!" He pulled the branch and revealed Lily.

Lily was scared and angry. She said, "No, Sam! That was not fair! You cheated! You are a bad seeker!" She pushed Sam and ran away.

Sam was hurt and sad. He said, "Lily, wait! I did not cheat! I just saw the branch! I am sorry! Come back!" He chased after Lily.

But Lily did not listen. She ran to the road and did not look for cars. A big car came and hit Lily. Lily fell down and did not get up. Sam saw what happened and screamed. He ran to Lily and cried. He said, "Lily, Lily, please wake up! I love you! I am sorry! Please wake up!" But Lily did not wake up. She was gone. Sam was alone and very sad. He wished he had not pulled the branch. He wished he had been more careful. He wished he had been more comfortable. He wished he had been more kind.

Tim and Mia are friends. They like to play in the park. They like to slide, swing and run. But Tim is careless. He does not look where he goes. He does not listen to Mia.

One day, they see a big tree. The tree has a hole. Tim wants to see what is in the hole. He leans over the hole. He puts his head inside. Mia says, "Tim, be careful! The hole is dark and deep. You might fall in!"

But Tim does not listen. He leans more and more. He wants to see more and more. He does not hear Mia. He does not hear a growl. He does not see a big tooth.

Suddenly, a raccoon jumps out of the hole. The raccoon is angry. The raccoon bites Tim's nose. Tim screams. He falls back. He cries. Mia runs to him. She helps him. She says, "Tim, I told you to be careful! Now you have a big bite on your nose. It hurts. It bleeds. We have to go to the doctor."

Tim is sorry. He says, "Mia, you are right. I was careless. I did not look. I did not listen. I was silly. I am sorry. Please forgive me."

Mia says, "Tim, I forgive you. But you have to learn. You have to be careful. You have to look. You have to listen. You have to be smart. Or you will get hurt again."

The moral of the story is: Be careful and listen to your friends. Or you might get bitten by a raccoon.

"Wow, it's heavy," Lily said.

"Let's smell it," Ben said.

They brought the fruit to their noses and sniffed. It had a strong and sour smell.

"Yuck, it smells bad," Lily said.

"Maybe it tastes good," Ben said.

He opened his mouth and bit the fruit. He made a funny face and spit it out.

"Ow, ow, ow, it hurts, it hurts," he cried.

Lily dropped the fruit and ran to him.

"Ben, are you okay? What's wrong?" she asked.

"It's sour, it's sour, it burns my tongue," he said.

Lily hugged him and tried to comfort him.

"Shh, shh, it's okay, Ben. It's just a bad fruit. We won't eat it again," she said.

They heard a voice from the house.

"Kids, what are you doing? Come inside, it's time for lunch," their mom called.

They looked at each other and nodded.

"Okay, mom, we're coming," they said.

They left the fruit on the ground and ran to the house. They did not want to see the unknown fruit again. They hoped their mom had something sweet and yummy for lunch. They learned to stop and ask before they tried new things.

"Help! Help!" Tom shouted. "My blue plane is broken! I need to repair it!"

He saw a man who was working on a red truck. The man heard Tom and came to see him.

"Hello, little pilot," the man said. "What is wrong with your blue plane?"

"My blue plane is broken," Tom said. "It made a loud noise and smoke came out of it. Can you help me repair it?"

The man looked at Tom's blue plane and smiled.

"Sure, I can help you," the man said. "I am a mechanic. I know how to fix things. Let me see what I can do."

The man took some tools from his red truck and went to work on Tom's blue plane. He checked the engine, the wings, the wheels and the propeller. He fixed the problem and cleaned the smoke. He gave Tom a thumbs up.

"Your blue plane is good to go," the man said. "You can fly again."

Tom was very happy and thanked the man.

"Thank you, mechanic," Tom said. "You are very kind and smart. You saved my blue plane."

The man smiled and waved.

"You are welcome, little pilot," the man said. "You are very brave and good. You landed your blue plane safely. Have fun flying."

Tom got back into his blue plane and started the engine. It sounded good and smooth. He waved to the man and took off. He flew his blue plane in the sky and joined his friends. He was very happy and proud. He loved his blue plane and he loved flying.

"Give me the screw, Ben!" Lily said.

"No, it's mine!" Ben said.

"Let go, Lily!"

"Let go, Ben!"

Suddenly, they heard a loud noise. It was their dad, coming home from work. He parked his car in the driveway and got out. He saw Ben and Lily fighting over the screw.

"Hey, what are you two doing?" he asked.

Ben and Lily stopped and looked at him. They felt ashamed and scared. They knew they were in trouble.

They let go of the screw and ran to their dad. They hugged him and said they were sorry.

"It's okay, kids. I'm glad you're happy to see me. But why were you fighting over a screw?" he asked.

They told him they found it in the yard and they both wanted it.

He smiled and picked up the screw. He looked at it and said, "Do you know what this is? This is a special screw. It belongs to my toolbox. I must have dropped it when I fixed the fence. It's not a toy, it's a tool. You have to be careful with it. It can hurt you if you poke yourself or someone else with it."

He showed them how the screw worked. He said it was used to join things together, like wood or metal. He said he needed it for his next project.

"Can we help you, dad?" Ben and Lily asked.

"Sure, you can. But first, you have to promise me something. No more fighting over screws, okay? And no more digging holes in the yard. You might stumble and fall, or hit a pipe or a wire. That's dangerous. You can dig in the sandbox instead. That's safer and more fun. Deal?"

"Deal!" Ben and Lily said.

They gave their dad the screw and followed him to the garage. They helped him find his toolbox and his other tools. They were happy and excited. They forgot about their fight and their cold hands. They learned something new and had fun with their dad.

The band stopped playing and looked at Lily. Lily felt embarrassed and sad. But then, the drummer smiled and gave her a drumstick. He showed her how to play the drum and soon, she was making music with the band. Lily felt happy again and thought the music was even yummier than before.

Andy was so happy. He wore the fancy hat and showed it to all his friends. They all liked it too. Andy hoped that he could find more fancy things to wear. And they all played together, having fun with the fancy hat.

Once upon a time, in a colorful town, there lived a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to play dress-up and wear pretty clothes. She liked to look at fashion in the magazines her mom had.

One sunny day, Lily and her mom went to the park. Lily wore her favorite dress with lots of colors on it. She played with her friends and they all had fun. They played games, ran around, and laughed a lot.

After a while, Lily got tired. She found a big tree and sat down under it to rest. While she was resting, she saw a beautiful butterfly with colorful wings. It landed on her dress and seemed to like the colors too.

Lily's mom came over and they both looked at the butterfly. They smiled and felt happy. When it was time to go home, Lily said goodbye to her friends and the butterfly. She knew she would always remember the colorful day at the park.

One day, a little bird named Tim was flying in the sky. Tim saw a big tree with a hole in it. He thought it would be a perfect home for him. But first, he needed to know if the hole was big enough for him. So, Tim decided to measure the hole with his beak.

Tim flew to the tree and put his open beak near the hole. He said, "I will measure the hole with my mouth." He moved his mouth up and down, left and right. Tim was happy because the hole was just the right size for him. He knew he would fit in the hole.

The next day, Tim invited his friend, Sam the squirrel, over to see his new home. Sam looked at the hole and said, "Wow, you measured it well, Tim! It's a perfect fit for you!" Tim smiled and said, "Yes, I used my open mouth to measure it." They both laughed and played in the tree all day. And from that day on, Tim and Sam became the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a naughty boy named Tim. He loved to play hockey with his friends. One day, he found a big hockey stick in the park. Tim was very happy and wanted to play with it.

Tim asked his friend, Sam, "Do you want to play hockey with me?" Sam said, "Yes, but we must return the hockey stick if we find the owner." Tim and Sam played and had lots of fun. But Tim did not want to return the hockey stick.

Later, an old man came to the park. He was very sad. He said, "I lost my hockey stick. Did you see it?" Tim hid the hockey stick and said, "No, I did not see it." The old man walked away, still sad.

Sam was mad at Tim. He said, "You are naughty! We should return the hockey stick to the old man." But Tim did not listen. He kept the hockey stick and played with it all day. The old man never found his hockey stick and stayed sad. Tim's friends did not want to play with him anymore because he was naughty.

Once upon a time, there was a big mountain. A little boy named Tom wanted to go up the mountain. But the mountain was very hard to climb. Tom knew he had to struggle to reach the top.

One day, Tom met a girl named Lily. She wanted to go up the mountain too. Tom said, "Let's go up the mountain together!" Lily said, "Yes! We can help each other!" They started to climb the mountain. They struggled, but they did not give up.

As they climbed, they saw a dead tree. The tree was in their way. Tom and Lily had to find a way to get past the tree. They pushed and pulled, and finally, they moved the tree. They kept climbing the mountain. At last, they reached the top. Tom and Lily were happy. They had struggled, but they made it to the top together.

Once upon a time, there was a big ostrich named Ollie. Ollie loved to paint. One day, he found some bright colors to play with. He was so happy!

Ollie went to his friend, the little bird named Billy. "Look at my bright colors!" said Ollie. "Let's paint together!" Billy was excited too. They started to paint the trees and the grass with the bright colors.

But then, Ollie got an idea. "Let's paint the sun!" he said. Billy thought it was a bad idea, but Ollie didn't listen. He took the bright colors and painted the sun.

Suddenly, the sun was not happy. It got too hot, and the bright colors started to melt. The trees, the grass, and even Ollie and Billy were all covered in the melted colors.

And that is why you should never paint the sun. The end.

The moral of the story is: when you meet new friends, you can be happy and not miserable.

One day, a small fish named Fin was swimming in the ocean. The water was icy, but Fin liked it. He saw a big rock near the shore and wanted to rest on it. Fin swam closer to the rock, but the tide was very strong. It was hard for him to swim.

As Fin tried to swim to the rock, he met a crab named Carl. Carl said, "Be careful, Fin! The tide can make you soak if you go too close to the shore." Fin was scared, but he really wanted to rest on the rock.

Fin asked Carl for help. Carl thought for a moment and said, "I have an idea! Hold onto my shell, and I will walk to the rock. That way, you won't soak." Fin held onto Carl's shell, and they slowly moved towards the rock.

The tide was strong, but Carl was stronger. They finally reached the rock, and Fin was so happy. He thanked Carl for helping him. They both rested on the rock, enjoying the icy water and the sound of the tide. From that day on, Fin and Carl became best friends.

Once upon a time, there was a chubby dog named Bobo. Bobo loved to play with his ball all day long. One day, he saw a shiny watch on the ground. Bobo picked it up with his mouth and ran to show his friend, Kitty.

"Look, Kitty!" said Bobo, as he dropped the watch in front of her. "I found a shiny thing!" Kitty looked at the watch and said, "Oh no, Bobo! This is not a toy. We must find the person who lost it."

Bobo and Kitty walked around, asking their friends if they lost a watch. But no one knew whose watch it was. They were very tired and sad. They wanted to find the owner, but they did not know what to do.

As they walked, they saw a big pond. Bobo had an idea. "Maybe if we drop the watch in the pond, the person who lost it will find it there," he said. Kitty thought it was a good idea, too. So, they dropped the watch in the pond.

But the watch did not float. It sank to the bottom of the pond. Bobo and Kitty felt bad. They could not find the owner, and now the watch was gone forever. They went home, sad that their adventure had a bad ending.

"Please, Ben, can I have a coin? I want to make a wish," Lily said.

Ben looked in his pocket. He only had one coin left. He liked his coin. It was shiny and round. He did not want to give it to Lily.

"No, Lily, this is my coin. You cannot have it," Ben said.

Lily felt sad. She did not have any coins. She looked at the fountain and the water. She wanted to make a wish. She thought of a wish. She wished that Ben would be more generous.

Then, she saw something. On the ground, near the fountain, there was another coin. It was not shiny and round like Ben's coin. It was dirty and bent. But it was still a coin. Lily picked it up. She was happy.

"Look, Ben, I found a coin. Now I can make a wish," Lily said.

She ran to the fountain. She threw the coin in the water. She closed her eyes. She made her wish.

Ben watched Lily. He felt a little bad. He saw that Lily was happy with her coin. He thought that maybe he was not very nice. He thought that maybe he could share his coin with Lily. He wanted to make her happier.

He took out his coin. He ran to the fountain. He threw his coin in the water. He closed his eyes. He made a wish.

He wished that Lily would be his friend.

Lily opened her eyes. She saw Ben next to her. She saw that he threw his coin in the water. She smiled.

"Thank you, Ben. That was very generous of you. What did you wish for?" Lily asked.

Ben opened his eyes. He saw Lily's smile. He felt happy.

"I wished that you would be my friend," Ben said.

Lily hugged Ben. She said, "You are my friend, Ben. And I wished that you would be more generous. And you are. You are the best friend ever."

They laughed and played in the park. They were happy. Their wishes came true.

One day, Lily zoomed into the kitchen and saw a big cake on the table. It was for her dad's birthday. Lily thought the cake looked boring. She wanted to make it pretty with her crayons.

She climbed on a chair and reached for the cake. She started to draw flowers and stars and hearts on the white frosting. She was having fun.

But then, her mom came into the kitchen and saw what Lily had done. She was very angry.

"Lily, what have you done?" she shouted. "You ruined the cake! How could you be so naughty?"

Lily felt scared and sad. She did not mean to make her mom angry. She just wanted to make the cake pretty.

She started to cry and said, "I'm sorry, mom. I'm a painter. I like to make pictures."

Her mom sighed and hugged her. She said, "I know you are a painter, Lily, and I love your pictures. But you can't paint on everything. Some things are not for painting. You have to ask before you touch something that is not yours. Do you understand?"

Lily nodded and said, "I understand, mom. I'm sorry. I won't paint on the cake again."

Her mom smiled and said, "That's good, Lily. I forgive you. But you have to help me clean up the mess and make a new cake for dad. OK?"

Lily said, "OK, mom. I will help you. And I will make a card for dad with my crayons. I think he will like that."

Her mom said, "I think he will, too. Come on, let's go to the store and buy some more frosting. And maybe some sprinkles, too."

Lily smiled and said, "Yay, sprinkles! Can we zoom to the store, mom?"

Her mom laughed and said, "Sure, we can zoom to the store. But only if you hold my hand and look both ways before we cross the street."

Lily said, "OK, mom. I will do that. I love you, mom."

Her mom said, "I love you, too, Lily. You are my restless painter."

The moral value of the story is: You should respect other people's things and ask before you touch them. You should also apologize and make up for your mistakes. You should use your creativity in appropriate ways.

"Wealthy? What does that mean?" Ben asked.

"It means you have a lot of money and things," Lily said.

"Oh, we don't care about money and things. We just want to have fun and make friends," Ben said.

"Then you are very lucky," Lily said. "Come on, let's play!"

Anna and Ben had a lot of fun with Lily and the other children. They swung on the swings, slid on the slides, and fed the ducks in the pond. They forgot about the time and the cold and the fog.

But soon, the mist became thicker and darker. They could not see their house or Lily's house anymore. They could only see each other and the park.

"We should go back," Anna said. "Our parents will be worried."

"OK, let's go," Ben said.

They said goodbye to Lily and the other children and thanked them for playing with them. They ran back to the hole in the fence, but they could not find it. The mist was too thick. They were lost.

They started to cry and call for help. They wished they had never left their house. They wished they had listened to their parents.

Then, they heard a familiar voice.

"Anna! Ben! Where are you?" their father shouted.

"Daddy! Daddy! We're here!" Anna and Ben shouted back.

Their father found them and hugged them. He was angry and relieved. He took them back to their house and scolded them for running away. He also told them he loved them and was glad they were safe.

Anna and Ben felt sorry and happy. They said they were sorry and they loved him too. They also told him about Lily and the other children and the park. They asked him if they could play with them again.

Their father smiled and said, "Maybe, but only if you ask me first and if the weather is clear. No more mist adventures, OK?"

"OK, Daddy," Anna and Ben said.

They learned their lesson and never ran away again. They also made friends with Lily and the other children and played with them often. They realized that being wealthy was not as important as being happy and having fun. And they lived happily ever after.

The end.

"Can we look in the hole?" Sara asked Tom.

"Maybe. But be careful. There might be something scary in there," Tom said.

They walked closer to the pine tree and peeked in the hole. It was dark and empty. They saw nothing but dirt and leaves.

"Can we go in?" Sara asked again.

"I don't know. It looks too small for us," Tom said.

But Sara was curious. She crawled into the hole and said, "Come on, Tom. It's not scary. It's fun."

Tom followed her, but he felt nervous. He wished they had brought a flashlight. He hoped they would not get lost.

They crawled deeper into the hole, until they saw a faint light at the end. They reached the light and saw another hole. They looked out and saw a different part of the woods. They saw a pond and a bridge and some ducks.

"Wow, this is cool," Sara said. "We found a secret tunnel."

"Maybe we should go back," Tom said. "Mom and Dad might be looking for us."

But Sara wanted to explore more. She said, "Let's go see the ducks. Maybe they have babies."

"Run, Tom, run!" Sara shouted.

They ran back to the hole, but they saw something else. They saw a big bear with a black fur. It was hungry and smelled them. It roared and followed them.

"Help, Sara, help!" Tom cried.

They ran faster and faster, until they reached the hole. They crawled in and hoped the bear would not fit. They heard it scratch and growl and try to get in. They were scared and cried.

They crawled back to the other hole, where they had come from. They hoped to see their house and their parents. But they saw something else. They saw a big fire with a red flame. It was burning the woods and the pine tree. It crackled and smoked and reached the hole. They felt the heat and the pain.

They said they loved them too. They said they would never go into the hole again. They said they would always listen to their mom and dad.

She took them to the bathroom. There, on the sink, was a new toy. It was the same as the one they had broken, but better. It had bright colors and shiny buttons. It made funny sounds and lights.

"Wow!" Tom and Anna said.

"This is for you," their mom said. "Your dad and I bought it for you. We know you love this toy, and we love you. We are sorry we were angry with you. We know you are sorry too. Can you forgive us?"

Tom and Anna hugged their mom and said, "Yes, we forgive you. We love you too. And we are sorry we were foolish. Can you forgive us?"

Their mom nodded and said, "Of course, we forgive you. You are our children, and we are proud of you. Now, why don't you play with your new toy together, and then we can have lunch?"

Tom and Anna smiled and said, "Yes, let's do that. Thank you, mom. Thank you, dad. Thank you, God."

One day, Lily saw a big ladder in the garage. It was brown and tall and had many steps. Lily wanted to climb the ladder and see what was on top. She thought maybe there was a secret place or a treasure or a new friend.

She asked her mom if she could climb the ladder. Her mom said no. She said the ladder was not for kids. She said it was dangerous and Lily could fall and hurt herself. She said Lily should play with her toys or read a book or dance.

But Lily did not listen. She waited until her mom was busy and sneaked into the garage. She grabbed the ladder and dragged it to the wall. She put one foot on the first step and then the other. She felt brave and curious. She climbed higher and higher.

She reached the top of the ladder and looked around. She saw a big box with a bow. She wondered what was inside. She reached for the box and tried to open it. But the box was heavy and the ladder was shaky. Lily lost her balance and the ladder tipped over. Lily screamed and the box fell on the floor.

Her mom heard the noise and ran to the garage. She saw Lily on the ground and the box next to her. She was scared and angry. She hugged Lily and checked if she was hurt. She was not hurt, but she was scared and sorry.

She said to Lily, "Why did you climb the ladder? I told you not to. You could have been hurt. You were very naughty."

Lily said to her mom, "I'm sorry, mom. I wanted to see what was in the box. I thought it was a surprise for me."

Her mom said to Lily, "The box was a surprise for you. It was a new dress for you to dance in. But you spoiled the surprise and the dress. Now you can't have it."

Lily cried and said to her mom, "I'm sorry, mom. I love you. Can I still dance with you?"

Her mom said to Lily, "I love you too. You can still dance with me. But you have to promise me to never climb the ladder again. And you have to be a good girl and listen to me."

Lily said to her mom, "I promise, mom. I will be a good girl and listen to you. And I will dance with you."

Her mom said to Lily, "Okay, then. Let's go and dance in the kitchen. But first, let's put the ladder away and clean up the mess."

One night, a little boy named Tom looked out of his window and saw many stars in the sky. He wondered what they were and how they tasted. He asked his mom, "Mom, can I eat a star?"

His mom smiled and said, "No, Tom, you can't eat a star. Stars are very far away and very hot. They are not food for us. They are lights that shine at night."

"But why do they shine?" Tom asked.

"Because they are made of fire and gas," his mom said. "They are like big balls of fire that burn and glow. They are very beautiful, but also very dangerous. If you try to eat a star, you will get burned and hurt."

Tom felt scared and curious. He wanted to see a star up close, but he also did not want to get burned. He asked his mom, "How can I see a star, then?"

His mom hugged him and said, "You can see a star with a telescope. A telescope is a tool that makes things look bigger and closer. Maybe someday we can get a telescope and see the stars together. But for now, you can see them with your eyes and make a wish."

Tom liked that idea. He looked at the stars again and picked one that was bright and shiny. He closed his eyes and made a wish. He wished that he could have a telescope and see the stars with his mom. He also wished that he could have a cookie and some milk before bed. He opened his eyes and said, "Mom, I made a wish. Can I have a cookie and some milk, please?"

His mom laughed and said, "Sure, Tom, you can have a cookie and some milk. But only one, okay? You don't want to eat too much before bed. Come on, let's go to the kitchen."

Tom followed his mom to the kitchen. He was happy and sleepy. He ate his cookie and drank his milk. He thanked his mom and gave her a kiss. He said, "Mom, I love you. And I love the stars. But I don't want to eat them. They are too hot and bad."

His mom said, "I love you too, Tom. And I'm glad you don't want to eat the stars. They are not for us. They are for the sky. Now, let's go to bed. It's late and you need to sleep."

Tom nodded and yawned. He went to his room with his mom. He got into his bed and snuggled with his teddy bear. He looked out of his window and saw the stars again. He smiled and said, "Good night, stars. Thank you for shining. Maybe someday I will see you with a telescope. But for now, I will dream of you."

He closed his eyes and fell asleep. He dreamed of stars and cookies and his mom. He was happy and warm. He did not eat a star, but he felt like one.

"Let's make it more cozy. Let's make a fire!" Ben said, picking up a match from the ground. He had seen his dad use matches to light candles.

"No, Ben, fire is bad! Fire can hurt us and the birds!" Lily said, scared. She tried to take the match from Ben, but he was faster.

"Fire is fun! Watch!" Ben said, striking the match and throwing it into the nest. The leaves caught fire and made a big flame. The toy birds melted and burned.

"Ben, what did you do? You changed our nest into a fire! You are mean!" Lily cried, running away from the fire.

The fire spread quickly and reached the fence. The fence was made of wood and it burned too. The fire reached the house and the curtains. The house was made of bricks, but the curtains were made of cloth and they burned too.

The fire alarm went off and made a loud noise. Ben and Lily's mom and dad came out of the house and saw the fire. They were angry and scared. They called the firemen and tried to put out the fire with water.

The firemen came with a big truck and a hose. They sprayed water on the fire and made it smaller. They put out the fire and made it stop.

But it was too late. The house was damaged and the toys were gone. Ben and Lily's mom and dad were sad and mad. They hugged Lily and scolded Ben.

"Ben, you were very naughty and careless. You played with fire and you changed our home into a mess. You could have hurt yourself and Lily and us. You are in big trouble!" they said.

Ben felt sorry and ashamed. He wished he had listened to Lily and not played with fire. He wished he could change everything back to how it was before. But he couldn't. He had made a big mistake and he had to face the consequences. He had learned a hard lesson.

Anna and Ben were twins who loved to play in the snow. They made snowmen, snowballs and snow angels. But one day, the snow started to melt. It became wet and muddy. Anna and Ben were sad. They thought the snow was fun and the mud was boring.

"Where did the snow go?" Anna asked.

"It vanished," Ben said. "It turned into water and went away."

"Will it come back?" Anna wondered.

"Maybe next winter," Ben said. "But that's a long time."

They wished they could see the snow again. They wished they could have a new adventure.

That night, they heard a strange noise outside their window. They looked out and saw a big sleigh with eight reindeer. The reindeer had shiny noses and antlers. They were pulling the sleigh through the air. On the sleigh, there was a man with a red suit and a white beard. He had a big sack of presents. He waved at Anna and Ben and smiled.

"Hello, Anna and Ben!" he said. "I'm Santa Claus. I heard you miss the snow. Do you want to come with me to the North Pole?"

Anna and Ben were amazed. They nodded and ran to the door. They put on their coats and boots and climbed on the sleigh. Santa gave them each a warm blanket and a candy cane. He snapped his fingers and the reindeer flew faster. They soared over the houses and the trees and the stars. They saw the moon and the clouds and the northern lights. They felt the cold wind and the snowflakes on their faces. They laughed and sang and hugged each other.

"This is not boring at all!" Anna said.

"This is the best adventure ever!" Ben said.

They thanked Santa for taking them to the North Pole. They saw his workshop and his elves and his toys. They played with the reindeer and the snowmen and the snowballs. They had hot chocolate and cookies and cake. They felt happy and cozy and sleepy.

Santa tucked them in their beds and gave them each a kiss. He said he had to go and deliver more presents to other children. He said he would come back next year. He said he was glad they loved the snow. He said they were good and brave and kind.

"Good night, Anna and Ben!" he said. "Merry Christmas!"

He climbed on his sleigh and waved goodbye. The reindeer flew away with him. They vanished into the night. Anna and Ben closed their eyes and dreamed of snow.

One day, she saw a chair with a loose leg. She decided to fix it. She took her box of screws and her screwdriver and went to the chair. She put a screw in the hole and turned it with the screwdriver. She did the same for the other holes.

"Look, Mommy, I fixed the chair!" she said proudly. She stood on the chair to show her mom.

"Wow, Lily, you are very clever and independent!" her mom said. "But be careful, standing on the chair is not safe. You might fall and hurt yourself."

Lily listened to her mom. She got down from the chair and gave her mom a hug. She was happy that she fixed the chair, but she also knew that she had to be safe. She put her box of screws and her screwdriver away and went to play with her toys.

Tom and Mia are not happy. They really want to see the train. They think Mom is not looking. They sneak to the shelf. They try to remove the box. But the box is too heavy. It slips from their hands. It falls to the floor. It makes a loud noise. Mom hears the noise. She runs to the living room. She sees the box on the floor. She sees Tom and Mia. She is very angry.

Tom and Mia are very sad. They know they have made a big mistake. They say sorry to Mom. They go to their room. They cry. They wish they had not touched the box. They wish they had waited for Dad. They wish they had been good. They hope Dad will forgive them. They hope they can still make him happy. They hope they can still see the train.

Anna and Ben are very happy. They want to eat the cake soon. They put on their aprons and help Mom to pour the batter into a pan. Mom puts the pan in the oven and sets the timer. She says, "We have to wait for 20 minutes. The cake will be hot and yummy."

Anna and Ben are bored. They want to play. They see Mom's pants on the chair. They have an idea. They take Mom's pants and put them on their heads. They pretend to be elephants. They say, "Look at us, Mom! We are elephants! We have long trunks!"

Mom hears them and laughs. She says, "You are very funny, Anna and Ben. But those are not trunks. Those are my pants. Please take them off and put them back on the chair."

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play in the garden. They see a big plant with green leaves and purple flowers. Anna says, "What is this?"

Ben says, "This is a bean plant. My mom grows beans. She says they are good for us."

Anna says, "Can we pick some beans?"

Ben says, "No, we have to be careful. The beans are delicate. They can break easily. We have to wait until they are ripe."

Anna says, "How do we know when they are ripe?"

Ben says, "We have to look at the color. When they are green, they are not ripe. When they are yellow, they are ripe. Then we can pick them and eat them."

Anna and Ben decide to lead the bean plant. They tie a string to the stem and pull it gently. They make the plant grow along the fence. They say, "Grow, bean plant, grow!"

Every day, they check the beans. They see them change from green to yellow. They are happy. They say, "The beans are ripe! We can pick them and eat them!"

They pick some beans and wash them. They share them with their moms. They say, "These are the best beans ever! We grew them ourselves!" Their moms are proud of them. They say, "You are good gardeners! You took care of the bean plant. You were gentle and patient. You deserve a treat!"

They give them some cookies and milk. Anna and Ben smile. They say, "Thank you, mom! We love you and we love beans!"

Lily and Sam were best friends. They liked to play outside in the sun. But one day, it was raining hard. Lily and Sam were sad. They wanted to go out and have fun.

"Can we play in the rain?" Lily asked her mom.

"Sure, but you need to wear your raincoats and boots. And take an umbrella with you," her mom said.

Lily and Sam put on their raincoats and boots. Lily chose a bright yellow umbrella. Sam chose a blue one with stars. They went outside and opened their umbrellas.

"Wow, look at the raindrops!" Lily said. "They make funny sounds on the umbrella."

"Yeah, and look at the puddles!" Sam said. "They are like little lakes."

Lily and Sam jumped in the puddles. They splashed and laughed. They saw a worm crawling on the ground.

"Hello, worm!" Lily said. "Are you having fun in the rain?"

The worm did not answer. It just wiggled and wriggled.

"Maybe he is shy," Sam said. "Let's encourage him to join us."

"How?" Lily asked.

Sam had an idea. He bent down and whispered to the worm.

"Hey, worm, don't be afraid. We are your friends. We like the rain, too. Come and play with us. We have umbrellas to keep you dry."

The worm looked at Sam and Lily. He saw their smiling faces and their colorful umbrellas. He felt curious and happy. He decided to give it a try.

He crawled out of the dirt and onto Sam's hand. Sam lifted him up and put him on his umbrella. The worm felt the raindrops bounce off the umbrella. He felt the wind blow the umbrella. He felt the sun peek through the clouds. He felt the joy of playing with Lily and Sam.

He smiled and said, "Thank you, friends. You are very kind. I like the rain, too. And I like your umbrellas. They are bright and beautiful."

Sara loved to play the violin. She had a small violin that her grandma gave her. She liked to make music with it. She played it every day in her room.

One day, Sara wanted to play the violin for her friends. She asked her mom if she could. Her mom said yes, but she had to be polite. She had to ask her friends if they wanted to hear her play. She had to say please and thank you. She had to share her violin if they wanted to try.

Sara was happy. She took her violin and went to the park. She saw her friends Lily and Ben. She said hello to them. She asked them if they wanted to hear her play the violin. Lily loves to sing. She sings all the time. She sings in the morning, in the afternoon, and at night. She sings to her toys, to her mom, and to her dad. She sings loud and happy.

One day, Lily sees a microphone in the store. It is shiny and big. It has a button and a cord. Lily wants the microphone. She asks her mom, "Can I have the microphone, please?"

Her mom says, "Why do you want the microphone, Lily?"

Lily says, "Because I love to sing. And the microphone makes my voice louder and better. And I can sing to more people. And they will like my songs. And I will be important."

Her mom smiles and hugs Lily. She says, "Lily, you are important. You are important to me, and to dad, and to your toys. And you have a beautiful voice. You don't need a microphone to sing. You can sing with your heart. And I will always listen to you."

Lily thinks for a moment. She says, "You are right, mom. I don't need a microphone. I have you. And you are the best listener. Can we sing together?"

Her mom says, "Of course, Lily. Let's sing together. What song do you want to sing?"

Lily says, "I want to sing the song you taught me. The one that says, 'I love you, you love me, we are a happy family.'"

Her mom says, "I know that song. I love that song. Let's sing it loud and happy."

Lily and Tom were best friends. They liked to play in the park with their toys. One day, they found a big, hairy dog. The dog was friendly and wagged its tail. Lily and Tom wanted to pet the dog, but they were afraid.

"Let's make a promise," Lily said. "We will pet the dog together. You go first, then I go."

"OK," Tom said. He was brave and walked to the dog. He reached out his hand and touched the dog's fur. The dog licked his hand and made a happy sound. Tom smiled and said, "See, he is nice. Your turn, Lily."

Lily nodded and took a step. But then she saw the dog's teeth. They were big and sharp. She got scared and ran away. She tripped and fell on the ground. She hurt her knee and cried.

Tom heard her cry and ran to her. He saw her knee was bleeding. He felt sorry for her and hugged her. He said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I broke our promise. I should have stayed with you. Are you OK?"

Lily sniffed and said, "It's OK, Tom. You didn't mean to. I was silly and ran away. My knee hurts, but I'll be OK."

They heard the dog bark and looked up. The dog was still wagging its tail. He came to them and licked their faces. He was not mean, he was just playful. Lily and Tom laughed and petted the dog. They made a new promise: to be friends with the dog and each other.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park. They saw a stream with many stones and fish. They wanted to cross the stream, but they did not have a bridge.

"Let's make a bridge with the stones!" said Tom.

"Good idea!" said Lily.

They picked up some stones and threw them into the stream. They tried to make a path from one side to the other. But some stones were too big and some were too small. They could not balance on them.

"I have an idea!" said Lily. "We can weigh the stones with this stick. The stick will tell us if the stone is heavy or light. We can use the heavy stones for the bottom and the light stones for the top. Then the bridge will be strong and stable."

"That's very clever!" said Tom.

They found a stick and used it as a scale. They weighed the stones and sorted them by size. They built a bridge with the stones, layer by layer. They tested the bridge with their feet. It was firm and steady.

"Yay! We did it!" they cheered.

They crossed the stream on their bridge. They were happy and proud. They saw more fish and flowers on the other side. They continued to play and explore. They had a lot of fun.

"Let's march to the woods!" Tom says. "We can see what is there with the flashlight."

"OK!" Anna says. "But we have to be careful. The woods are scary."

They take the flashlight and march to the woods. They see many trees and animals. They hear many noises. They are not afraid. They have the flashlight.

But then, the flashlight stops working. It is out of batteries. Tom and Anna are in the dark. They are scared. They do not know how to go back.

"Help!" Tom cries. "We are lost!"

"Help!" Anna cries. "We are alone!"

They hug each other. They wish they had not gone to the woods. They wish they had stayed home.

Then, they see a light. It is their dad. He has a flashlight too. He has been looking for them. He is angry and worried.

"Tom! Anna! What are you doing here?" he asks. "You should not go to the woods without me. It is dangerous. You could get hurt."

"Sorry, dad," Tom says. "We wanted to explore. We found a flashlight. But it stopped working. We were scared."

"Sorry, dad," Anna says. "We wanted to have fun. We marched to the woods. But we got lost. We were alone."

"Next time, you have to listen to me," he says. "I know what is best for you. I love you. You have to be smart and careful. The woods are not a place to play. The flashlight is not a toy. You have to respect nature and things."

Tom nodded and ran after the cricket. But the cricket was fast and jumped away. Tom tried to catch it with his hands, but he missed.

"Wait for me, Tom!" Lila said. She followed Tom, but she was slow. She had a sore leg from falling down yesterday.

Tom did not wait for Lila. He wanted to catch the cricket by himself. He chased the cricket across the yard, but he did not see the big rock in his way. He tripped over the rock and fell down. He scraped his knee and started to cry.

"Are you okay, Tom?" she asked. She gave him a hug and a band-aid.

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there lived a wet frog named Fred. Fred loved to jump in the puddles after it rained. One sunny day, after a big rain, Fred met a new friend named Harry. Harry was a big animal with a long horn on his head.

"Hi, I'm Fred," said the wet frog. "Do you like to play in the puddles too?"

"No, I don't like to get wet," said Harry, shaking his big horn. "I like to stay dry in the sun."

Fred thought for a moment and then smiled. "I have an idea! Let's play a game. You can stay dry in the sun, and I will jump in the puddles. When I am wet, I will try to make you wet too by shaking the water off me."

Harry laughed and agreed to play the game. They played all day long. Fred would jump in the puddles and try to make Harry wet, but Harry would use his big horn to block the water. They laughed and had so much fun together.

At the end of the day, Fred and Harry were both tired but happy. They had made a new friend and found a fun game to play together. From that day on, they played together in the forest, with Fred always trying to make Harry wet and Harry always trying to stay dry.

Remy was persistent. He tried to open the stove, but it was too hot. Remy felt sad because he could not open the stove. He wanted to find a way to cool it down. Remy thought and thought, then he had an idea.

Remy went to the river and filled a bucket with water. He took the water and poured it on the stove. The stove became cool. Remy opened the stove and found a yummy carrot cake inside. He was so happy that he could finally enjoy the cake.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there lived a boy named Tom. Tom was an adventurous boy who loved to play outside. One day, he saw a big apple tree in his yard. The tree had many red apples on it. Tom wanted to eat the apples, but they were too high for him to reach.

Tom had an idea. He called his friend, Sam, and said, "Let's joke and play by the apple tree. Maybe we can find a way to get the apples." Sam agreed and they both went to the tree. They tried to climb, but it was too hard. They tried to jump, but they couldn't reach. Then, Tom saw a long stick on the ground.

Tom picked up the stick and said, "I will use this stick to get the apples." Sam laughed, thinking it was a joke. But Tom was serious. He swung the stick at the apples, trying to knock them down. One apple fell, but it was not enough. Tom swung the stick harder and harder, trying to get more apples.

Suddenly, the stick hit a big branch and the branch broke. The broken branch fell down and landed on Tom's foot. Tom cried out in pain, and Sam ran to get help. Tom's mom came and saw what happened. She was very sad and worried. Tom had to go to the doctor, and he could not play outside for a long time.

From that day on, Tom learned not to be too adventurous. He never tried to get apples with a stick again. And every time he saw an apple tree, he remembered the day he got hurt and decided not to take risks he was not ready for.

"Sure, you can," Tom said. "That's the best thing to do. Then it will be happy and healthy. And maybe you can see it again another day."

Lila nodded. She took the worm out of the bucket and put it gently in the hole. She covered it with some earth and patted it softly.

Lily was sad and angry. She did not want to wait. She wanted to spend time with her daddy and the surprise. She thought he was being mean and unfair. She decided to open the box when he was not looking. She sneaked into the living room and lifted the lid.

Inside the box, there was a beautiful doll. It had long hair, a pretty dress, and shiny shoes. Lily gasped. She loved the doll. She wanted to hug it and play with it. She reached for the doll, but then she heard her daddy's voice.

She said, "I'm sorry, daddy. I was curious and excited. I wanted to see the surprise. I wanted to spend time with you and the doll. I didn't mean to be bad. Please don't be mad at me."

You have to respect my rules and my wishes. Do you understand?"

Her daddy smiled. He said, "Yes, we can still play with it. But only after you clean up the mess and apologize to your mommy. And next time, when I say no, you have to say okay. Deal?"

"Mom, can you help us?" they ask. Mom comes to their room. She smiles and hugs them.

"Of course, I can help you. Let me show you how to tie your shoes. It is easy and fun. You just need to make a loop, a cross, and a pull."

Mom shows them how to tie their shoes. She makes a loop with one lace, and a cross with the other lace. Then she pulls the laces through the loop. She makes a bow and tucks the ends.

"Wow, that is so cool!" Tom says.

"I want to try it too!" Lily says.

They practice tying their shoes. They make loops, crosses, and pulls. They make bows and tucks. They are very proud of themselves.

"Look, Mom, we did it!" they say.

Mom claps her hands and cheers. "You did it! You are so smart and brave. I am very happy for you. Now you can tie your shoes by yourselves. You are ready for a new day."
