Lily and Tom were friends who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a big cop car parked on their street. They were curious and wanted to look inside.

"Let's go and see the cop car!" Tom said.

"OK, but be careful. We don't want to get in trouble," Lily said.

They walked to the cop car and peeked through the window. They saw a radio, a badge, and a gun. They thought it was cool and exciting.

"Wow, look at this! I want to be a cop when I grow up," Tom said.

"Me too! I want to catch bad guys and help people," Lily said.

They decided to play cop and robber. Tom pretended to be the cop and Lily pretended to be the robber. Tom was very bossy and told Lily what to do.

"Stop, robber! You are under arrest! Put your hands up!" Tom shouted.

"No, I won't! You can't catch me!" Lily shouted back.

They ran around the car, chasing and dodging each other. They had fun, but they also made a lot of noise.

Suddenly, they heard a loud voice behind them.

"Hey, what are you kids doing here? This is my car!" It was the real cop who owned the car. He looked angry and stern.

Lily and Tom were scared and sorry. They stopped playing and turned around.

"Sorry, sir. We were just playing. We didn't mean to bother you," Lily said.

"Yeah, sorry. We like your car. We want to be cops like you," Tom said.

The cop looked at them and softened his expression. He saw that they were just innocent and curious.

"Well, I'm glad you like my car, but you can't play with it. It's not a toy. It's for work. And you can't be so loud. You might disturb the neighbors or cause an accident," the cop said.

He walked to his car and opened the door. He took out two stickers that had a star and the word "cop" on them.

"Here, I'll give you these stickers as a gift. You can put them on your shirts and pretend to be cops. But remember, being a cop is not just about having a car and a gun. It's about being brave, honest, and kind. And it's also about listening and following the rules. Do you understand?" the cop said.

Lily and Tom nodded and smiled. They thanked the cop and took the stickers. They put them on their shirts and felt proud.

"Thank you, sir. You are a nice cop. We will be good cops too," Lily said.

"Yeah, thank you. And we will be quiet and careful too," Tom said.

The cop smiled and waved at them. He got in his car and drove away.

Lily and Tom walked back to their homes. They learned a lesson that day. They learned that playing is fun, but they also have to respect other people's things and feelings. And they learned that being a cop is not just about being bossy, but about being helpful and fair.

The moral of the story is: do not judge people by their names, nations, or differences. Be kind and friendly to everyone. You can make new friends and learn new things from people who are different from you.

After many days, Anna saw a green sprout in the pot. She was happy. She watered it more and watched it grow. It grew taller and taller. It grew leaves and buds. She did more math. She added the leaves and the buds. She took away the days until the flower would bloom.

One morning, Anna saw a bright color in the pot. It was a flower. It was big and yellow. It smelled sweet. Anna was very happy. She ran to her mom and showed her the flower. "I am the famous clown. I just wear this old clothes and beard to hide. But when I go on stage, I put on my nose, my smile and my hair. And I make everyone laugh and have fun. Do you want to come and see me?" the old man said.

Lily and Tom laughed. They were not scared anymore. They were happy.

One day, a boy and a girl went to the park with their mom. They saw a big tree with many birds and squirrels. The boy and the girl liked to watch the wild animals and listen to their sounds.

"Look, there is a nest with eggs!" the boy said, pointing to a branch. "Can we see them closer?"

"No, we have to be careful and not touch them," the mom said. "They are not our stuff, they belong to the birds. They need to be safe and warm."

The boy and the girl nodded and moved away from the tree. They saw a slide, a swing, and a sandbox. They decided to play there for a while.

But then, they heard a loud noise. A big dog was running towards the tree. He barked and jumped and tried to reach the nest. The birds and the squirrels were scared and flew and ran away.

"Oh no, the dog will break the eggs!" the girl said. "We have to save them!"

The boy and the girl ran to the tree. They shouted and waved their arms to scare the dog away. The mom followed them and called the dog's owner.

"Hey, stop that! Your dog is not allowed to chase the wild animals!" the mom said. "He could hurt them or their babies!"

The dog's owner came and grabbed the dog by the collar. He said he was sorry and that the dog was just curious. He took the dog away from the park.

The boy and the girl looked at the nest. The eggs were still there, unbroken. The birds and the squirrels came back to the tree. They made happy sounds and thanked the boy and the girl.

"You did a good job, kids," the mom said. "You saved the wild stuff. They are very grateful to you."

The boy and the girl smiled and hugged their mom. They felt proud and happy. They liked to help the wild animals. They said goodbye to the tree and went home.

Tom and Anna were playing in the garden. They saw a big bag of leather that Dad had brought home. They wanted to make something with it.

"Let's cut some leather and make a hat!" Tom said.

"OK, but be careful with the scissors," Anna said.

They took the scissors and the leather and went to the table. Tom cut a big piece of leather. He tried to make a hat, but it was too big and floppy. He cut some more, but it was still too big.

"Look at my hat!" Tom said. He put it on his head. It covered his eyes and ears.

Anna laughed. "That's not a hat, that's a tent!"

Tom felt ashamed. He did not like Anna's laugh. He was angry. He took the scissors and cut Anna's hair.

"Hey, stop that!" Anna shouted. She felt the scissors snip her hair. She was scared and sad. She ran to Mom.

Mom saw Anna's hair. She was shocked. She saw Tom's hat. She was angry.

"Tom, what have you done?" Mom said. "You cut Anna's hair and you wasted the leather!"

Tom knew he was in trouble. He felt more ashamed. He said sorry to Anna and Mom. He took off his hat and threw it away.

Mom hugged Anna and Tom. She said they had to be more careful and respectful. She said she would fix Anna's hair and find a use for the leather.

Tom and Anna learned their lesson. They did not cut leather or hair again. They played with other things. They were friends again.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They saw a big pond with many ducks. Lily liked the ducks. She wanted to feed them some bread.

"Look, Ben, pretty ducks!" Lily said. She took out a piece of bread from her bag and threw it into the pond.

"Wait, Lily, don't do that!" Ben said. He saw something else in the pond. It was not a duck. It was a crocodile. It had big teeth and a long tail. It was hungry. It saw the bread and the children.

"Roar!" The crocodile said. It swam fast towards the bread and the children. It wanted to eat them.

Lily and Ben were scared. They ran away from the pond. They found their mom and dad. They told them what they saw.

"Mom, dad, there is a crocodile in the pond!" Lily said.

"A crocodile? Are you sure?" Mom said.

"Yes, mom, it was big and scary!" Ben said.

Mom and dad looked at the pond. They saw the crocodile. It was still there. It was angry. It did not belong in the pond. It belonged in the zoo.

"Come on, children, let's go and tell the park keeper. He will call the zoo and take the crocodile away." Dad said.

Lily and Ben nodded. They followed their mom and dad. They were glad they were safe. They did not want to play with the crocodile. They wanted to play with the pretty ducks.

Lily slides down and laughs. She thinks she is funny. But then she sees something on her dress. It is gray and sticky. It is bird poop. A bird pooped on her when she was on the slide.

"Yuck!" Lily says. She tries to wipe it off, but it only makes it worse. She looks at her dress and feels embarrassed. She starts to cry.

Max gets up and sees Lily crying. He is not angry anymore. He feels sorry for her. He goes to her and gives her a hug.

"It's okay, Lily. It was an accident. You can get a new dress. Do you want to play with me?" Max says.

Lily stops crying and nods. She hugs him back. She is glad he is her friend.

They go to their moms and tell them what happened. Their moms help them clean up and get new clothes. Then they go back to the park and play together. They share the slide and have fun. They are happy.

Lila and Ben are furry cats who live in a big house with their human. They like to play with toys, chase birds and nap on the sofa. One day, they see a movie on the TV that shows cats who can fly. They are very curious and excited.

"Wow, look at those cats!" Lila says. "They have wings and they fly in the sky!"

"I want to fly too!" Ben says. "How do they do that?"

"Maybe they have magic," Lila says. "Or maybe they eat something special."

They decide to try to find out how to fly. They look around the house for anything that might help them. They find a feather, a balloon, a hat and a scarf. They try to put them on and jump from the sofa, but they only fall to the floor.

"This is not working," Ben says. "We are not flying."

"Maybe we need to go outside," Lila says. "Maybe there is more air and space there."

They sneak out of the house and run to the garden. They see a big tree with a branch that is high up. They think that maybe if they climb up there, they can fly.

"Come on, let's try it!" Lila says. "Maybe we can be like the cats in the movie!"

They climb up the tree and sit on the branch. They look at the sky and the birds. They feel the wind and the sun. They are happy and brave.

"Ready?" Lila says.

"Ready!" Ben says.

They spread their arms and legs and jump from the branch. They feel a rush of air and a thrill of joy. They think they are flying.

But they are not flying. They are falling. They land on the soft grass and roll over. They are not hurt, but they are surprised and sad.

"We are not flying," Ben says. "We are just falling."

"We are not like the cats in the movie," Lila says. "We are just furry cats."

They look at each other and sigh. They are disappointed and confused.

But then they hear a voice. It is their human. He is calling them from the house. He sounds happy and kind.

"Lila! Ben! Where are you? I have a surprise for you!"

They perk up their ears and run to the house. They wonder what the surprise is. They hope it is something good.

They enter the house and see their human holding a big box. He smiles and opens it. Inside, there are two shiny costumes. They are furry and colorful. They have wings and tails. They look like the cats in the movie.

"These are for you," their human says. "I saw the movie too and I thought you would like them. You can wear them and pretend to fly. Do you like them?"

Lila and Ben are amazed and happy. They jump into the box and try on the costumes. They fit perfectly. They feel soft and warm. They look at each other and laugh. They look like the cats in the movie.

"Thank you, thank you!" they say to their human. "We love them!"

They hug their human and then run to the sofa. They jump on it and flap their wings. They pretend to fly. They have fun. They are furry cats who can fly.

Ben and Sam are friends. They like to play with cars and balls. One day, they see a big gray cat in the park. The cat has wide eyes and a long tail. Ben and Sam want to pet the cat.

"Hello, cat," Ben says. "Can we pet you?"

The cat does not say anything. It looks at Ben and Sam. Then it runs away.

"Come back, cat," Sam says. "We are nice."

Ben and Sam chase the cat. They run and run. But the cat is faster. It jumps over a fence and disappears.

Ben and Sam are sad. They sit on the grass and cry.

A lady sees them. She walks over to them. She has a kind face and a red hat.

"Why are you crying, boys?" she asks.

"We wanted to pet the cat, but it ran away," Ben says.

"We are nice, but the cat did not like us," Sam says.

The lady smiles. She sits down with them. She says, "The cat did not know you. Maybe it was scared of you. You should not chase animals that you do not know. They might think you want to hurt them. You should be gentle and respectful. Then they might trust you and let you pet them."

Ben and Sam listen to the lady. They nod. They say, "We are sorry. We did not mean to scare the cat. We will be gentle and respectful next time."

The lady hugs them. She says, "That's good, boys. You are smart and kind. I have a dog at home. He is friendly and likes to play. Do you want to meet him?"

Ben and Sam smile. They say, "Yes, please!"

The lady takes them to her home. She shows them her dog. He is brown and fluffy. He has a wet nose and a wagging tail. He barks and licks them.

Ben and Sam pet the dog. They play with him. They are happy.

They learn that animals are not toys. They are living beings that have feelings. They need love and care. They need to be treated well. That is the moral of the story.

But they were clumsy. They knocked over the pot. The soup spilled everywhere. It was hot and sticky. They screamed.

"Who did this? Who ruined my soup?" she shouted.

Ben and Mia were scared. They ran away. They hid behind a tree.

They felt sorry. They had made a big mess. They had not borrowed the soup. They had stolen it.

They learned a lesson. They should not take things that are not theirs. They should ask first. They should be careful. They should say sorry.

Anna and Ben were playing with their toys in the living room. Anna had a doll and Ben had a car. They were having fun, but then Anna saw Ben's car and wanted it.

"Give me your car, Ben. It is shiny and fast. I like it more than my doll," Anna said.

"No, Anna. This is my car. You have your doll. We can share, but you cannot take it," Ben said.

Anna did not listen. She grabbed Ben's car and ran away. Ben was sad and angry. He chased Anna and tried to get his car back. They started to fight and yell.

Mom heard the noise and came to see what was wrong. She saw Anna and Ben pulling and pushing each other. She was not happy.

"Anna, Ben, stop it right now. Why are you fighting?" Mom asked.

"Anna took my car and she won't give it back. It is not fair," Ben said.

"Ben has a nice car and I want it. It is better than my doll," Anna said.

Mom shook her head. She took the car and the doll and put them on the table.

"Listen to me, both of you. You have to be kind and respectful to each other. You cannot take someone else's toy without asking. You have to share and take turns. How would you feel if someone did that to you?" Mom said.

Anna and Ben looked at each other. They realized that they were wrong. They felt sorry for what they did.

"I'm sorry, Ben. I should not have taken your car. It was not nice. Can you forgive me?" Anna said.

"I'm sorry, Anna. I should not have yelled at you. It was not nice. I forgive you," Ben said.

They hugged and said sorry to Mom. Mom smiled and hugged them back.

"That's good, Anna and Ben. I'm proud of you. You are compassionate. You care about how others feel. You can play with your toys again, but remember to share and take turns. OK?" Mom said.

"OK, Mom. Thank you," Anna and Ben said.

They took their toys and played together happily. They learned their lesson. They realized that being compassionate is better than being selfish.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to swing, slide and run. But then the sky became dark and the wind became cold. They heard a loud noise. It was thunder.

"Let's go home!" Lily said. She was scared of the thunder.

"But I want to play more!" Tom said. He was not scared. He was strong.

"You are not strong, you are silly!" Lily said. She grabbed her coat and ran to the gate. Tom frowned. He did not like what Lily said.

He followed her, but he was angry. He did not want to wear his coat. He threw it on the ground. He wanted to show Lily that he was strong.

But then he felt something wet on his head. It was rain. It was raining hard. He looked at his coat. It was wet too. He felt cold and wet. He wished he had his coat.

He ran to the gate, but Lily was not there. She had gone home with their mom. He was alone. He was not strong. He was sad.

He cried. He wanted his mom. He wanted his coat. He wanted Lily. He was sorry for what he did.

He saw a man coming. It was the park keeper. He had a big hat and a big umbrella.

"Hey, little boy, what are you doing here?" the park keeper asked. He saw Tom's coat on the ground. He picked it up and gave it to Tom.

"Thank you," Tom said. He put on his coat. He felt warm and dry.

"Where is your mom?" the park keeper asked.

"She went home with Lily," Tom said.

"Who is Lily?" the park keeper asked.

"She is my sister. She is scared of thunder. I am not scared. I am strong," Tom said.

"Is that so?" the park keeper said. He smiled. "Well, being strong is good, but being kind is better. Sometimes you have to think of others, not just yourself. Do you understand?"

Tom nodded. He understood. He was not kind to Lily. He was mean.

"I am sorry," Tom said.

"That's okay. Everyone makes mistakes. The important thing is to learn from them and say sorry. Do you want me to take you home?" the park keeper asked.

"Yes, please," Tom said.

The park keeper took Tom's hand and walked with him to his house. Tom saw his mom and Lily waiting for him. They were happy to see him.

"Tom, where were you? We were worried!" his mom said. She hugged him.

"I was in the park. I was playing. I was strong. But I was also silly. I threw my coat. I made Lily sad. I am sorry," Tom said.

Lily hugged him too. "It's okay, Tom. I forgive you. You are my brother. I love you," she said.

Tom smiled. He felt happy. He loved his mom. He loved his sister. He loved his coat. He was strong. But he was also kind.

"OK, mom," they say.

Lily and Tom were friends who liked to play outside. One day, they found a big tree with many fruits. They wanted to pick some fruits and eat them.

"Look, Tom, these fruits are red and sweet. Let's get some!" Lily said.

"OK, Lily, but we have to be careful. The tree is very high and the fruits are hard to reach. We need a stick or a ladder," Tom said.

They looked around and saw a long stick leaning on a fence. They ran to get it and brought it to the tree. They took turns to use the stick to poke the fruits and make them fall.

They collected many fruits and put them in a basket. They were very happy and hungry. They decided to sit under the tree and enjoy their fruits. The tree gave them shade and made them cool.

"These fruits are so yummy! I'm glad we found them," Lily said.

"Me too, Lily. They are the best fruits ever. Thank you, tree, for giving us your fruits," Tom said.

They ate and ate until they were full. They still had some fruits left in the basket. They wondered what to do with them.

"Tom, what should we do with these fruits? We can't eat them all. They will spoil if we leave them here," Lily said.

"Lily, I have an idea. Why don't we share them with our friends? They will be happy to have some fruits too. And we can play with them and have more fun," Tom said.

"That's a great idea, Tom. Sharing is caring. Let's go and find our friends and give them some fruits," Lily said.

They picked up the basket and left the tree. They met their friends on the way and gave them some fruits. Their friends were very grateful and excited. They all played together and had a wonderful time.

The moral of the story is: Sharing is caring. It is better to share what you have with others than to keep it for yourself and let it spoil. You will make others happy and have more friends. And you will also be thankful for what nature gives you.

The ball does not say anything. It just floats on the water. Anna pushes it gently with her hand. The ball makes a squeaky sound. Anna laughs. She says, "You are a silly ball. You sound like a mouse."

But then, something strange happens. The ball starts to grow bigger and bigger. It becomes as big as Anna's head, then as big as her body, then as big as the bathtub. It fills up the whole bathtub with its yellow roundness. It pushes the other toys out of the water. It makes a loud squeaky sound.

Anna is scared. She says, "Stop, ball. Stop. You are too big. You do not fit in the bathtub. You are not a toy. You are a monster."

She tries to get out of the bathtub, but the ball blocks her way. She cries for help. She says, "Mommy, daddy, help me. The ball is a monster. It is too big. It does not fit in the bathtub. It wants to eat me."

She smiles and laughs. She plays with her toys in the bathtub. She pretends that the bathtub is a big lake. She is happy.

As the sun went down, Tim saw something glow in the woods. He walked closer to see what it was. He remembered his mom's words and was careful not to go too far. The glowing thing was a little firefly. Tim smiled and said, "Hello, firefly! You make the woods less scary with your glow."

The firefly flew around Tim, and he laughed. Then, Tim went back to his tent, happy and safe. He knew that even in the dark, there were friendly things that glowed to light the way.

One day, a little boy named Tim went to the barber with his mom. Tim was very worried. He thought the barber would make him look ugly. He did not want an ugly haircut.

At the barber, Tim sat in a big chair. The barber said, "Don't worry, Tim. I will make you look nice." Tim tried not to worry, but he was still a little scared.

The barber cut Tim's hair, and soon it was all done. Tim looked in the mirror and saw that he did not look ugly at all. He looked very nice. Tim said, "Thank you, barber. I am not worried anymore." And Tim and his mom went home happy.

Once upon a time, there was a tall tree. The tree was very popular with all the birds. They loved to stand on its branches and sing. One day, a little boy named Tim came to the tree. He wanted to be friends with the birds too.

Tim said, "Hi, birds! Can I stand with you in the tree?" The birds said, "Yes, Tim! Come up and stand with us." So, Tim tried to climb the tree to stand with the birds. But, the tree was very big and Tim was very small.

As Tim tried to climb, he fell down to the earth. The birds flew away, scared. Tim was sad and hurt. He went home, and the tree was not popular anymore. The birds did not come back to stand and sing in the tree again.

Lily was scared because she couldn't ride away from the bear. But then she remembered a trick her dad taught her. She used her broken pedal to make a loud noise and scare the bear away. She was happy she remembered the trick and could ride home safely.

Once upon a time, there was a farmer who had a big field of corn. The corn was very tall and had long leaves that swayed in the wind. One day, the farmer went to check on his corn and found that some of it was missing. He looked around but couldn't find any clues as to what happened.

The next day, the farmer decided to stay up all night and keep watch over his field. As the night went on, he saw a group of crows flying towards his corn. The farmer knew that the crows loved to eat corn, so he made a loud noise to scare them away. The crows flew away, but one of them remained behind.

The farmer watched as the lone crow tried to sneak a piece of corn. But the farmer was ready and chased the crow away. From that day on, the farmer made sure to keep a close eye on his corn and the crows remained far away.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and go on adventures. One day, Lily and her friends decided to go on a picnic in the park. They packed their gear and set off on their journey.

As they were walking, Lily noticed that her friend Jack was feeling very tired. He yawned and said he wanted to go home and sleep. Lily felt bad for Jack and wanted to help him feel better. She thought of an idea and asked her friends to help her.

Together, they made a cozy bed for Jack to sleep on. They fluffed up the pillows and tucked him in with a warm blanket. Jack felt so happy and enthusiastic about his friends' kindness. He fell asleep feeling loved and cared for.

The moral of the story is that when we see someone who needs help, we should always try to do something kind for them. It can make a big difference in their day and make them feel happy and loved, just like Jack.

Once upon a time, there was a little fish named Nemo who lived in the ocean. Nemo loved to swim and play with his fish friends. One day, Nemo saw something shiny at the bottom of the ocean. He swam down to take a closer look.

As he got closer, he saw that it was a beautiful seashell. Nemo picked up the seashell and showed it to his friend, Sammy the crab. "Look, Sammy! I found a pretty seashell. It must belong to someone special," Nemo said.

Sammy looked at the seashell and said, "That seashell belongs to the queen of the ocean. She is very powerful and lives in an icy palace deep in the ocean."

Nemo was curious and wanted to meet the queen of the ocean. He swam deeper and deeper until he saw the icy palace. When he got there, he saw the queen of the ocean holding the same seashell. "That seashell belongs to you, your majesty," Nemo said.

The queen was impressed by Nemo's honesty and bravery. She thanked him and gave him a special gift. From that day on, Nemo knew that he belonged in the ocean with his fish friends and the queen of the ocean.

Sam sees the new car and wants to play with it too. He says, "Can I play with your car, Tim? It looks very fun. We can share it."

Tim gets grumpy. He says, "No, you can't. It is my car. Go away. Find your own car."

Sam gets sad. He says, "But I don't have a car like that. You have so many cars. Why can't you share?"

Tim says, "Because I don't want to. It is mine. Mine. Mine."

He pushes Sam away and grabs the car. He hugs it and says, "My car. My car. My car."

Sam starts to cry. He runs to their mom and tells her what happened. Mom comes to the room and sees Tim with the car. She says, "Tim, what are you doing? Why are you being so grumpy and selfish? You have to share your toys with your brother. He is your friend. Sharing is caring."

Tim says, "But mom, this is my car. I found it in my toy box. It is special. I don't want to share it."

Mom says, "Tim, I know you like the car, but it is not your car. It is a gift from your grandma. She sent it for both of you to play with. She wanted you to have fun and be happy. She loves you both very much. How do you think she would feel if she saw you being so grumpy and mean to your brother?"

Tim thinks for a moment. He feels bad. He says, "I'm sorry, mom. I'm sorry, Sam. I didn't know it was a gift. I was being silly. I don't want to make grandma sad. I want to make her happy. I want to make you happy. I want to make Sam happy."

He gives the car to Sam and says, "Here, Sam. You can play with the car. It is a nice car. We can share it. We can take turns. We can have fun. We can be friends."

Sam smiles and says, "Thank you, Tim. You are a good brother. I'm sorry I made you grumpy. I like the car too. It is a nice car. We can share it. We can take turns. We can have fun. We can be friends."

They hug and say, "We love you, mom. We love you, grandma. We love each other."

Mom smiles and says, "I'm proud of you, boys. You learned a good lesson today. Sharing is caring. And caring is love. And love is the best thing ever."

They play with the car and make noises and pretend to drive it on the floor. They are happy. Mom is happy. Grandma is happy. The end.

Sara and Tom are playing with blocks. They want to make a big tower, but the blocks keep falling down. Sara has an idea.

"Let's use glue!" she says. "Glue can make the blocks stick together."

"Good idea!" Tom says. He runs to get the glue from the shelf. He brings it back and gives it to Sara.

Sara opens the glue and squeezes some on the blocks. She puts one block on top of another, and then another, and another. The glue makes the blocks stay in place.

"Wow, look at our tower!" Tom says. "It's so tall and strong!"

They are very happy with their tower. They want to show it to their mom. They call her to come and see.

Mom comes and sees the tower. She smiles and claps her hands.

"Wow, what a great tower!" she says. "You two worked very well together. You supported each other with your ideas and your glue."

"Thank you, Mom!" Sara and Tom say. They hug their mom.

Then they see something hairy moving behind the couch. It is their cat, Fluffy. Fluffy is curious about the tower. He jumps on the couch and reaches for the tower with his paw.

"Uh-oh, Fluffy!" Sara and Tom say. "Don't touch our tower!"

But it is too late. Fluffy knocks down the tower with his paw. The blocks and the glue fall on the floor. Fluffy runs away.

Sara and Tom are sad. They look at their broken tower.

"Oh, no, our tower!" they say.

Mom hugs them and says, "Don't worry, my loves. You can make another tower. You still have your blocks and your glue. And you still have each other. You can always support each other, no matter what."

Sara and Tom smile and say, "You're right, Mom. We can make another tower. And we can make it even better!"

They pick up their blocks and their glue and start to build again. They are happy and proud. They love their mom and their cat, even if he is hairy and naughty.

Tim and Kim were twins who liked to play in the garden. They had a big sandbox, a slide, and a swing. They also had a dog named Spot who liked to dig holes and chase birds.

One day, Mom told them to come inside for lunch. "Tim, Kim, Spot, it's time to eat. Come on, hurry up!" she called from the kitchen.

But Tim and Kim did not want to stop playing. They wanted to build a castle in the sand. "Just a little more, Mom. We are almost done," they said.

Mom sighed. She knew they loved to play, but they also needed to eat. She decided to give them a few more minutes. She went back to the kitchen and finished making sandwiches and juice.

Meanwhile, Spot saw a big black bird on the fence. He barked and ran towards it. The bird flew away, but Spot did not stop. He jumped over the fence and followed the bird into the street.

Tim and Kim heard Spot's barking and looked up. They saw him running away from the garden. They were scared. They knew the street was dangerous. There were cars and trucks and bikes. They dropped their shovels and ran after Spot. "Spot, come back! Spot, stop!" they shouted.

Mom heard their shouting and looked out the window. She saw them running after Spot. She was very worried. She grabbed her keys and ran outside. She saw a mop leaning against the wall. She took it with her. She thought she might need it to catch Spot or to scare away the cars.

She ran after Tim and Kim and Spot. She saw them crossing the street. She saw a car coming fast. She yelled, "Tim, Kim, Spot, watch out!"

The car saw them and stopped. The driver honked his horn. He was angry. He got out of his car and said, "What are you doing? You could have been hurt. You should not run in the street. It's very serious."

Mom reached Tim and Kim and Spot. She hugged them and said, "I'm so glad you are okay. But you should not have run after Spot. You should have listened to me. It's very serious. You could have been hurt. You made me very scared."

Tim and Kim and Spot looked at Mom. They saw her face. They saw her mop. They knew they were in trouble. They said, "We are sorry, Mom. We were playing and we did not hear you. We wanted to save Spot. We did not mean to delay lunch. We did not mean to make you scared."

Mom said, "I know you love Spot, but you have to be careful. The street is not a place to play. You have to obey me when I call you. You have to come inside for lunch. You have to eat and rest. Then you can play again. But only in the garden. Do you understand?"

Tim and Kim and Spot nodded. They said, "We understand, Mom. We will obey you. We will come inside for lunch. We will eat and rest. Then we will play again. But only in the garden."

Mom smiled. She said, "That's good. Now let's go inside. Your sandwiches and juice are waiting for you. And your mop too. You have to help me clean the floor. You made it dirty with your shoes and paws. It's not serious, but it's fair."

Tim and Kim and Spot said, "Okay, Mom. We will help you clean the floor. We will use the mop. We will make it shiny. It's not serious, but it's fair."

They all went inside. They ate their lunch. They helped Mom clean the floor. They used the mop. They made it shiny. Then they played again. But only in the garden. They were happy. And Mom was happy too.

"What's wrong with Spot?" Lily asked Ben.

"I don't know. Maybe he is sick. Let's ask Mom," Ben said.

They ran to find their mom, who was in the kitchen. They told her about Spot and how he did not want to play.

"Let me see him," Mom said. She followed them to Spot's bed and checked his ears and his paws. She frowned and said, "Spot has a fever. He needs to go to the vet."

"What's a vet?" Lily asked.

"A vet is a doctor for animals. He can help Spot feel better," Mom said.

"Can we go with you?" Ben asked.

"Of course. Let's get in the car," Mom said.

They drove to the vet's office, where a nice lady with a white coat took Spot to a room. She gave him a shot and some medicine. She told Mom that Spot had a cold and that he would be fine in a few days. She also gave them some treats for Spot.

"Thank you, vet lady," Lily and Ben said.

"You're welcome. Spot is a brave and good dog. He just needs some rest and love," the vet lady said.

They took Spot home and gave him his treats. They cuddled with him on his bed and told him stories. Spot wagged his tail and licked their faces. He looked happy and not so tired.

"Spot, we love you," Lily and Ben said.

He thinks hard. How can he make his rainbow regular? He counts his blocks. He sees that he has more blocks of some colors than others. He needs to make the strips the same. He needs to use the same number of blocks for each color.

He takes some blocks away from the longer strips. He adds some blocks to the shorter strips. He moves his blocks around until he has six strips that are the same. He makes his rainbow regular. He is happy.

He looks at his rainbow. He thinks it is beautiful. He smiles. He solved his problem with his blocks. He is proud.

Tim and Sam are brothers. They like to play in the woods near their house. One day, they find a big cave. They want to see what is inside.

"Let's go in," Tim says. He is brave and curious.

"No, it is dark and scary," Sam says. He is careful and afraid.

"Come on, don't be a baby," Tim says. He walks into the cave.

Sam follows him. He does not want to be alone.

They see a lot of bones and fur on the ground. They hear a loud snore. They see a big wolf sleeping in the corner.

"Wow, look at that," Tim says. He wants to touch the wolf.

"Shh, don't wake him up," Sam says. He wants to run away.

But Tim does not listen. He goes closer to the wolf. He reaches out his hand.

The wolf opens his eyes. He sees Tim and Sam. He growls.

Tim and Sam scream. They turn around and run.

But the wolf is faster. He jumps and blocks the exit.

"Please, don't eat us," Tim says. He is sorry and scared.

"Please, be polite," Sam says. He is polite and hopeful.

The wolf looks at them. He thinks for a moment. He says:

"Polite? What does that mean?"

Tim and Sam are surprised. They did not know the wolf can talk.

"It means you are nice and kind and friendly," Sam says.

"Nice and kind and friendly?" the wolf says. "Why should I be that?"

"Because it is good and right and fair," Sam says.

"Good and right and fair?" the wolf says. "How do you know that?"

"Because our mom and dad told us," Sam says.

"Mom and dad?" the wolf says. "What are they?"

"They are our family. They love us and take care of us and teach us things," Sam says.

"Family? Love? Teach?" the wolf says. "I don't have those. I only have myself. I am alone and hungry and angry."

Tim and Sam feel sad for the wolf. They say:

"Maybe you can have those too. Maybe you can be our friend. Maybe we can share our food and play with you and learn from you."

"Friend? Share? Play? Learn?" the wolf says. "What are those?"

"They are fun and happy and good things," Sam says.

"Fun and happy and good?" the wolf says. "I never had those. I only had fear and pain and hate."

Tim and Sam feel sorry for the wolf. They say:

"Maybe you can try those. Maybe you can give them a chance. Maybe you can change your life."

"Change my life?" the wolf says. "How can I do that?"

"By being polite," Sam says.

"By being polite," Tim says.

The wolf thinks for a long time. He looks at Tim and Sam. He sees their eyes and smiles. He feels something new in his heart.

He says:

"Okay. I will try. I will be polite. I will not eat you. I will let you go. I will be your friend."

Tim and Sam are happy. They hug the wolf. They say:

"Thank you. You are polite. You are our friend."

They leave the cave. They take the wolf with them. They go to their house. They introduce the wolf to their mom and dad. They share their food and play with him and learn from him.

The wolf is happy. He has a family. He has love. He has fun. He has changed his life.

He is polite.

After a while, the little bear got tired and he wanted to go back to his cave to sleep. The butterfly understood and they said goodbye to each other. The little bear went back to his cave, curled up and fell asleep, dreaming of his fun adventure with the blue butterfly.

Once upon a time, there was a little mouse named Timmy. Timmy was very poor, and he didn't have much food to eat. One day, Timmy saw a big piece of cheese in a maze. He wanted to eat the cheese, but he didn't know how to get to it.

Timmy decided to run through the maze to find the cheese. He ran and ran, but he couldn't find it. Just when Timmy was about to give up, he saw a small hole in the wall. He ran through the hole and found himself in front of the cheese. Timmy was so happy, and he ate the cheese until his belly was full.

From that day on, Timmy knew that if he ran through the maze, he could find food to eat. He never forgot the lesson he learned, and he always ran through the maze when he was hungry.

But the eraser is not a toy. It is a magic eraser. It can erase anything. It can erase crayons and papers. It can erase animals and flowers and cars. It can erase songs.

Tim and Lily do not know. They keep playing. They draw and sing. They have fun.

But the eraser is bad. It does not like fun. It does not like drawing and singing. It wants to erase everything. It waits for a chance.

When Tim and Lily are not looking, the eraser jumps. It lands on their papers. It erases their drawings. It erases their crayons. It erases their animals and flowers and cars.

Tim and Lily turn around. They see their papers. They are blank. They see their crayons. They are gone. They see their eraser. It is smiling.

Tim and Lily are sad. They cry. They want their drawings back. They want their crayons back. They want their animals and flowers and cars back. They want their songs back.

But the eraser does not care. It is not sorry. It is happy. It has erased everything. It sings a bad song. It sings:

I am the eraser
I erase what I see
I erase your drawings
I erase your crayons
I erase your animals
I erase your flowers
I erase your cars
I erase your songs
I erase your fun
I erase you

Tim and Lily are scared. They run away. They try to hide. But the eraser follows them. It jumps and jumps. It erases everything in its way. It erases the door. It erases the window. It erases the wall. It erases the floor. It erases the sky.

Tim and Lily are gone. The eraser is alone. It has erased everything. It has nothing to play with. It has nothing to erase. It is bored. It is sad. It stops singing. It is quiet.

The end.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play in the park. They saw a big log that was lying on the ground. They wanted to walk on it like a bridge.

Tom went first. He put one foot on the log and then the other. He tried to balance, but he wobbled and fell off. He scraped his knee and cried.

Lily felt sorry for Tom. She gave him a hug and said, "It's okay, Tom. I will help you." She took his hand and they went back to the log.

This time, Lily went first. She walked slowly and carefully on the log. She did not wobble or fall off. She reached the other end and smiled.

"Come on, Tom. You can do it. Just look at me and follow me," she said.

Tom nodded and tried again. He held Lily's hand and looked at her. He walked slowly and carefully on the log. He did not wobble or fall off. He reached the other end and smiled.

They hugged each other and said, "We did it! We are mighty!" They felt happy and proud. They played on the log some more and had fun.

Lily was a little girl who liked to play with her dolls. She had many dolls, but her favorite one was Anna, who had a beautiful dress and long hair. Lily liked to pretend that Anna was a princess who lived in a big castle.

One day, Lily's mom had to work at home. She had a small office in the living room, where she had a computer and some papers. She told Lily to be quiet and not to bother her while she was working.

But Lily wanted to play with her mom. She took Anna and went to the office. She knocked on the door and said, "Mom, can you play with me and Anna? We want to have a tea party."

Mom looked at Lily and smiled. She said, "I'm sorry, honey, but I can't play with you right now. I have to finish some important work. Can you play by yourself for a little while?"

Lily did not like that answer. She felt angry and sad. She said, "No, I can't play by myself. I want you to play with me now. You always work and never play. You are a bad mom." She stamped her foot and demanded, "Play with me and Anna!"

Mom felt sorry for Lily, but she also felt annoyed. She said, "Lily, that's not nice. You can't demand things like that. You have to be patient and respectful. I love you, but I also have to do my work. Why don't you go to your room and play with your other dolls? I'll come and play with you later, I promise."

Lily did not listen to her mom. She threw Anna on the floor and started to cry. She said, "I don't want to play with my other dolls. I only want to play with you and Anna. You are a mean mom. You don't love me." She ran out of the office and slammed the door.

Mom sighed and picked up Anna from the floor. She felt sad and tired. She wished she could play with Lily, but she also had to finish her work. She hoped Lily would calm down and understand. She hugged Anna and said, "Don't worry, Anna. You are still a beautiful princess. And Lily is still a sweet girl. She just needs some time to learn how to share and wait." She put Anna on the desk and went back to her work.

"Ben, please, let's go. We should not touch these things. They belong to someone else. Maybe they are very important or very old or very special," she said.

But Ben did not care. He took more and more, until his pockets were full. He closed the chest and ran to the stairs.

"Come on, Lily, hurry up. We can hide these in our room and play with them later," he said.

Lily followed him, but she felt bad. She wished they never found the chest.

They ran down the stairs, but they did not see Mom and Dad waiting for them. They looked angry and sad.

"Ben, Lily, what have you done?" Mom asked. She saw the jewels and coins and candy falling out of Ben's pockets.

"We found a chest in the attic and we opened it and we took some things," Ben said.

"That chest was your great-grandma's. She left it for us when she died. It had her most precious memories and gifts. You broke the lock and stole her things. How could you?" Dad asked.

Ben and Lily felt ashamed. They realized they made a big mistake. They wanted to say sorry, but it was too late.

Mom and Dad took them to their room and locked the door. They said they were very disappointed and angry. They said they had to think about a punishment.

Ben and Lily cried. They wished they listened to Lily and asked Mom or Dad first. They wished they did not choose to be greedy and selfish. They learned a difficult lesson: respect other people's things and always tell the truth.

Lily understood and went back outside to play. She saw the pine tree again and instead of hugging it, she gently touched its needles. "I'm sorry I got mad at you, pine tree. You're still my friend," she said. 

Just then, a gust of wind blew a pine cone and it hit Lily's cheek. "Ow! That hurt!" she yelled. 

Her mom came outside and asked what happened. "The pine cone slapped me!" Lily said. 

Her mom smiled and said, "Well, sometimes even friends can accidentally hurt each other. But it's important to forgive and move on. Just like you did with the pine tree." 

Lily nodded and went back to playing, happy to have learned a valuable lesson about forgiveness and friendship.

They looked at the wand. They decided to put it back in the box. They said, "Let's never play with the magic wand again!" They went to dry themselves and find something else to do. They hoped the rain would stop soon.

But Tom was still sad. He had lost his worms and his finger hurt. He wished he had quit playing with worms when his mom and dad told him to. He learned a hard lesson.

"Come on, Ben, let's go see the mill!" Anna said.

"OK, Anna, but be careful. The water is fast and deep," Ben said.

They ran to the mill and climbed on a big rock. They could hear the water splashing and the wheel creaking. They saw a hose that came out of the mill. It was spraying water into the air.

"Wow, look at that, Anna! The mill is making a fountain!" Ben said.

"Let's go touch it, Ben! It looks fun!" Anna said.

She jumped off the rock and ran to the hose. She reached out her hand to feel the water. But the water was too strong and it pushed her back. She fell on the ground and got wet.

"Anna, are you OK?" Ben shouted. He was worried about his sister.

He jumped off the rock and ran to help her. He lifted her up and hugged her.

"I'm OK, Ben, but I'm wet and cold," Anna said.

"Me too, Anna, me too. Let's go back to Mom and Dad. They will dry us and warm us," Ben said.

They ran back to their parents, who were sitting on a bench. They saw their children wet and muddy.

"What happened, Anna and Ben? Did you fall in the water?" Mom asked.

"No, Mom, we were playing with the mill. It was spraying water and we wanted to touch it. But it was too strong and it pushed us back," Anna said.

"Oh, you silly kids. You should be careful with the water. It can be dangerous. Come here, let's dry you and change your clothes," Dad said.

He took out a towel and some clothes from his bag. He dried Anna and Ben and helped them change. He gave them a hug and a kiss.

"Are you feeling better, Anna and Ben?" Dad asked.

"Yes, Dad, thank you. We're sorry we got wet and dirty," Anna and Ben said.

"It's OK, Anna and Ben. We're glad you're OK. But next time, be more careful with the water, OK?" Mom said.

"OK, Mom, we will. We love you, Mom and Dad," Anna and Ben said.

They smiled and cuddled with their parents. They learned a lesson about the water and the mill. They still liked the mill, but they didn't want to spray it anymore.

"Give me the cushion!" Ben shouted. "It's mine!"

"No, it's mine!" Lily shouted back. "I saw it first!"

Suddenly, the wind pushed the cushion out of their hands. The cushion flew out of the window and into the street. Lily and Ben watched in horror as a car ran over the cushion and made it flat.

"Oh no!" Lily cried. "Our cushion!"

Lena was a lively girl who liked to play and sing. She had a big sister, Sara, who was getting married soon. Sara had a beautiful white veil that she would wear on her wedding day. Lena wanted to try on the veil and pretend to be a bride too.

One day, when Sara was not at home, Lena sneaked into her room and found the veil on the bed. She put it on her head and looked at herself in the mirror. She felt very pretty and happy. She started to rock back and forth, humming a song. She did not notice that the veil was getting caught on the bedpost.

Suddenly, she heard Sara's voice outside the door. "Lena, what are you doing in my room?" Sara asked, sounding angry. Lena got scared and tried to run away, but the veil was stuck. She pulled hard and ripped the veil in half. She dropped it on the floor and ran to her room, crying.

Sara came in and saw the torn veil. She was very sad and angry. She had saved a lot of money to buy the veil and now it was ruined. She went to Lena's room and knocked on the door. "Lena, how could you do this? You know how much this veil means to me. You are very naughty and selfish. You have to say sorry and help me fix it." Sara said, sternly.

Lena opened the door and looked at Sara with tearful eyes. She felt very sorry and ashamed. She knew she had done a bad thing. She hugged Sara and said, "I'm sorry, Sara. I just wanted to be like you. You are so pretty and happy. I love you, Sara. Please don't be mad at me. I will help you fix the veil. I will do anything to make you happy."

Sara hugged Lena back and said, "I love you too, Lena. I know you didn't mean to hurt me. You are also pretty and happy, in your own way. You don't have to be like me. You have to be yourself. And you have to respect other people's things. You can't take them without asking. That is not nice. Do you understand?"

Lena nodded and said, "I understand, Sara. I'm sorry. I will never do it again. Can we still be friends?"

Sara smiled and said, "Of course we can. You are my sister and my friend. Come on, let's go and see if we can fix the veil together. Maybe we can make it even more beautiful."

The end.

Moral value: The story teaches the value of respect, honesty, apology, forgiveness, and love. It shows that taking other people's things without permission is wrong and can cause harm. It also shows that everyone is unique and special, and does not have to imitate others. It also shows that siblings can overcome conflicts and help each other.

Sara wanted to go and see the other elephants. She asked her dad, "Can we go and see the elephants, dad?"

Dad said, "Yes, we can, Sara. But we have to be careful and not get too close. The elephants are not used to people and they might get scared or angry. We have to stay behind the fence and not touch them or feed them. We can just look and call them and say hello."

The elephants waved their noses and said goodbye to Sara. They said, "Goodbye, Sara. We will miss you, too. You are the best human we ever met. You are very brave and curious and nosy. You made us happy and proud. We hope you have a good day and a happy life. Take care, Sara. We love you."

Anna and Ben were twins who liked to play in the kitchen. They wanted to be chefs like their mom and dad. One day, they found a big jar of pepper on the counter. They opened it and smelled it. It made them sneeze.

"Let's make some soup with pepper," Ben said. "It will be yummy and spicy."

"Okay," Anna said. "But we have to be careful. Mom and dad said not to touch the stove. It is hot and dangerous."

They took a big pot and filled it with water. They put it on the stove, but they did not turn it on. They added some carrots, potatoes, and salt. Then they poured a lot of pepper into the pot. They stirred it with a wooden spoon.

"Look, we made soup!" Anna said. "It smells good."

"Let's taste it," Ben said. He took a spoonful of soup and put it in his mouth. He spat it out right away. It was too spicy. It burned his tongue. He cried.

"Ow, ow, ow!" he said. "It hurts! It hurts!"

Anna wanted to help him. She ran to the fridge to get some milk. But she did not see the rug on the floor. She stumbled and fell. She hurt her knee. She cried too.

"Ow, ow, ow!" she said. "It hurts! It hurts!"

Mom and dad heard their cries. They came to the kitchen and saw the mess. They saw the pot of soup, the jar of pepper, the spilled milk, and the twins on the floor.

"What happened here?" mom asked.

"We wanted to make soup with pepper," Anna said. "But it was too spicy and we got hurt."

Mom and dad hugged them and kissed their wounds. They gave them some water and ice cream to cool their mouths and knees.

"I'm sorry, mom and dad," Ben said. "We should have listened to you. We should not have played with the stove and the pepper."

"I'm sorry too," Anna said. "We should have been more careful. We should not have run in the kitchen."

Mom and dad smiled and said, "It's okay. We forgive you. We know you were curious and wanted to have fun. But you have to remember that some things are not for playing. They are for grown-ups. They can be dangerous or harmful. You have to ask us before you use them. And you have to be safe and respectful in the kitchen. It is not a playground. It is a place to cook and eat."

The twins nodded and said, "We understand. We will do better next time. We love you, mom and dad."

Mom and dad said, "We love you too, Anna and Ben. You are our little chefs. But you still have a lot to learn. Maybe next time we can make soup together. But with less pepper."

The twins laughed and said, "Yes, please. That sounds good."

The end.

Moral value: The story teaches the children to listen to their parents, to be careful and respectful in the kitchen, and to avoid playing with dangerous or harmful things. It also shows the importance of forgiveness and love.

Tom was a young boy who liked to help his dad with the wood. His dad had a big axe that he used to chop the wood. Tom wanted to use the axe too, but his dad said it was too sharp and heavy for him.

One day, Tom saw the axe lying on the ground near the woodpile. He thought his dad was not looking, so he ran to the axe and tried to lift it. But the axe was too heavy for him, and he dropped it on a rock. The axe made a loud clang and the blade broke.

Tom was scared and sad. He broke his dad's axe. He did not know what to do. He hid the axe behind some bushes and ran to his room.

His dad heard the clang and went to see what happened. He saw the broken axe and the rock. He knew Tom had tried to use the axe. He was angry and worried. He went to Tom's room and knocked on the door.

"Tom, come out. I need to talk to you," his dad said.

Tom opened the door and looked at his dad. He saw his dad's angry face and felt sorry.

"Dad, I'm sorry. I broke your axe. I wanted to help you with the wood. I did not mean to break it," Tom said.

His dad sighed and hugged him.

"Tom, I'm glad you are sorry. But you should not touch my axe. It is dangerous and not for you. You could have hurt yourself or someone else. You need to be careful and listen to me," his dad said.

"I know, dad. I'm sorry. I won't touch your axe again. Can you fix it?" Tom asked.

His dad smiled and nodded.

"Yes, I can fix it. I can repair it with some glue and a new handle. But you have to help me. You have to find the broken piece and bring it to me. And you have to promise me you will never touch my axe again," his dad said.

"I promise, dad. I will help you. I will find the broken piece and bring it to you. And I will never touch your axe again," Tom said.

Tom and his dad went to the woodpile and found the broken piece. They took it to the shed and repaired the axe. They worked together and had fun. Tom learned how to repair things and his dad forgave him. They hugged and said they loved each other. They were happy.

Anna is scared and angry. She jumps off her bed and tries to get her diary back. She says, "No, give it back! It's mine! It's private!"

Tom laughs and runs away with the diary. He says, "Too bad, I'm going to read it and tell everyone your secrets!"

Anna cries and follows him. She hopes he does not open the lock. She thinks Tom is a poor brother. She wishes he would leave her alone. She wants her diary back. She wonders what she can do.

Ben and Sam ran to the man. They wanted to buy some toys. They had some money from their piggy bank. They looked at the toys. They saw cars, dolls, balls, and puzzles. They also saw a green box. The box was dull and had no picture on it.

"It is a surprise toy. It is very fun and special. You can have it for only one dollar," the man said.

Ben and Sam were curious. They wanted to see the surprise toy. They gave the man one dollar and took the green box. They ran back to their house. They opened the box.

But there was no toy in the box. There was only a rock. A dull, gray rock. Ben and Sam were sad and angry. They had wasted their money. They had no new toy. They had been tricked by the man.

They tried to find the man and his truck. But he was gone. He had driven away with his toys and their money. Ben and Sam cried. They wished they had not bought the green box. They wished they had bought a car or a doll or a ball or a puzzle instead. They learned a hard lesson. They learned to be careful and not trust strangers. Bunny was a little rabbit who loved to hop around the meadow. He liked to explore new places and meet new friends. One day, he saw a big pond with shiny water and green plants. He wanted to hop closer and see what was inside.

But Frog, who lived in the pond, did not like strangers. He saw Bunny hopping near his home and croaked loudly. "Who are you and what do you want?" he asked in a grumpy voice.

Bunny was scared and anxious. He did not know how to answer Frog's question. He thought Frog might be angry or mean. He wanted to hop away, but he also wanted to be polite. He said in a small voice, "I am Bunny and I just want to look at the pond. It is very pretty."

Frog was surprised by Bunny's answer. He realized that Bunny was not a threat, but a curious and friendly visitor. He felt sorry for being rude and decided to be nice. He said in a softer voice, "I am Frog and this is my home. You can look at the pond, but be careful not to fall in. The water is deep and cold."

Bunny was relieved and happy. He thanked Frog and hopped closer to the pond. He saw fish and ducks and water lilies. He asked Frog many questions and learned a lot. Frog answered patiently and shared his knowledge. They became friends and had fun.

The moral of the story is: Don't judge someone by their appearance or voice. Be kind and respectful to others and you might make a new friend.

Lily and Tom were twins who liked to play together. One day, they found a candle in a drawer and decided to light it. They thought it was fun to watch the flame flicker and make shadows on the wall.

"Look, Lily, the candle is so pretty!" Tom said.

"Yes, Tom, it is. But we have to be careful. Mommy said candles can be hot and dangerous," Lily said.

They played with the candle for a while, but then they heard Mommy calling them for dinner. They ran to the kitchen, forgetting to blow out the candle.

The candle burned slowly on the table, until it reached a paper napkin. The napkin caught fire and soon the whole table was on fire. Smoke filled the room and the fire alarm went off.

Mommy smelled the smoke and ran to the living room. She saw the fire and grabbed a blanket to put it out. She was very scared and angry.

"Lily! Tom! What have you done? You could have burned the house down! How could you play with a candle?" Mommy shouted.

Lily and Tom came back to the living room and saw the mess. They felt very sorry and ashamed. They hugged Mommy and cried.

"We're sorry, Mommy. We didn't mean to. We just wanted to see the candle. We forgot to blow it out. We love you, Mommy. Please don't be mad at us," they said.

Mommy hugged them back and calmed down. She was glad they were not hurt, but she was still upset.

"I love you too, Lily and Tom. But you have to listen to me. Candles are not toys. They are for grown-ups only. They can cause fire and hurt people. You have to be more careful and responsible. Do you understand?" Mommy said.

"Yes, Mommy. We understand. We're sorry. We won't play with candles again. We learned our lesson. We don't want to miss you or our home," they said.

Mommy kissed them and took them to dinner. She hoped they would remember their mistake and never do it again. She also hoped they would always appreciate what they have and not take it for granted. She knew they were good kids who made a bad choice. She loved them very much.

Lily felt angry. She wanted to see the stone too. She tried to take it from Ben, but he pulled it away.

"Hey, stop it!" Ben said. "It's mine! I found it first!"

"That's not fair!" Lily said. "You're being rude! We're supposed to share!"

Ben stuck out his tongue and ran away. He wanted to keep the diamond for himself. He thought it was very special and valuable.

Lily ran after him. She wanted to tell him that he was wrong. She had learned about diamonds in a book. They were not real stones. They were made by people. They were not worth anything in the park. They were only for grown-ups who liked to wear them on their fingers or necks.

She caught up with Ben and shouted at him.

"Ben, wait! Listen to me! That's not a diamond! It's fake! It's just glass!"

Ben stopped and looked at her. He did not believe her. He thought she was lying. He wanted to make him give her the stone.

"No, it's not! It's a diamond! It's real! You're just jealous!" Ben said.

He held the stone up to his eye and looked at it. He saw the colors of the rainbow. He smiled. He thought it was beautiful.

Lily shook her head. She felt sad. She realized that Ben was not a good friend. He did not care about her. He only cared about the stone. She decided to leave him alone. She turned around and walked back to the sand. She hoped to find a real treasure. A treasure that was not rude. A treasure that she could share.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to watch television after lunch. They sit on the sofa and hold the remote. They press the buttons to change the channels.

One day, they see a show about animals. They see a big cat with stripes. It is a tiger. The tiger is in a cage. It looks sad. Anna and Ben feel sorry for the tiger.

"Can we help the tiger?" Anna asks Ben.

"I don't know," Ben says. "Maybe we can rub its fur. It might feel better."

They get up from the sofa and walk to the television. They reach out their hands and try to rub the tiger's fur. But they are clumsy. They bump into the television and make it fall. It makes a loud noise and breaks.

"Oh no!" Anna and Ben say. They are scared. They run back to the sofa and hide under a blanket.

Mom hears the noise and comes to the living room. She sees the broken television and the twins under the blanket. She is angry.

"What did you do?" Mom asks.

"We wanted to help the tiger," Anna says.

"We tried to rub its fur," Ben says.

Mom sighs. She is not happy. She tells the twins that they cannot touch the television. It is not a real tiger. It is a picture. They can only watch it, not rub it.

She picks up the television and takes it to the garage. She says she will try to fix it later. She tells the twins to play with their toys instead. She gives them a hug and a kiss. She says she loves them, but they have to be careful.

Anna and Ben say they are sorry. They promise to be careful. They play with their toys and forget about the tiger. They hope Mom can fix the television soon. They want to watch more shows about animals. But they will not try to rub them anymore.

Sara and her mom went to the park. Sara liked to play on the swings and the slide. Her mom sat on a bench and watched her. She had a big purse with snacks and water.

"Mom, can I have some water?" Sara asked. She was thirsty from running and jumping.

"Sure, honey. Come here and I'll give you some." Her mom opened her purse and took out a bottle of water.

Sara ran to her mom and stretched her arms to reach the bottle. But she was too short. She tried to jump, but she still could not get it.

"Here, let me help you." Her mom lifted Sara up and gave her the bottle. Sara drank some water and said, "Thank you, mom. You are the best."

"You're welcome, sweetie. Be careful, don't spill the water." Her mom said.

Sara nodded and ran back to the playground. She wanted to go on the slide again. But when she got there, she saw that the slide was wet. Someone had poured water on it. It looked slippery and shiny.

"Who did this?" Sara wondered. She saw a boy with a bucket near the slide. He was laughing and splashing water on the slide.

"Hey, stop that!" Sara shouted. "You are making the slide wet. That's not nice."

The boy looked at Sara and said, "So what? It's fun. You can slide faster when it's wet. Watch me." He climbed up the slide and slid down. He went very fast and landed on the grass.

Sara did not think it was fun. She thought it was dangerous and rude. She did not want to slide on the wet slide. She wanted to tell her mom. She ran to the bench where her mom was. But when she got there, she saw that her mom's purse was wet too. The boy had splashed water on it when he slid down.

"Oh no!" Sara cried. "Mom, look! Your purse is wet. The boy did it. He made the slide wet too. He is a bad boy."

Her mom looked at her purse and frowned. She saw that her snacks and water were wet and soggy. She was not happy. She said, "That's not nice at all. He should not do that. Let's go and talk to him. Maybe he will say sorry and stop."

Sara and her mom went to the slide and found the boy. They told him that he was wrong to splash water on the slide and the purse. They asked him to say sorry and stop.

The boy looked at them and said, "Sorry. I was just having fun. I didn't mean to make you mad. I won't do it again."

Sara and her mom accepted his apology and thanked him. They hoped he would be more careful and respectful next time. They decided to go to another part of the park where it was dry and clean. They had fun playing together and forgot about the wet slide and the wet purse.

The rose does not say anything. It just stands there. Anna feels sad. She thinks the rose does not like her. She says, "Please, rose, talk to me. I want to play with you."

Anna turns around and sees her mom. She says, "Mom, look at this rose! It is so great! But it does not talk to me. Why not?"

Ben and Lily liked to play with their toys in the garden. They had a big box of toys with cars, dolls, balls and animals. One day, they found a new toy in the box. It was a sheep. It was white and soft and had a button on its back.

"What does this button do?" Ben asked.

"Let's press it and see," Lily said.

They pressed the button and the sheep made a sound. "Baa, baa," it said. Ben and Lily laughed. They liked the sheep. It was lovely.

They played with the sheep for a long time. They made it run, jump and roll. They gave it grass to eat and water to drink. They hugged it and kissed it. They named it Fluffy.

But they did not know that the button had another function. Every time they pressed it, the sheep shrank a little bit. It was so small that they did not notice at first. But after a while, they saw that the sheep was much smaller than before.

"Look, Fluffy is tiny!" Ben said.

"Oh no, what happened?" Lily said.

They pressed the button again, hoping to make Fluffy bigger. But it did not work. The sheep shrank even more. It was now the size of a mouse.

"Stop, stop, don't press it anymore!" Ben said.

But it was too late. They pressed the button one more time, and Fluffy disappeared. It was gone.

"Where is Fluffy?" Lily cried.

"I don't know, I can't see it," Ben said.

They looked everywhere for Fluffy. They searched the box, the grass, the flowers, the rocks. But they could not find it. They were very sad. They had lost their lovely sheep.

They went inside the house and told their mom what happened. She hugged them and said, "I'm sorry, my dears. Fluffy was a magic sheep. It was a gift from your uncle. He is a magician. He wanted to surprise you with a special toy. But he forgot to tell you how to use it. You have to press the button twice to make it bigger, not once. Once makes it smaller."

"Can we get Fluffy back?" Ben asked.

"Maybe, if we call your uncle. He might know where Fluffy went. Maybe he can bring it back. But you have to be careful with magic toys. They can be tricky. Next time, ask me before you play with them, okay?" Mom said.

"Okay, Mom," Ben and Lily said.

They hoped that their uncle would find Fluffy and bring it back. They missed their lovely sheep. They learned a lesson. They would never press a button without knowing what it does.

"Uh oh!" Tim says. "What can we do?"

"Excuse me, lady!" Tim says. "Can you help us? The zip is stuck!"

"Don't worry, boys!" she says. "I can fix it. Hold still!"

She cuts the zip with the scissors. The vest opens. Sam takes it off. He is free!

"Thank you, lady!" Sam says. "You are very nice!"

"You're welcome, boys!" she says. "But be careful with zips. They can be tricky!"

Max was sad. He wanted to play with Lila, but she was too busy being a guard. He barked and wagged his tail, but Lila ignored him. He tried to sneak past her, but she blocked him with her shield. He whimpered and lay down on the grass, feeling lonely.

Bella was a bunny who loved to bounce. She bounced all day in the garden, in the house, and even on her bed. She bounced so much that sometimes she bumped into things and hurt herself. But she did not care, because bouncing was fun.

One day, she bounced too high and hit her head on a branch. She felt a big pain and started to cry. Her mom heard her and ran to see what happened. She saw the bump on Bella's head and said, "Oh, my poor baby, you need to see the veterinarian. He will make you feel better."

Bella did not want to go to the veterinarian. She was scared of the big building, the strange smells, and the other animals. She said, "No, mom, I don't want to go. I want to stay here and bounce."

Her mom said, "Bella, you have to go. The veterinarian is a nice person who helps animals. He will check your head and give you some medicine. If you don't go, your bump might get worse and you might not be able to bounce anymore."

Bella did not like that idea. She loved bouncing more than anything. She said, "Okay, mom, I will go. But only if you come with me and hold my hand."

Her mom said, "Of course, I will come with you and hold your hand. I love you, Bella."

They went to the veterinarian, who was very kind and gentle. He looked at Bella's head and said, "You have a small cut, but nothing serious. I will clean it and put a bandage on it. It will heal soon. But you have to be careful when you bounce. Don't bounce too high or too fast, and watch out for branches and other things. Bouncing is fun, but safety is important too."

Bella said, "Thank you, veterinarian. I will be careful. I'm sorry I was scared of you. You are a good person."

The veterinarian said, "You're welcome, Bella. You are a brave bunny. And you have a good mom who cares for you. Here, have a carrot. It's delicious and good for you."

Bella ate the carrot and smiled. She felt better and happier. She said, "Thank you, mom, for taking me to the veterinarian. I love you, mom."

Her mom said, "I love you too, Bella. Now let's go home and rest. You can bounce again tomorrow, but not too much."

Bella nodded and hugged her mom. She learned that bouncing was fun, but not worth getting hurt. She also learned that the veterinarian was a friend, not a foe. And she learned that her mom was always there for her. She was a lucky bunny.

He takes the ball from Anna and shakes it. The picture of the temple changes and becomes snowy and sparkly. Ben says, "Wow, this is cool. The temple is in the snow now. Maybe it is a snow globe."

Anna says, "Can I try, Ben? Please?"

Ben gives the ball back to Anna and she shakes it too. The picture of the temple changes again and becomes sunny and colorful. Anna says, "Look, Ben, the temple is in the sun now. Maybe it is a rainbow globe."

They take turns shaking the ball and watching the temple change. They are very happy and amazed by the magic ball.

But they don't know that the ball is very delicate and can break easily. They shake it too hard and too fast. The ball slips from their hands and falls on the floor. It cracks and the water and the picture spill out.

Anna and Ben are very sad and sorry. They say, "Oh no, we broke the magic ball. It was so pretty and fun. What can we do?"

They pick up the pieces and try to fix the ball. But they can't. The ball is too delicate and too broken. They hug each other and say, "We are sorry, magic ball. We didn't mean to break you. We hope you can forgive us."

Lily and Ben are playing in the kitchen. They see a big onion on the table. Lily wants to cut it with a knife. Ben says no.

"That is difficult. You can hurt yourself. Mommy says only big people can cut onions," Ben says.

But Lily does not listen. She takes the knife and tries to cut the onion. She makes a big mess. The onion makes her eyes water. She cries.

"Help! Help!" Lily shouts.

Mommy hears Lily and rushes to the kitchen. She sees the onion, the knife and the tears. She is angry and worried.

"What are you doing, Lily? You could have cut yourself! That is very dangerous. You should never play with knives. And onions are not toys. They are for cooking," Mommy says.

She takes the knife and the onion away. She hugs Lily and wipes her eyes. She tells Ben to get a band-aid, just in case. She says sorry to the onion.

"Next time, listen to your brother. He is right. Cutting onions is difficult and not for little kids. Maybe when you are older, I can teach you how to do it safely. But for now, let's find something else to play with. How about some blocks?" Mommy says.

Lily and Ben nod. They say sorry to Mommy and to the onion. They go to the living room and play with the blocks. They are happy. The onion is happy too.

Tom and Sam are brothers. They like to play in the park. But the park has a big road next to it. The road is dangerous. There are many cars and trucks that go fast and make noise.

One day, Tom and Sam are playing with a ball. The ball is red and shiny. They throw the ball to each other and catch it. They have fun. But then, the ball goes too far. It goes over the fence and onto the road.

Tom runs after the ball. He does not look at the road. He does not see the cars and trucks. He only sees the ball. Sam sees Tom run. He is scared. He shouts to Tom.

"Tom, stop! Come back! The road is dangerous!"

But Tom does not hear Sam. He hears the ball. He reaches the ball. He picks it up. He smiles. He turns around. He sees a big truck. The truck is coming fast. The truck is loud. The truck does not see Tom.

Sam sees the truck. He shouts louder.

"Tom, watch out! The truck is coming!"

But it is too late. The truck hits Tom. Tom falls down. The ball flies away. Sam runs to Tom. He cries. He calls for help.

"Help! Help! Someone help Tom!"

But no one comes. The park is empty. The road is quiet. Tom does not move. Tom does not breathe. Tom is gone. Sam is alone. He is sad. He is sorry. He wishes he had listened to his mom. His mom had given him an order.

"Boys, do not play near the road. The road is dangerous. Stay in the park. Be careful."

But they did not listen. They did not obey. They did not follow the order. They played near the road. They were not careful. They were in danger. And now, Tom is dead. And Sam is alive. But he wishes he was not.

Lily did not like the pill that Mom gave her. It was big and white and tasted weird. Mom said it would make her feel better, but Lily did not believe her.

"Please, Lily, swallow the pill. It will help you with your cough and your fever," Mom urged.

Lily shook her head and hid under the blanket. She did not want the pill. She wanted juice and a hug.

Mom sighed and sat on the bed. She lifted the blanket and smiled at Lily.

"I know you don't like the pill, but it is good for you. How about this? If you take the pill, I will give you some juice and a hug. And we can read your favorite book together. How does that sound?"

Lily thought for a moment. She liked juice and hugs and books. Maybe the pill was not so bad after all.

"Okay, Mom. I will try the pill. But you have to stay with me," she said.

Mom nodded and hugged Lily. She gave her the pill and a glass of juice. Lily made a face and swallowed the pill. It was still weird, but not as bad as she thought.

"Good girl, Lily. I'm proud of you. Now, let's cuddle and read your book. Which one do you want?"

Lily smiled and pointed to the book with the bunny on the cover. She snuggled with Mom and listened to the story. She felt a little warmer and happier. Maybe the pill did help her after all.

One day, Lily was playing with Silver in her room, when she heard a loud noise. She ran to the window and saw a big truck outside. The truck was taking away some old things from her neighbor's house. Lily saw a big box on the truck. She gasped. It was her box of old toys that she did not want anymore.

I didn't know Silver was in that box. Maybe we can find another doll like her. Or maybe you can make a new friend with one of your other dolls."

"Wow, that is cool!" Tom said. He wanted to see the octopus better. He ran to the water and got closer to the rock. He did not listen to mom, who told him to be careful and stay away.

The octopus saw Tom and did not like him. It felt scared and angry. It twisted its arms and grabbed Tom's leg. It pulled him into the water. Tom screamed and tried to get free, but the octopus was too strong.

Mom and dad heard Tom and ran to help him. They saw the octopus and Tom in the water. They were scared and sad. They tried to get the octopus off Tom, but it was too late. The octopus had bitten Tom and made him bleed. Tom was hurt and sick. He did not wake up.

The octopus let go of Tom and swam away. It was not hungry anymore. It had eaten a yummy snack. It did not care about Tom or his family. It only cared about itself. It was a bad octopus.

One day, Lily and Ben are drawing animals. Lily draws a cat. Ben draws a dog. But Ben makes a mistake. He draws the dog's tail too long. He tries to erase it, but his eraser is too small. He asks Lily to share her eraser.
