One day, a little boy named Ben saw a big dragon in the sky. He was not afraid, he was curious. He wanted to talk to the dragon and make friends.

"Hello, dragon!" he shouted. "Can you come down and play with me?"

The dragon heard the boy and flew down to the ground. He was a friendly dragon, but he was also ignorant. He did not know much about people and their things.

"Hello, little one," he said. "What do you want to play?"

Ben smiled and pointed to his toy car. "This is my car. It can go fast and make noises. Do you want to try?"

The dragon nodded and picked up the car with his claws. He tried to make it go, but he did not know how. He pushed it, he pulled it, he shook it, but nothing happened. He got frustrated and angry.

"This car is broken!" he roared. "It does not work!"

He threw the car away and it landed on a rock. It broke into pieces. Ben was sad and angry too.

"No, dragon, no!" he cried. "You broke my car! You are ignorant! You do not know how to play!"

The dragon felt sorry and ashamed. He did not mean to break the car. He did not know it was important to the boy.

"I am sorry, little one," he said. "I did not know. I am ignorant. I do not know much about your things. But I can provide something else for you. I can provide fire."

He opened his mouth and breathed out a stream of fire. He made shapes and patterns with the fire in the air. He made a circle, a star, a heart, and a smiley face. He hoped the boy would like it.

Ben watched the fire and forgot about his car. He was amazed and happy. He liked the fire. He liked the dragon.

"Wow, dragon, wow!" he exclaimed. "You can provide fire! That is amazing! You are not ignorant, you are smart! You know how to make fire!"

He clapped his hands and laughed. He ran to the dragon and hugged his neck. The dragon hugged him back with his wings. They became friends. They played with fire and had fun.

Once upon a time, in a cool green park, there lived a little cat named Tom. Tom loved to play and run around the park. One day, Tom saw a big tree and wanted to climb it.

Tom started to step on the tree slowly. As he climbed higher, he saw a bird on a branch. "Hello, bird!" Tom said. "Do you want to play with me?" The bird looked at Tom and said, "No, thank you. I am going to take a nap." Tom felt sad but kept climbing the tree.

At the top of the tree, Tom found a nice spot to rest. He decided to take a nap too. As Tom slept, the cool wind blew gently. When Tom woke up, he saw the bird flying down to play with him. They played all day long and became good friends.

Here is one possible story, but there are many other ways to write it.

Sam and Mia liked to play heroes and villains. Sam was the hero and Mia was the villain. They used sticks as swords and pillows as shields. They ran around the house and pretended to fight.

One day, they found a new toy in the basement. It was a big gun that made a loud noise and flashed a blue light. Mia picked it up and said, "This is my freeze gun. I can freeze you with it and make you my prisoner."

Sam said, "No, you can't. I have my shield. It will protect me from your freeze gun." He held his pillow in front of him and smiled.

Mia aimed the freeze gun at Sam and pulled the trigger. The blue light hit the pillow and bounced back. It hit Mia in the chest and she felt very cold. She dropped the freeze gun and fell to the floor. She could not move or speak. She was frozen.

Sam saw what happened and ran to Mia. He tried to warm her up with his hands and his breath. He said, "Mia, Mia, wake up. I'm sorry. I didn't mean to freeze you. Please, wake up."

But Mia did not wake up. She stayed frozen. Sam started to cry. He wished he had not played with the freeze gun. He wished he had been more modest and not tried to be a hero. He wished he had listened to his mom, who had told him not to go to the basement. He wished he could go back in time and change everything. But he could not. He had made a big mistake and he had to live with it. He had lost his best friend.

Tom and Lily were playful twins who liked to run and hide. One day, they saw a big maze in the park. They wanted to go inside and explore. But their mom said no. She said the maze was not for children. It was for grown-ups who paid money.

Tom and Lily did not listen. They waited until their mom was busy. Then they ran to the maze and sneaked in. They thought it was fun to find their way through the paths and walls. They laughed and shouted.

But soon they got lost. They could not see the exit. They could not see their mom. They could not see each other. They were scared and alone. They cried and called for help.

A man heard them. He came to the maze. He saw Tom and Lily. He did not look nice. He looked mean. He had a big bag. He said he would help them. But he lied. He grabbed Tom and Lily and put them in his bag. He wanted to steal them. He ran away with them.

Their mom heard them scream. She looked for them. She saw the man with the bag. She ran after him. She shouted for help. But it was too late. The man was faster. He got in a car and drove away. He took Tom and Lily with him. Their mom could not catch him. She could not save them. She was very sad. She wished they had listened to her.

Lily was a shy girl who liked to play with her dolls. She did not talk much to the other kids at school. She was afraid they would laugh at her or be mean to her.

One day, a new boy came to her class. His name was Max. He had curly hair and a big smile. He sat next to Lily and said hello. Lily did not say anything. She looked down at her desk and hoped he would go away.

Max did not go away. He wanted to be friends with Lily. He saw her dolls and asked if he could play with them. Lily shook her head and hugged her dolls tighter. Max did not give up. He poked Lily gently on the arm and said, "Please, can I play with you? I like dolls too. They are fun and pretty."

Lily felt the poke and looked up at Max. She saw his smile and his kind eyes. She felt a warm feeling in her chest. She wondered if he was really nice and not mean. She decided to give him a chance. She nodded and said, "Okay, you can play with me. But be careful with my dolls. They are my friends."

Max was happy. He thanked Lily and picked up a doll. He said, "This one is my favorite. She has a pink dress and a bow. What is her name?" Lily smiled and said, "Her name is Rose. She is my favorite too. She likes hugs and stories." Max said, "Me too. Can I hug her?" Lily said, "Yes, you can. But only if I can hug this one." She pointed to a doll with a blue shirt and a hat. Max said, "Sure, you can. His name is Jack. He likes jokes and games." Lily said, "I like jokes and games too. Do you know any jokes?" Max said, "Yes, I do. Do you want to hear one?" Lily said, "Yes, please."

They laughed and played with the dolls. They told jokes and stories. They hugged the dolls and each other. They became friends. Lily was not shy anymore. She was happy.

Sam and Tom are brothers. They like to play outside in the mud. They make mud pies and mud castles. They have fun, but they get very filthy.

"Boys, time for your meal!" Mom calls from the kitchen. "Come inside and bathe first!"

Sam and Tom run to the bathroom. They take off their clothes and jump in the tub. They splash water and soap on each other. They wash their hair and their faces. They rinse off the mud and the dirt.

"Look, we are clean now!" Sam says to Tom.

"Yes, we are!" Tom says to Sam.

They dry themselves with towels and put on fresh clothes. They go to the kitchen and sit at the table. Mom serves them soup and bread. They eat their meal and say thank you to Mom.

"Did you have fun playing outside?" Mom asks them.

"Yes, we did!" Sam and Tom say together.

"But we also like to bathe and eat!" Sam adds.

Mom smiles and hugs them. She is happy that they are clean and full. She loves her boys.

Tom and Lily were playing in the sand. They liked to make castles and dig holes. They had a bucket and a shovel each. They were having fun.

But then Tom saw something shiny in the sand. He dug it out with his shovel. It was a necklace with a blue stone. Tom liked it. He put it around his neck.

Lily saw the necklace and wanted it. She said, "Give me the necklace, Tom. It is mine." Tom said, "No, it is mine. I found it." They started to fight.

A man was walking by. He saw them fighting. He said, "Stop fighting, children. Why don't you share the necklace? Or you can replace it with something else. Look, there is an oasis over there. Maybe you can find something nice there."

Tom and Lily looked at the oasis. It was a place with water and trees and flowers in the sand. It looked pretty. They decided to go there. They took their bucket and shovel.

They found many things in the oasis. They found shells and rocks and feathers and fruits. They were flexible. They traded some things with each other. They both got something they liked. They forgot about the necklace.

They thanked the man and went back to their sand. They played with their new things. They were happy. They did not fight anymore.

Sara and Ben like to play in the sand near the sea. They make castles and dig holes and look for shells. One day, they find a big shell that is shiny and pretty. Sara wants to keep it, but Ben wants it too.

"Give me the shell, Sara!" Ben says. "It is mine!"

"No, it is mine!" Sara says. "I saw it first!"

They pull and tug at the shell, but it does not break. They get angry and yell at each other. They do not see the octopus that is hiding under the water.

The octopus is hungry and curious. It sees the shiny shell and wants to touch it. It reaches out with one of its arms and grabs the shell from Sara and Ben. They are surprised and scared. They let go of the shell and run away.

The octopus is happy. It has a new toy to play with. It opens the shell and finds a pearl inside. The pearl is round and white and smooth. The octopus thinks it is beautiful. It puts the pearl in its mouth and feels how hard it is. It bites the pearl and hears a crunch.

"Ow!" the octopus says. "This pearl is sharp! It hurts my teeth!"

The octopus spits out the pearl and the shell. It does not want them anymore. It swims away to look for something else to eat.

Sara and Ben come back to the sand. They see the shell and the pearl on the ground. They are happy and amazed. They pick them up and look at them.

"Wow!" Sara says. "This is a pearl! It is so rich and rare!"

"Wow!" Ben says. "This is a sharp pearl! It can cut things!"

They decide to share the shell and the pearl. They make a necklace with them and put it around Sara's neck. They hug and say sorry to each other. They are friends again. They play in the sand and have fun. They do not see the octopus that is watching them from the water. The octopus is not hungry and curious anymore. It is sad and lonely. It wishes it had a friend to play with.

Tom and Sam are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a man with a stick in his mouth. The stick makes smoke. Tom and Sam are curious.

"Hello, man. What is that?" Tom asks.

"This is a cigarette. It helps me relax. Do you want to try?" the man says.

Tom and Sam shake their heads. They know cigarettes are bad. They make people sick and smell bad.

"No, thank you. Cigarettes are stupid. They hurt your lungs and teeth. We don't want to smoke," Sam says.

The man laughs. He thinks Tom and Sam are silly. He blows smoke in their faces. Tom and Sam cough and run away.

"Hey, come back. Don't be afraid. Smoking is cool. You are missing out," the man says.

Tom and Sam ignore him. They find a bench and sit down. They see a dog. The dog is friendly. He wags his tail and licks their hands. Tom and Sam pet the dog. They like the dog.

"Hello, dog. What is your name?" Tom asks.

The dog barks. He does not have a name. He is a stray. He is hungry and lonely.

"Can we be your friends?" Sam asks.

The dog nods. He is happy. He likes Tom and Sam. They share their snacks with him. They play fetch with him. They hug him.

"You are a good dog. We love you," Tom and Sam say.

The dog loves them too. He bites the man's cigarette and spits it out. The man is angry. He yells at the dog. He tries to kick the dog. Tom and Sam protect the dog. They bite the man's leg. The man screams and runs away.

"Good job, dog. You are brave. You saved us from the smoke," Tom and Sam say.

The dog barks. He is proud. He thanks Tom and Sam. They thank him too. They decide to adopt him. They name him Spot. They take him home. They give him a bath, a bed, and a collar. They are a family.

The moral of the story is: Smoking is bad for you and others. It is not cool or relaxing. It is stupid and harmful. Friends are good for you and others. They are not silly or afraid. They are kind and helpful. Friends are the best.

Ben and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to swing on the ropes and slide on the slides. They saw a big rope hanging from a tree. It looked like fun.

"Let's swing on the rope!" Ben said.

"OK!" Lily said.

They ran to the rope and took turns to swing. Ben swung high and low. Lily swung fast and slow. They laughed and shouted.

But then a boy came. He was bigger than Ben and Lily. He had a mean face and a loud voice. He wanted the rope.

"Get off the rope! It's mine!" he said.

"No, it's not! We were here first!" Ben said.

The boy got angry. He grabbed the rope and pulled it hard. Ben and Lily fell to the ground. They hurt their knees and elbows. They cried.

The boy laughed. He swung on the rope. He thought he was smart.

But he was not smart. He was crazy. He swung too high and too fast. He lost his grip and flew off the rope. He landed on a bush. The bush had thorns. The thorns pinched his skin. He screamed.

Ben and Lily stopped crying. They saw the boy in the bush. They felt sorry for him. They went to help him.

"Are you OK?" Lily asked.

"No, I'm not! The bush pinched me! It hurts!" the boy said.

"Maybe you should not be mean to other kids. Maybe you should share the rope." Ben said.

The boy nodded. He was sorry. He said sorry to Ben and Lily. They said it was OK. They helped him out of the bush. They gave him a band-aid.

They became friends. They swung on the rope together. They had fun. They learned to be nice. The end.

Tom and Jen are twins. They like to play in the snow. They wear warm coats, hats, gloves and boots. They make a snowman and a snow fort. They have fun.

But then they hear a loud noise. It is a big dog. The dog is crazy. It runs and barks and jumps. It knocks down the snowman and the snow fort. It makes a mess.

Tom and Jen are scared. They run to their house. They call their mom.

"Mom, mom, there is a crazy dog outside. It ruined our snowman and our snow fort. It is scary."

Mom comes to the door. She sees the dog. She is not scared. She knows the dog. It is Rex, the neighbor's dog. He is not crazy. He is playful. He likes the snow.

Mom says, "Don't worry, Tom and Jen. That is Rex. He is a friendly dog. He just wants to play with you. He likes your snowman and your snow fort. He thinks they are toys."

Tom and Jen look at Rex. He wags his tail. He licks his nose. He looks happy.

Tom and Jen are not scared anymore. They are curious. They go outside. They pet Rex. They play with him. They make a new snowman and a new snow fort. They share their gloves and hats and boots with Rex. They have more fun.

Lily and Ben were playing in the pool. They liked to dive and splash and swim. They had a task to find the hidden toys that mom threw in the water. Lily was good at diving. She could hold her breath for a long time and see the toys at the bottom. Ben was not so good at diving. He was scared of the deep water and the dark.

"Look, I found a duck!" Lily said, holding up the yellow toy. "Can you find the frog?"

Ben shook his head. He did not want to dive. He wanted to stay in the shallow water and play with the ball.

"Come on, Ben, it's fun!" Lily said. "Don't be a baby. I'll help you. Just follow me."

Lily grabbed Ben's hand and pulled him to the deep end. Ben tried to resist, but Lily was stronger. She dove with him, holding his hand. Ben felt the water go over his head. He felt scared. He wanted to breathe. He wanted to go back up. He tried to let go of Lily's hand, but she held on tight.

"Look, there's the frog!" Lily said, pointing to the green toy. "Grab it, Ben!"

Ben did not care about the frog. He cared about the air. He opened his mouth and screamed. Water filled his mouth and nose. He choked and coughed. He felt pain in his chest. He felt dizzy. He blacked out.

Lily did not notice. She was happy. She had found the frog. She let go of Ben's hand and swam up with the toy. She smiled and shouted.

"Mom, look, I found the frog! I did the task! Where's Ben?"

Mom looked at the pool. She saw Ben's body floating in the water. She screamed and jumped in. She grabbed Ben and pulled him out. She tried to make him breathe. She called for help. But it was too late. Ben was gone. Lily had killed him.

Tom and Lily were twins who loved to sing. They sang all the time, at home, at school, and in the park. They wanted to be opera singers when they grew up, because they heard that opera was brilliant and beautiful.

One day, their mom took them to see a real opera at a big theater. They were very excited and curious. They wore their best clothes and sat in their seats. The lights went down and the music started.

But when the opera singers came on stage, Tom and Lily were scared. They sang very loud and high, and made funny faces and gestures. They sounded like angry animals or ghosts. Tom and Lily did not like it at all. They wanted to go home.

"Mom, can we leave?" Tom whispered. "This opera is scary and ugly."

"Shh, be quiet," mom said. "This opera is brilliant and wonderful. You have to listen and learn. Maybe you will like it later."

But Tom and Lily did not like it later. They felt bored and frightened. They wished they could sing their own songs, or listen to something else.

At the end of the opera, the singers bowed and the audience clapped. Mom was happy and proud. She said to Tom and Lily, "Did you enjoy the opera? Wasn't it amazing?"

Tom and Lily shook their heads. They said, "No, mom, we did not enjoy the opera. It was not amazing. It was scary and ugly. We like our songs better. Can we go home now?"

Mom was surprised and sad. She said, "But Tom and Lily, you love to sing. You want to be opera singers. How can you not like opera?"

Tom and Lily said, "We love to sing, but we do not love opera. Opera is not for us. We want to sing our own way, and listen to different music. Can we try something else?"

Mom thought for a moment. She said, "Well, I guess you have your own tastes and preferences. I'm sorry you did not like the opera, but I'm glad you tried something new. Maybe you will find another kind of music that you love. There are many kinds of music in the world, and you can sing them all. But you have to be respectful and open-minded. You never know what you might learn or enjoy."

Tom and Lily nodded. They said, "We're sorry, mom. We did not mean to be rude or close-minded. We will try to be respectful and open-minded. But can we go home now?"

Mom smiled. She said, "Yes, we can go home now. But maybe next time, we can try something else. How about jazz, or rock, or folk? There are many kinds of music in the world, and you can sing them all."

Tom and Lily smiled. They said, "OK, mom. We will try something else. Maybe we will like it. But we will always love our songs, too. Can we sing them on the way home?"

Mom said, "Of course, you can. Let's sing together. There are many kinds of music in the world, and you can sing them all."

And they did.

Lila was a playful girl who liked to run and jump and sing. She had a fairy friend who lived in the garden. Her name was Zee and she had wings and a wand. Zee liked to play with Lila and make magic.

One day, Lila and Zee were playing hide and seek in the garden. Lila counted to ten and then looked for Zee. She checked behind the flowers, under the leaves, and in the birdhouse. But she could not find Zee. She called out, "Zee, where are you? I give up!"

Zee giggled and flew out of a rose. She landed on Lila's shoulder and said, "Here I am! You could not find me because I used my wand to make myself very small. Do you want to see?"

Lila nodded and Zee waved her wand. Lila felt a tickle and then she saw everything change. The grass became like a forest, the ants became like elephants, and the rose became like a castle. Lila gasped and said, "Wow, this is amazing! Can we explore?"

Zee smiled and said, "Of course! Come on, let's go!" She took Lila's hand and flew with her to the rose castle. They saw many wonders and had many adventures. They met a ladybug who was a queen, a spider who was a knight, and a worm who was a dragon. They had fun and laughed a lot.

After a while, Lila said, "Zee, this is very nice, but I miss my mom and dad. Can we go back to normal?"

Zee nodded and said, "Sure, we can. But first, let me show you one more thing." She flew with Lila to the top of the rose and pointed to the sky. Lila saw a rainbow and said, "Oh, how pretty!"

Zee said, "Yes, it is. And do you know what? There is a pot of gold at the end of the rainbow. And it belongs to the fairies. Do you want to see it?"

Lila looked at Zee and said, "Really? Is that true?"

Zee winked and said, "Maybe. Maybe not. What do you think?"

Lila thought for a moment and then she shrugged. She said, "I don't know. But I know I love you and I love playing with you. You are my best fairy friend."

Zee hugged Lila and said, "I love you too and I love playing with you. You are my best human friend."

Then they flew back to the ground and Zee waved her wand. Lila felt a tickle and then she saw everything change back to normal. She ran to her mom and dad and told them about her fairy friend and their magic game. They smiled and hugged her and said, "We are happy you have such a playful imagination. And we are happy you have such a good friend."

Ben and Mia liked to swim in the sea. They had masks and fins to see the fish and the reef. The reef was like a big garden under the water, with many colors and shapes. Ben and Mia liked to play with the fish and look for shells and starfish.

One day, they saw a big boat near the reef. The boat had a big net that it threw into the water. Ben and Mia were curious and swam closer to see what the boat was doing. They saw that the net was catching many fish and some of the reef. They felt sad and angry. They wanted to help the fish and the reef.

They saw a man on the boat who was speaking to another man. They could not hear what he was saying, but they saw that he was pointing at the net and smiling. He looked happy and greedy. Ben and Mia did not like him. They wanted to make him stop.

They had an idea. They swam to the net and started to pull and bite it. They made holes in the net and let some of the fish and the reef out. They hoped that the man would see and get scared. They hoped that he would leave the reef alone.

But the man did not see. He was too busy speaking and laughing. He did not care about the fish and the reef. He only cared about the money he would get. He did not know that there was something else in the water. Something big and fierce. Something that did not like boats and nets. Something that liked to eat fish and men.

It was a shark. A big, fierce shark. It smelled the fish and the blood in the water. It saw the boat and the net. It saw the man who was speaking and laughing. It felt hungry and angry. It wanted to make him stop.

It swam fast and hard. It jumped out of the water and bit the net. It tore the net and let all the fish and the reef out. It saw the man who was speaking and laughing. It bit him too. It made him stop.

Ben and Mia saw the shark. They were scared and amazed. They swam away from the boat and the net. They swam back to the shore. They were safe and happy. They thanked the shark for saving the fish and the reef. They hoped that the man would learn his lesson. They hoped that he would never come back.

Tom and Lily were twins who loved to play in the water. One day, their dad took them to the lake and gave them a big surprise. He had a kayak for them to ride in. A kayak is a long boat that you sit inside and move with a stick that has a paddle on each end.

"Wow, a kayak!" Tom and Lily shouted. They put on their life jackets and helmets and climbed into the kayak with their dad. He showed them how to hold the stick and paddle together. "Are you ready for some fun?" he asked.

"Yes, dad!" they said. They were very jolly and excited. They paddled around the lake, looking at the fish, the ducks, and the trees. They sang songs and made funny noises. They felt the sun on their faces and the breeze in their hair.

Suddenly, they saw a big splash in the water. It was a frog that had jumped out of a lily pad. Tom and Lily laughed and tried to catch the frog. But the frog was too fast and slippery. It jumped back into the water and swam away.

"Bye, frog!" Tom and Lily shouted. They waved their sticks and smiled. They had so much fun in the kayak. They thanked their dad for the surprise and hugged him. They were very happy and tired. They went back to the shore and had a picnic. They ate sandwiches, cookies, and juice. They told their mom about their adventure in the kayak. They said it was the best day ever.

Mom put the cookies on a tray and slid them into the oven. She set the timer and said, "Now we have to wait for them to bake. Do you want to read a book while we wait?"

Lily nodded and picked up her favorite book. It was about a princess who lived in a castle. Mom read the book to Lily and they looked at the pictures. Lily imagined she was the princess and wore a beautiful dress.

Ding! The timer went off and mom said, "The cookies are ready! Let's take them out and let them cool." She put on oven mitts and took out the tray. The cookies smelled yummy and looked golden. Lily clapped her hands and said, "They are so impressive, mom!"

Mom smiled and said, "Thank you, sweetie. You did a great job. Let's put them on the shelf to cool down. Then we can have some with milk."

Lily helped mom put the cookies on the shelf. She counted them and said, "We have twelve cookies. Can we share them with dad and grandma?"

"Of course, we can. They will love them too. You are such a kind and generous girl, Lily," mom said. She hugged Lily and said, "I love you, my little baker."

Lily and Ben were at the park with their mom. They saw a big fountain with water that went up and down. Lily wanted to play in the fountain, but Ben said no.

"Mom said we can't get wet, Lily. It's too cold today. You are stupid if you go in the fountain," Ben said.

Mom heard them and came to see what was wrong. She saw them wet and pinching and crying. She was not happy.

Lily and Ben were playing with blocks. They wanted to build a big tower. They had many blocks of different colors and shapes. They took turns to put one block on top of another.

"Look, Lily, I have a red block. It is a square. Where should I put it?" Ben asked.

"Put it here, Ben. It will make the tower stronger. I have a blue block. It is a circle. I will put it on top of your red block." Lily said.

They kept building the tower higher and higher. They were happy and proud of their work. They counted the blocks they used. They knew some numbers, like one, two, three, four, and five.

"Ben, how many blocks do we have?" Lily asked.

"I don't know, Lily. I can't count more than five. Let's ask Mom. She knows all the numbers." Ben said.

They ran to the kitchen, where Mom was making cookies. They asked her to come and see their tower. They wanted her to tell them how many blocks they used.

"Wow, Lily and Ben, you made a very big tower. It is very nice. You used a lot of blocks. Let me see. You used one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten, eleven, twelve, thirteen, fourteen, fifteen, sixteen, seventeen, eighteen, nineteen, twenty blocks. That is a big number." Mom said.

Lily and Ben were confused. They did not understand what Mom said. They did not know what twenty meant. They thought it was a funny word. They laughed and repeated it.

"Twenty, twenty, twenty. Ha ha ha." They said.

They ran back to their tower. They wanted to play some more. They wanted to make the tower even bigger. They looked for more blocks. They saw a box in the corner. It had a label that said "Supply". They did not know what that meant. They thought it was another funny word. They opened the box. It had more blocks inside. They were happy. They took some blocks and added them to their tower.

But the box did not have blocks for playing. It had blocks for building. They were heavy and hard. They were not meant for children. They were meant for Dad. He was a builder. He used them to make houses and walls. He left them in the corner by mistake. He forgot to put them away.

When Lily and Ben put the heavy blocks on their tower, the tower became unstable. It could not hold the weight. It started to wobble and shake. It fell down with a loud crash. It broke into pieces. It hurt Lily and Ben. They cried and screamed. They had cuts and bruises. They were scared and sad.

Mom heard the noise. She ran to the living room. She saw the mess and the children. She was shocked and angry. She called Dad. He came home quickly. He saw what happened. He was sorry and worried. He took Lily and Ben to the hospital. They had to get stitches and bandages. They had to stay in bed for a long time. They could not play with blocks anymore.

The moral of the story is: Do not play with things you do not know. They can be dangerous and hurt you. Always ask your parents before you use something new. They can tell you what it is and how to use it safely. They can supply you with the right toys and the right numbers. They can help you have fun and learn. They love you and want you to be happy and healthy.

Lisa and Ben are very happy. They get their tickets and go to the circus. They see many things. They see a clown who makes funny jokes. They see a lion who roars and jumps through a hoop. They see a girl who walks on a rope high in the air.

But then, something bad happens. Ben trips and falls. He hurts his knee. He cries and says: "Ow, ow, ow! It hurts!"

Lisa sees Ben and runs to him. She says: "Don't cry, Ben. I will help you. I have a band-aid in my pocket. I will put it on your knee. It will make you feel better. It will heal your boo-boo."

Lisa takes out her band-aid and puts it on Ben's knee. She gives him a hug and says: "There, there. You are brave, Ben. You are my friend. Do you want to see more of the circus?"

Ben smiles and says: "Yes, Lisa. Thank you. You are my friend too. You are very kind and independent. You can do many things. Let's go and see more of the circus."

Lisa and Ben hold hands and go to see more of the circus. They have a lot of fun. They are happy. They are friends.

Tom and Sam are friends. They like to play with trucks in the park. They have big trucks and small trucks. They make noises like vroom and beep.

One day, Tom has a new truck. It is red and shiny. It can carry many things. Tom is happy. He wants to show Sam his new truck.

"Look, Sam, look!" Tom says. "I have a new truck. It is red and shiny. It can carry many things. Do you want to play with it?"

Sam looks at Tom's new truck. He likes it. He wants to play with it. But he also has his own truck. It is blue and old. It can carry some things. Sam is sad. He thinks Tom will not like his truck.

"Your truck is nice, Tom," Sam says. "But I have my own truck. It is blue and old. It can carry some things. Do you want to play with it?"

Tom looks at Sam's truck. He does not care if it is blue and old. He cares if it is fun. He sees that Sam's truck can carry some things. He has an idea.

"Let's play together, Sam," Tom says. "We can bring our trucks to the sandbox. We can fill them with sand and dump them. We can make a castle or a hill. We can have fun with our trucks."

Sam smiles. He likes Tom's idea. He thinks Tom is a good friend. He agrees to play with Tom.

"OK, Tom, let's play together," Sam says. "We can bring our trucks to the sandbox. We can fill them with sand and dump them. We can make a castle or a hill. We can have fun with our trucks."

Tom and Sam run to the sandbox. They bring their trucks. They fill them with sand and dump them. They make a castle and a hill. They have fun with their trucks. They are happy.

Tommy loves to watch cartoons on TV. He likes the funny animals and the bright colors. He always laughs when they do silly things. Sometimes he pretends to be a cartoon animal too.

One day, Tommy found a big bag of candy in the kitchen. He was very happy. He wanted to eat all the candy and watch cartoons. He took the bag to the living room and turned on the TV. He saw his favorite cartoon. It was about a dog and a cat who were friends.

Tommy opened the bag and took out a candy. It was red and shiny. He put it in his mouth and started to chew. It was very sweet and sticky. He liked it a lot. He took out another candy and chewed it too. He did not notice that the candy was making his teeth dirty.

Soon, Tommy had eaten many candies. He felt sick. His tummy hurt. He did not want to watch cartoons anymore. He wanted to lie down. He turned off the TV and went to his bed. He closed his eyes and tried to sleep.

His mom came home and saw the empty bag of candy on the floor. She was angry. She went to Tommy's room and saw him in his bed. He looked pale and sad. She saw his teeth and they were black and brown. She was worried.

"Tommy, what did you do?" she asked.

"I ate candy and watched cartoons," Tommy said in a weak voice.

"That was not a good idea, Tommy. Candy is bad for your teeth and your tummy. You should not eat so much. You should eat healthy food and drink water. And you should not watch too much TV. You should play and read and learn. That is more interesting and fun," she said.

"I'm sorry, mom. I did not know. I thought candy and cartoons were good. But they made me feel bad. I don't want them anymore. I want to be healthy and happy," Tommy said.

"I'm glad you understand, Tommy. I love you and I want you to be well. Come on, let's go to the bathroom and brush your teeth. Then I will make you some soup and read you a story. How does that sound?" she said.

"That sounds good, mom. I love you too. Thank you for taking care of me," Tommy said.

They hugged and went to the bathroom. Tommy brushed his teeth and felt better. He ate some soup and listened to a story. He learned something new and he smiled. He decided to eat less candy and watch less cartoons. He decided to do more interesting and fun things. He was a good boy.

Tom and Sam were brothers who liked to play with their toy trucks. They had a big pile of sand in the backyard, and they pretended to be builders. They used their trucks to load and unload the sand, and made roads and hills and castles.

One day, it was very hot and sunny, and they got sweaty and dirty from playing. Their mom called them inside and said, "It's time for a shower, boys. You need to wash off the sand and cool down." But Tom and Sam did not want to stop playing. They said, "No, mom, we want to play more. We are not dirty, we are builders."

Their mom was not happy. She said, "You are not builders, you are boys. And boys need to listen to their mom and take a shower. If you don't, you will get itchy and smelly and have bad dreams. Now come on, or I will take away your trucks."

Tom and Sam did not like that. They did not want to lose their trucks. But they were also restless and wanted to play more. They thought of a plan. They said, "OK, mom, we will take a shower. But can we take our trucks with us? They are dirty too, and they need a shower."

Their mom thought for a moment. She said, "Well, I guess you can, but only if you promise to wash them well and not make a mess in the bathroom. And you have to be quick, because it's almost time for dinner."

Tom and Sam agreed. They ran to the bathroom with their trucks, and turned on the shower. They put their trucks under the water, and pretended to wash them. But they also splashed and sprayed and made a lot of noise. They had fun, but they also made the bathroom wet and sandy.

Their mom heard the noise and came to check on them. She was not happy. She said, "Boys, what are you doing? You are not taking a shower, you are making a mess. Look at the floor, and the walls, and the towels. They are all wet and sandy. And you are still dirty. You did not wash yourselves, you only played with your trucks."

Tom and Sam felt ashamed. They knew they did not listen to their mom, and they did not do what they said. They said, "Sorry, mom, we were having fun. We did not mean to make a mess. We will clean it up, and we will take a real shower."

Their mom said, "You better do that, boys. And next time, when I tell you to do something, you do it. Playing is good, but you also need to take care of yourself and your things. And you need to respect your mom and your home. Do you understand?"

Tom and Sam nodded. They said, "Yes, mom, we understand. We will do better next time. We love you, mom."

Their mom smiled. She said, "I love you too, boys. Now go and take a shower, and then come for dinner. And don't forget to dry your trucks."

The moral of the story is: Listen to your mom and do what she says. Playing is good, but you also need to take care of yourself and your things. And you need to respect your mom and your home.

"Yes, I do. But first, can I see your hair?" Lily said.

"Sure, come in." Anna said. She led Lily to her room.

Lily followed Anna and pretended to admire her hair. She waited until Anna turned her back. Then, she grabbed the scissors and cut off a big chunk of Anna's hair.

"Hey! What are you doing?" Anna screamed. She touched her head and saw her hair falling to the floor.

"I'm sorry, Anna. I just wanted to have your hair. It's so adorable. Now I can own it." Lily said. She held the hair in her hand and smiled.

Anna started to cry. She ran to her mom and told her what Lily did. Her mom was very angry. She called Lily's mom and told her to come and get her.

Lily's mom came and saw what Lily did. She was very disappointed. She scolded Lily and took her home. She threw away the hair and made Lily apologize to Anna.

But Anna did not want to be friends with Lily anymore. She was very sad and hurt. She did not like her hair anymore. She did not trust Lily anymore.

Lily lost her best friend. She was very sorry. She realized that she made a big mistake. She wished she could take it back. But it was too late.

Ben ran to her and hugged her. He felt sorry for her. He used his hands to say, "Are you OK, Jill? I told you to be careful."

"I am sorry, Ben," she said. "You are a good brother. You tried to help me. I should have listened to you. I love you."

"Can I go first?" Tom asked Sue.

"Okay, but be careful," Sue said.

Tom climbed up the ladder to the top of the slide. He saw a shiny handle on the side of the slide. He wondered what it was for. He grabbed the handle and pulled it.

Suddenly, the slide moved and made a loud noise. Tom was scared and let go of the handle. He slid down very fast and hit the ground hard. He cried and felt pain in his arm.

Sue saw what happened and ran to Tom. She hugged him and tried to make him feel better.

"Are you okay, Tom?" Sue asked.

"No, it hurts a lot," Tom said.

A jolly man in a uniform came to help them. He was a park ranger. He saw the handle and the slide.

"Who pulled this handle?" he asked.

"I did," Tom said.

The park ranger was not jolly anymore. He was angry.

"This handle is not for playing. It is for emergencies. It makes the slide fold up and lock. You could have been hurt very badly. You were very naughty and foolish," he said.

He took Tom and Sue to their mom and dad. He told them what Tom did. Mom and dad were not happy. They scolded Tom and took him to the doctor. The doctor said Tom had a broken arm. He put a cast on his arm and told him to rest.

Tom was very sorry and sad. He learned a lesson. He learned not to touch things he did not know. He learned to listen to his sister. He learned to be careful and safe. He hoped he would never pull a handle like that again.

Lily and Tom were friends. They liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big dog. The dog was brown and had a long tail. The dog looked mild and friendly.

"Can we pet the dog?" Lily asked Tom.

"I don't know," Tom said. "Maybe we should ask the owner first."

But the owner was not in the park. The dog was alone. Lily and Tom walked closer to the dog. The dog wagged its tail and licked its nose.

"Hello, dog," Lily said. "You are so cute. Can we help you? Are you lost?"

The dog barked and jumped on Lily. It bit her arm and made her cry. Tom was scared and ran away. He did not help Lily. He did not call for help. He left Lily alone with the dog.

Lily was hurt and sad. She wished Tom was still her friend. She wished the dog was not mild. She wished someone would help her. But no one came. No one heard her cry. No one helped her yet.

One day, Tom sees a big car in the street. It is red and shiny, and it has four doors and four wheels. Tom thinks it is a nice car. He wants to drive it too. He runs to the car and opens the door. He climbs inside and sits on the seat. He puts his hands on the wheel and his feet on the pedals.

Tom does not know how to drive a big car. He pushes the pedals and turns the wheel. The car makes a loud noise and moves. Tom is scared. He does not know how to stop the car. He sees a tree in front of him. He screams.

Mom hears Tom scream. She runs to the street and sees the car. She is very angry and very worried. She runs to the car and opens the door. She pulls Tom out of the car and hugs him. She checks his finger and his head. He is not hurt, but he is very sorry.

Mom tells Tom that he should never drive a big car. He should only drive his toy car. He should always ask before he touches something that is not his. He should always be careful and listen to Mom. Tom nods and says he is sorry. He says he loves Mom and he loves his toy car. Mom says she loves Tom and she is glad he is okay. She gives him a kiss and takes him home. She gives him his toy car and tells him to drive it nicely. Tom smiles and says he will. He drives his toy car nicely on the floor. He is happy.

"No, you can't!" Sara says. "This is my doll and she is very clean. You have dirty hands and you will make her dirty too."

"Can I see your car?" Sara asks Tom. She wants to touch the car's wheels and horn.

"No, you can't!" Tom says. "This is my car and he is very fast. You have slow hands and you will make him slow too."

Sara and Tom are not happy. They do not want to share their toys. They turn away from each other and play alone.

But then they hear a loud noise from the kitchen. It is their mom. She is making cookies for them. They smell the cookies and they feel hungry.

"Come here, Sara and Tom!" their mom calls. "I have a surprise for you!"

Sara and Tom run to the kitchen. They see a big plate of cookies on the table. They look yummy and sweet.

"Wow, cookies!" Sara and Tom say. "Can we have some, mom?"

"Yes, you can, but first you have to do something for me," their mom says. "You have to wash your hands and be nice to each other. Can you do that?"

Sara and Tom look at each other. They remember their toys and their words. They feel sorry and ashamed.

"Yes, mom, we can do that," they say. "We are sorry for being mean. We will share our toys and be friends."

They hug each other and say sorry. Then they wash their hands and sit at the table. Their mom gives them each a cookie and a glass of milk. They smile and thank their mom. They eat their cookies and drink their milk. They are happy and full.

The flower and the cloud looked around and smiled. They both agreed that the meadow was now very wonderful. The flower smiled and said, "I'm so happy we could disagree."

Later that day, Lily's mom made her a sandwich for lunch. As Lily took a bite, she noticed something hard in her mouth. She spit it out and saw that it was a small piece of the vine she had chewed on earlier. She realized that sometimes things that look fun to chew on aren't always good for you. 

From that day on, Lily only chewed on her favorite gum and never on any vines again.

When he picked the radishes, he noticed that they were a bit smelly. But he didn't mind because he loved the taste of radishes. From that day on, the farmer took good care of his garden and always had plenty of radishes to eat. The end.

Her mom came running and saw the broken vase. She was upset and said, "Lily, you need to be more gentle with things. This is not a success." Lily felt sad and wished she could turn back time to fix her mistake. But it was too late, and the bad ending was that Lily had to learn a lesson about being careful with things.

Lily's mom came out to see what was going on. She saw Lily wearing her clothes and how they were ruined. She was very angry and sad. She asked Lily why she took her clothes without asking. Lily said she just wanted to borrow them and play dress-up. She said she was sorry and did not mean to hurt them.

But Lily's mom did not forgive her. She said Lily was naughty and selfish. She said she had to pay for the clothes and do extra chores. She took Lily inside and made her take off the clothes. She did not let her play with her friends or watch TV. She sent her to her room and told her to think about what she did.

Lily felt very bad and lonely. She wished she had not borrowed her mom's clothes. She wished she had asked first or used her own clothes. She wished she could say sorry again and make her mom happy. She cried and cried until she fell asleep. She had a bad day.

Lily and Ben were friends who liked to play with blocks. They liked to build towers and houses and bridges with their blocks. One day, they decided to make a big map of the country with their blocks. They used different colors and shapes to show the mountains, the rivers, the cities and the farms.

They worked hard and had fun, but they also had some problems. Sometimes, they ran out of blocks or they disagreed on where to put them. Sometimes, they knocked over each other's blocks by accident or on purpose. They started to argue and shout and cry.

"Stop it, Ben! You ruined my city!" Lily said.

"No, you stop it, Lily! You took my blocks!" Ben said.

They were very angry and sad. They did not want to play together anymore. They sat on opposite sides of the room and glared at each other.

Then, their teacher came in and saw their map. She smiled and clapped her hands.

"Wow, Lily and Ben, what a wonderful map of the country you made! You are very clever and creative. I am so proud of you!" she said.

Lily and Ben looked at their teacher and then at their map. They saw how big and beautiful it was. They saw how they used all their blocks and how they made different parts of the country. They remembered how they helped each other and had fun.

They felt sorry for being mean and rude to each other. They got up and walked towards each other.

"I'm sorry, Lily. I should not have ruined your city. Can we be friends again?" Ben said.

"I'm sorry, Ben. I should not have taken your blocks. Can we be friends again?" Lily said.

They hugged and smiled. They were happy again. They finished their map and showed it to their teacher and their classmates. Everyone liked their map and praised them. They learned that playing together is better than fighting and that sharing and caring make them happy.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play with trains. They have a big track with many trains. They make the trains go fast and slow, and stop and go.

One day, a new boy comes to play. His name is Tom. He has a pretty train. It is red and shiny. Anna and Ben want to see his train. They ask him nicely.

"Can we play with your train, Tom?" they say.

But Tom is not nice. He says no. He says his train is better than their trains. He says they have old and ugly trains. He teases them.

"That is not nice, Tom," Anna says. "You should share your train. We share our trains with you."

But Tom does not listen. He keeps his train to himself. He makes it go around the track. He laughs at Anna and Ben.

Anna and Ben are sad. They do not like Tom. They do not want to play with him. They go to another corner. They play with their trains. They have fun.

Tom sees them. He wants to play with them. He feels lonely. He says sorry.

"Can I play with you, Anna and Ben?" he says. "I am sorry I teased you. Your trains are nice too. Can we share our trains?"

Anna and Ben think. They are still mad at Tom. But they are also kind. They decide to give him a chance.

"Okay, Tom," they say. "You can play with us. But you have to be nice. You have to share your train. And you have to say nice things."

Tom nods. He is happy. He gives his train to Anna. He takes a train from Ben. They play together. They make the trains go fast and slow, and stop and go. They have fun. They are friends.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. They have a dog named Spot. Spot is big and brown. He likes to run and bark.

One day, Lily and Ben see a pond in the park. The pond is deep and blue. They want to swim in the pond. But they do not have swimsuits. They have an idea. They take off their shoes and socks. They tie their socks together. They make a rope. They throw the rope in the pond. They want to pull the rope and splash the water.

But Spot sees the rope. He thinks it is a toy. He runs to the pond. He grabs the rope with his teeth. He pulls the rope hard. Lily and Ben fall in the pond. They get wet and cold. They cry for help.

A man hears them. He comes to the pond. He sees Lily and Ben and Spot. He helps them out of the pond. He gives them a towel. He says, "You should not play near the pond. The pond is deep and dangerous. You could drown. And you should not tie your socks together. You could lose them. And you should not leave your dog alone. He could get into trouble. You should be careful and responsible."

Lily and Ben are sorry. They say, "Thank you for helping us. We are sorry for being silly. We will not play near the pond again. We will not tie our socks together again. We will watch our dog better. We will be careful and responsible."

The man smiles. He says, "You are welcome. I am glad you are safe. You are good kids. You learned a lesson today. You should always respect the water and your things and your pet. They are important and precious."

Lily and Ben nod. They hug Spot. They put on their shoes and socks. They go home with the man. They tell their parents what happened. They say they learned a lesson. They say they will be careful and responsible. Their parents are proud of them. They hug them and kiss them. They say they love them. Lily and Ben are happy. They love their parents and their dog. They are good friends. They are good kids.

One day, they hear a loud noise outside the tent. They peek out and see a big dog. The dog is friendly and wags its tail. He wants to play with them.

"Hello, doggy!" Anna says. "Do you want to join our adventure?"

The dog barks and runs into the tent. He sniffs around and finds a toy ball. He picks it up and drops it at Ben's feet.

"Good doggy!" Ben says. "You can be our helper. We are looking for treasure in the jungle. Can you help us find it?"

The dog barks again and nods his head. He follows Ben and Anna as they crawl out of the tent. They look around the garden and pretend that they see lions, monkeys and snakes. They have a lot of fun.

After a while, they get tired and hungry. They go back to the tent and sit down. Anna has a basket with some sandwiches and juice. She shares them with Ben and the dog.

"Let me serve you, Ben," Anna says. "You are the leader of our adventure. You need to eat well."

"Thank you, Anna," Ben says. "You are very kind. And thank you, doggy, for being our helper. You are very brave."

The dog wags his tail and licks their faces. He is happy to have new friends. They eat and drink and then lie down in the tent. They close their eyes and dream of more adventures.

"Wow, look at all the toys and books!" Anna said. She pointed to a teddy bear and a puzzle on the back seat.

"Can we take them?" Ben asked. He reached for the door handle.

"No, we can't!" Anna said. "They are not ours. They belong to someone else. Maybe they are a mystery. Maybe they are a spy or a princess or a superhero."

Ben did not listen. He opened the door and grabbed the teddy bear. He ran away with it.

"Ben, come back!" Anna shouted. "That is bad. You are stealing. You have to give it back."

But Ben did not hear her. He was too happy with his new toy.

Suddenly, they heard a loud honk. They turned around and saw a man in a suit and a hat. He was angry. He was the owner of the car.

"Hey, you little thieves!" he yelled. "Give me back my stuff. That is my teddy bear. It is very special to me. It was a gift from my grandma."

He ran after Ben and Anna. Ben was scared. He dropped the teddy bear and ran faster. Anna followed him. They ran to the swings and hid behind them.

The man picked up the teddy bear and looked at it. He sighed. He was sad. He missed his grandma. He put the teddy bear back in the car and drove away.

Anna and Ben felt sorry. They learned a lesson. They should not take things that are not theirs. They should respect other people's things. They should be nice and honest. They hugged each other and said sorry. They decided to play with their own toys and books. They had fun and forgot about the fancy car and the mystery.

They try to go home. But they are lost. They do not know where they are. They are scared. They call for help. But no one hears them. They are alone in the dark. They wish they had listened to their friends.

Sam and Mia were twins who liked to play with their toys. They had many cars, trucks, trains and planes that they could zoom around the house. One day, their dad said he had a surprise for them in the garage. He took them by the hand and led them outside.

When they opened the garage door, they saw an enormous box with a big bow on it. It was bigger than their bed, bigger than their sofa, bigger than their fridge. Sam and Mia gasped and clapped their hands. "What is it, dad?" they asked.

"It's a gift for you two," dad said. "Do you want to open it and see?"

Sam and Mia nodded and ran to the box. They pulled the bow and tore the paper. Inside, they found a huge playset with roads, bridges, tunnels, buildings and signs. It was like a mini city for their toys. There were also many new cars, trucks, trains and planes that they had never seen before.

"Wow, dad, this is amazing!" Sam said. "Thank you so much!"

"This is the best gift ever!" Mia said. "Can we play with it now?"

"Of course you can," dad said. "But remember to share and be careful with your toys. And don't forget to clean up when you're done."

Sam and Mia hugged their dad and thanked him again. Then they started to fill the garage with their toys. Tom and Mia are playing in the garden. They have a big box and some sticks. They pretend the box is a rocket and the sticks are fire.

"Ready to blast off?" Tom asks Mia.

"Yes, yes, yes!" Mia says. She puts on a helmet made of a pot. Tom puts on a hat made of a bowl.

They sit in the box and count. "Three, two, one, go!" They shout. They make loud noises with their mouths. "Zoom, zoom, zoom!"

They imagine they are flying to the moon. They see stars and planets. They feel the wind and the heat.

But then, something goes wrong. The sticks catch fire. The box starts to burn. Smoke and ash come out.

"Help, help, help!" Tom and Mia scream. They jump out of the box. They run to the house.

Mum and Dad hear them. They come out and see the fire. They are angry and scared.

"What have you done?" Mum asks. "You could have hurt yourselves. You have to be careful with fire. It is dangerous."

"We are sorry, Mum. We are sorry, Dad." Tom and Mia say. They hug Mum and Dad. They are sad and sorry.

Mum and Dad put out the fire. They throw away the box and the sticks. They take Tom and Mia inside. They wash their faces and hands. They give them some water and cookies.

They talk to them about fire safety. They tell them to never play with fire. They tell them to always ask for permission. They tell them to use their imagination in a safe way.

Tom and Mia listen and nod. They understand. They say they will be more careful next time. They say they love Mum and Dad.

Mum and Dad smile and hug them. They say they love them too. They say they are proud of their imagination. They say they can still play rocket, but with something else.

They imagine they are flying to the moon. They see stars and planets. They feel the wind and the heat.

Lily wanted to try too. She threw a nut to another monkey. But the monkey did not catch it. It bounced off the cage and hit a lion on the head.

Ben and Lily were friends who liked to play in the farm. They liked to run in the grass, chase the chickens and watch the cows. Sometimes they helped their dads with the work, like picking corn or feeding the pigs.

One day, Ben and Lily decided to play a game. They wanted to see who could pick more corn from the field. They each took a big basket and ran to the corn plants. They started to pull the yellow ears and put them in their baskets.

"Look, Lily, I have more corn than you!" Ben said, showing his basket.

"No, you don't, Ben, I have more corn than you!" Lily said, showing her basket.

They kept picking corn and arguing, not paying attention to anything else. They did not see the sky getting dark and the wind getting strong. They did not hear the thunder and the rain. They did not notice the corn plants shaking and bending.

Suddenly, a loud noise made them stop and look up. They saw a big, black cloud spinning in the air. It was coming towards them, fast and angry. It was a tornado!

"Ben, Lily, run!" their dads shouted from the barn. "The tornado is coming! It will increase and destroy everything!"

Ben and Lily dropped their baskets and tried to run, but it was too late. The tornado was too close and too strong. It picked them up and threw them in the air, along with the corn, the baskets, the chickens and the cows. They screamed and cried, but no one could hear them or help them.

The tornado carried them far away, to a place where the sky was clear, but the land was empty and cold. There was no farm, no grass, no animals, no dads. There was only corn, scattered and broken. Ben and Lily were alone and scared. They wished they had not played that game. They wished they had listened to their dads. They wished they had been good friends. But it was too late. The end.

"What is that?" Sara asked, feeling worry.

"I don't know, let's go closer," Ben said, feeling brave.

They walked towards the roar and saw a big, furry, brown animal with horns and a long tail. It was a bull. The bull saw them and snorted.

"Hello, bull," Ben said, trying to be friendly. "We are Sara and Ben. We live on this farm. You are harmless, right?"

The bull did not answer. He lowered his head and charged at them. Sara and Ben screamed and ran back to the door. They slammed it shut and leaned against it.

"Mom! Dad! Help!" they shouted.

Mom and dad heard them and came running. They opened the door and saw the bull. They were angry and scared.

"What are you doing here?" mom asked. "We told you not to come near the barn. The bull is dangerous. He could have hurt you."

"We are sorry, mom," Sara said. "We were bored and curious. We thought the bull was harmless."

"You were wrong," dad said. "The bull is not a toy. He is a wild animal. He does not like strangers. You have to stay away from him."

Sara and Ben nodded. They felt sorry and scared. They hugged mom and dad and said they would never go near the barn again. Mom and dad forgave them and took them back to the house. They gave them some cookies and milk and told them a story about a friendly cow. Sara and Ben learned their lesson and never bothered the bull again.

Her mom laughed and said, "Sure, you can count the towels. But only up to ten. That's enough for today."

Tom was a boy who liked to play in the garden. He liked to dig and run and look for bugs. One day, he saw a lizard on a rock. The lizard was green and had a long tail. Tom wanted to catch the lizard and keep it as a pet.

He ran to the lizard and tried to grab it. But the lizard was fast and scared. It ran away from Tom and hid under a leaf. Tom was angry and frown. He did not like that the lizard ran away. He wanted to have it for himself.

He looked for the lizard and found it under the leaf. He reached his hand to take it. But the lizard was fierce and brave. It opened its mouth and bit Tom's finger. Tom cried out and let go of the lizard. He felt pain and fear. He ran to his mom and showed her his finger.

His mom was kind and gentle. She cleaned his finger and put a bandage on it. She hugged him and said, "Tom, you should not try to catch a lizard. Lizards are wild animals. They do not like to be touched or kept. They need to be free and happy in their own home. You should respect them and leave them alone. Do you understand?"

Tom nodded and said, "Yes, mom. I understand. I am sorry for the lizard. I will not bother it again. I will only watch it from far away. And I will be careful of its teeth." He smiled and said, "Thank you, mom. You are the best."

His mom smiled and said, "You are welcome, Tom. You are a good boy. I love you." She kissed him and said, "Now, let's go and have some cookies and milk. And maybe we can read a book about lizards and learn more about them. How does that sound?"

Tom said, "That sounds great, mom. I love you too." He held her hand and walked with her to the house. He learned a lesson that day. He learned to be kind and respectful to animals. And he learned that lizards are not good pets, but they are amazing creatures.

"Wow, look at this mushroom!" Tim said. "It is so big and pretty. I want to ride on it."

"No, I want to ride on it!" Mia said. "It is my mushroom. I saw it first."

They both ran to the mushroom and tried to climb on it. They pushed and pulled and shouted. They were very selfish. They did not want to share.

The mushroom did not like that. It felt their feet and hands and voices. It was angry and sad. It wanted to be left alone.

Suddenly, the mushroom shook and bounced. Tim and Mia fell off the mushroom. They landed on the ground. They were scared and hurt.

They looked at the mushroom. It had a face. It had eyes and a mouth and a nose. It glared at them.

"Go away!" the mushroom said. "You are bad children. You are not nice to me or to each other. You do not deserve to ride on me."

Tim and Mia felt sorry. They realized they were wrong. They got up and dusted themselves off.

"We are sorry, mushroom," Tim said. "We were selfish. We should have asked you first. And we should have taken turns."

"Yes, we are sorry, mushroom," Mia said. "We did not mean to hurt you. You are a living thing. You have feelings. We should have respected you."

The mushroom softened. It saw that they were sincere. It smiled a little.

"Thank you for saying sorry," the mushroom said. "That is very kind of you. Maybe you can ride on me another day. But only if you are gentle and careful and fair."

Tim and Mia nodded. They thanked the mushroom and said goodbye. They walked away, holding hands. They learned a lesson. They decided to be more friendly and generous. They hoped to see the mushroom again.

"Yes, please, Ben," Lily said in a high voice. "Thank you for inviting me. You have a lovely home."

"Ben! Lily! What are you doing?" she yelled. "That is not juice, that is wine! Wine is for grown-ups only! You are not allowed to drink wine! You could get sick!"

"That was very naughty and dangerous," she said. "You should never touch wine or any other drink that is not for you. You should always ask me or Dad before you take anything from the kitchen. Do you understand?"

Ben and Lily went to their room. They lay down on their beds and closed their eyes. They felt sleepy and dizzy. They learned their lesson. They did not want to drink wine ever again. They only wanted juice and water.

Bob saw lots of other animals too, like monkeys and lions. He kicked a ball at them too, and said "Nice kick!" to himself. He was having so much fun!

Before he had to go home, Bob saw a really big elephant. He ran up to it and kicked a ball right in the middle. He laughed and said, "Nice kick!" again. Bob had such a great time at the zoo that day, and he knew he would remember it forever.

Molly was a happy three year old girl. She loved music, dancing and playing with her toys. One day, Molly saw a guitar in the store. She wanted to buy it! 

Molly asked her mum if she could buy it. 'Yes', said her mum. Molly was so excited! 

Molly loved to strum the guitar and make music. Soon, she was able to play a few notes. But she had no idea how to make her guitar sound better. 

That night, Molly heard a noise coming from the next room. She opened the door and saw a man playing the guitar. He was amazing! His fingers flew on the strings and the notes were so beautiful. 

Molly said loudly, 'Can you teach me?' The man was deaf, so he couldn't hear her. Molly was so disappointed. 

But that didn't stop Molly from learning the guitar. She kept practising and soon she could play many numbers. In time, she even became a great guitar player!

At the beach, Joe found a big boat. He was so nosy that he wanted to go for a sail. He climbed into the boat, and found an old oat. It looked like the perfect snack, so Joe ate the oat.

He said, "Little girl, why don't you come outside and play with me? We can play until you feel sleepy." 

The little girl smiled and went outside. She played with the nosy little bird until she was too tired to keep playing. Then she said goodnight to the nosy little bird and hopped back into bed.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She liked to play outside in the dirt. One day, she was digging in the ground with her hands when she found a dirty palm.

Her mommy was surprised. "Wow, that's amazing, Lily," she said. "Where did you find it?"

"I found it in the dirt," Lily replied.

Her mommy smiled. "You have such a good eye for finding things, Lily," she said. "Let's wash the palm off and see what it looks like."

Lily and her mommy washed the palm and were surprised to find that it was actually a beautiful seashell. They put the seashell on display in their home and Lily was very proud of her discovery.

"I was scared," said Lily.

Ben and Mia loved to watch the dolphins at the beach. They liked to see them jump and splash in the water. Sometimes the dolphins made funny noises that sounded like they were talking.

One day, Ben and Mia saw a huge dolphin near the shore. It was bigger than any dolphin they had ever seen. It had a long, pointy nose and a big, curved fin. It looked sad and lonely.

"Hello, dolphin!" Ben shouted. "Do you want to play with us?"

The huge dolphin looked at Ben and Mia. It made a low, sad noise.

"I think he is lost," Mia said. "Maybe he can't find his family."

Ben and Mia felt sorry for the huge dolphin. They wanted to help him.

"Maybe we can unite him with his family," Ben said. "Maybe they are looking for him too."

"How can we do that?" Mia asked.

Ben thought for a moment. He had an idea.

"Maybe we can make a big noise, like the dolphins do. Maybe his family will hear us and come to find him."

Ben and Mia nodded. They took a deep breath and started to make loud, high-pitched noises. They sounded like dolphins.

The huge dolphin heard them. He looked surprised and curious. He made a loud, high-pitched noise back.

Ben and Mia smiled. They kept making noises with the huge dolphin.

Soon, they saw more dolphins coming from the water. They were different sizes and colors, but they all looked happy. They made noises too.

The huge dolphin saw them. He recognized them. They were his family. He swam towards them. They swam towards him. They united.

Ben and Mia watched as the dolphins hugged and kissed each other. They were happy for the huge dolphin. He was not sad and lonely anymore.

"Bye, dolphin!" Ben and Mia shouted. "We are glad you found your family!"

The huge dolphin and his family waved their fins at Ben and Mia. They thanked them for their help. They jumped and splashed in the water. They were happy.

Sara was a big girl who liked to do things by herself. She was independent and did not need help from her mom or dad. One morning, she wanted to make breakfast for her family. She saw some eggs in the fridge and decided to cook them.

She took a pan and put it on the stove. She turned on the fire and cracked an egg on the edge of the pan. But the egg was too hard and it broke into pieces. Some of the egg fell on the floor and some of the egg fell on the stove. Sara was sad and scared. She did not know what to do.

She heard her mom coming into the kitchen. She saw the mess and smelled the smoke. She quickly turned off the fire and took the pan away. She hugged Sara and said, "Are you okay, honey? What happened?"

Sara started to cry and said, "I'm sorry, mom. I wanted to make breakfast for you and dad. I wanted to cook eggs, but they broke and made a mess. I'm a bad girl."

Mom kissed Sara and said, "No, you're not a bad girl. You're a sweet and independent girl. But cooking eggs is not easy. You need to be careful and ask for help. Next time, we can cook eggs together, okay?"

"Let's go closer to the star," Anna said. "Maybe it has a wonder for us."

"OK," Ben said. "But how do we get there?"

They found a big hill near their house. They climbed up the hill. It was hard and tiring, but they did not give up. They reached the top of the hill. They looked at the star. It was very impressive.

"Wow," Anna said. "It is so beautiful. I wish we could touch it."

"Me too," Ben said. "Maybe we can fly to it. Let's jump and flap our arms."

They jumped and flapped their arms. But they did not fly. They fell down the hill. They rolled and bumped and hurt themselves. They cried and screamed. Their parents heard them and ran to help them. They took them to the doctor. The doctor gave them bandages and medicine.

"You were very foolish," the doctor said. "You cannot fly to the star. It is very far and hot. You could have burned or died. You should be happy with what you have and not chase after things you cannot reach."

Anna and Ben felt sorry and ashamed. They learned their lesson. They never tried to fly to the star again. "Yes!" Tom and Lily said. They were curious and excited. They had never seen a jeep like that before.

"Yes, please!" Tom and Lily said. They nodded and smiled.

They went back to their yard and played with their toy jeep and their flags. They pretended they were soldiers too. They had a new friend and a new adventure. They never forgot the man and his jeep.

Once upon a time, there was a big worm who lived in a garden. He loved to wriggle and squirm in the dirt all day long. One day, he saw a big apple on a tree and wanted to eat it. But the apple was too high up and he couldn't reach it.

The worm thought and thought about how he could get the apple. Suddenly, he saw a big leaf on the ground. He thought he could use it to climb the tree. So, he crawled onto the leaf and started to climb. But as he climbed, the leaf slipped and he fell down to the ground.

The worm was sad and frustrated. But then he had an idea. He crawled over to a group of ants and asked for their help. The ants were happy to help and together they climbed up the tree and got the apple. The worm was so happy and grateful that he shared the apple with all the ants. From that day on, they were all friends and helped each other whenever they needed it.

When they got home, Lily showed her mommy the mysterious button. Her mommy didn't know what it was for either, but she thought it was pretty. They put the button on the fridge so they could look at it every day. 

From then on, every time Lily and Max went jogging in the park, they looked for more mysterious buttons. They never found any more, but they had fun looking!

Tom and Anna are friends. They like to play in the park. They see a big fish tank with many fish. The fish tank has a sign that says "Oxygen". Tom and Anna do not know what oxygen is.

"Look at the fish, Anna. They are so pretty. Do you think they can talk?" Tom asks.

"I don't know, Tom. Maybe they can talk to each other. But we cannot hear them. They are in the water." Anna says.

"Maybe they need oxygen to talk. Like we need air to talk." Tom says.

"Maybe. But what is oxygen?" Anna asks.

Tom and Anna see a man who works at the park. He is wearing a blue shirt and a hat. He is feeding the fish.

"Excuse me, sir. What is oxygen?" Tom asks.

The man smiles and kneels down to talk to Tom and Anna.

"Oxygen is a very important thing, kids. It is in the air we breathe. It helps us live and talk. The fish also need oxygen, but they get it from the water. The water has oxygen too, but not as much as the air. That's why the fish tank has a machine that makes bubbles. The bubbles give more oxygen to the water and the fish." The man explains.

"Wow, that is very interesting. Thank you, sir." Tom says.

"Yes, thank you. You are very smart." Anna says.

The man laughs and says, "You are very welcome, kids. You are very curious and polite. I'm glad you like the fish. They are very beautiful and special. But remember, they are also very poor. They cannot leave the fish tank. They cannot see the sky or the trees or the flowers. They cannot play with other animals. They only have each other. So we have to be kind and respectful to them. We have to take care of them and their oxygen. Okay?"

"Okay, sir. We understand. We will be kind and respectful to the fish. We will not touch them or make noise or throw things at them. We will just watch them and learn from them." Tom and Anna say.

"Good. That's very nice of you. I'm sure the fish appreciate it. Now, have fun and enjoy the park. But don't forget to breathe. Oxygen is good for you too." The man says.

Tom and Anna wave goodbye to the man and the fish. They go to play on the swings and the slide. They breathe the fresh air and feel happy. They have learned something new today. They have learned about oxygen.

The doctor said, "Lily, I need to see inside your arm. I have a special machine that can do that. It is called an x-ray. It will not hurt you, I promise. But you need to be very still and let me take a picture of your arm. Can you do that?"

Lily nodded. She was scared, but she wanted her arm to feel better. Mom held her hand and said, "You are very brave, Lily. I am proud of you."

The doctor put Lily's arm on a table and covered it with a soft cloth. Then he moved a big machine over her arm. It made a funny noise. Lily closed her eyes and did not move.

The doctor said, "All done, Lily. You did great. Let me show you the picture of your arm." He took a paper from the machine and showed it to Lily and Mom. It had a black and white image of Lily's arm, with bones and shapes.

The doctor said, "See, Lily, this is your arm. And this is where it is broken. You need a cast to help it heal. A cast is a hard bandage that will keep your arm in place. You can choose the color you like. And you can have your friends sign it and draw on it. How does that sound?"

Lily smiled. She liked the idea of a cast. She said, "Can I have a pink cast, please?"

The doctor said, "Of course, Lily. Pink is a lovely color. Let me get it for you." He went to get the cast and came back with a roll of pink material. He wrapped it around Lily's arm and made it smooth and hard.

Lily looked at her arm and said, "Wow, it looks cool. Thank you, doctor."

The doctor said, "You are very welcome, Lily. You are a strong and brave girl. Now you need to rest and take care of your arm. And you can show it to your friends and family. They will love it."

Lily hugged Mom and said, "Thank you, Mom. I love you."

Mom said, "I love you too, Lily. You are my sweet girl." They left the doctor's office and went home. Lily felt better and was happy with her pink cast.

Mommy smiled and said, "I know, Lily, I know. But you can take your teddy bear, your ball and your blanket with you. You can have them in your big bed. And you can have more toys and books in your big bed. You will like your big bed. It's very cozy and soft."

Lily was not sure. She looked at her crib and then at her big bed. She saw that her big bed had a pink pillow, a purple quilt and a white lamp. She saw that there were more toys and books on a shelf near her big bed. She wondered if she would like her big bed.

Mommy picked her up and said, "Come on, Lily, let's try your big bed. You can always go back to your crib if you don't like it. But I think you will like it. You are a brave and smart girl." Mommy carried her to her big bed and put her down. She gave her her teddy bear, her ball and her blanket. She kissed her and said, "Good night, Lily. I love you."

Lily hugged her teddy bear, rolled her ball and covered herself with her blanket. She felt cozy and soft. She looked at her pink pillow, her purple quilt and her white lamp. She looked at her toys and books on the shelf. She smiled and said, "I like my big bed, mommy. I love you too." She closed her eyes and fell asleep.

They ran to the big oak tree and started to climb. They were careful not to fall or hurt themselves. They reached the top and looked at the mist. It was very close and very quiet.
